# What is left in the gameplay corpus, and what it costs

The implementation specification for the gap `docs/PARITY-GAP.md` opened and
`parity-cheapest-five` (`569323e`) closed thirteen of. Every missing behaviour
below is named as a class, a method and a bytecode offset range read with
`javap -p -c -constants` out of
`oracle-work/vanilla-26.2/versions/26.2/server-26.2.jar`; every count comes
from a recording that already existed.

**No corpus run and no oracle run was taken for this document.** Two trace
pairs already on disk carry all of it:

| pair | what it is | recorded | tree |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P1** | 88 scenarios, full corpus | 2026-08-07 02:02 / 02:19 | `chatcmd` `a938d64` — the pair `PARITY-GAP.md` §2.1 used |
| **P2** | 23 scenarios, the cheapest-five subset, **control arm** | 2026-08-07 07:10 | `e894224` (the run *before* `569323e`) |

P2 is the control, not the treatment: the treatment run finished at 06:54 and
its traces were overwritten by the control at 07:10. Both console logs survive
(`~/grit-logs-cheapfive-before.log`, `~/grit-logs-cheapfive-subset2.log` on the
box) and carry the verdicts, so treatment *verdicts* are known and treatment
*packets* are not. Where that matters it is said, and the run that would settle
it is named.

The method was pinned before it was trusted: the per-kind deltas recomputed
here from P1 reproduce `PARITY-GAP.md` §2.2's published delta column, including
`090 rotate_head 7->0`, `040 recipe_book_add 1->0` and `530 update_attributes /
set_entity_data / set_equipment 1->0`. A second reading that agreed with the
first everywhere it overlapped is the only kind worth quoting.

## 0. The four carried-forward verdicts, and a fifth

> **ALL FIVE RE-CHECKED AND ALL FIVE STILL HOLD — 2026-08-17, §52.** `237`,
> `560`, `090`, `060` and `520` are every one of them `match` on **both**
> denominators in all four full-corpus recordings of 2026-08-17, and in all
> fourteen full-corpus reports back to 2026-08-12 23:22, with **no flap in any
> of them**. So §0.5's "`520` is now a coin flip" is not what the recordings
> show over this window: 520 is `match`/`match` fourteen times running. That
> is a statement about a five-day window and not a refutation of the coin-flip
> mechanism — 520's reference projection is **one observation**, so its green
> is thin by construction and it remains the row here most likely to move.
> This block exists because a section of carried-forward verdicts is exactly
> the kind that nobody re-reads, and a silently regressed row is worse than a
> stale one.


### 0.1 `237-digging-a-tall-flower-takes-both-halves` — **instrument, not defect**

Its `level_event` is right, and that is now checked rather than assumed. In P2,
vanilla's actor stream carries `level_event 2001 at [1,1,0] data 12915` — the
**upper** half, at the position the cascade destroyed, not the position the
player dug ([1,0,0]). That is `Block.updateOrDestroy`'s air branch, the one
site of the four that passes `aconst_null`, which is exactly where `569323e`
put the emission. The same shape holds for its four siblings, and it is worth
recording because it is counter-intuitive for two of them:

| scenario | dug | vanilla's actor-visible `2001` | emitter |
|---|---|---|---|
| 132 | `[1,1,0]` top of a door | `[1,1,0]` | cascade off the hand-cleared bottom |
| 236 | `[1,0,0]` bed foot | `[1,0,0]` | cascade off the hand-cleared **head** |
| 237 | `[1,0,0]` flower bottom | `[1,1,0]` | cascade off the removed bottom |
| 238 | `[1,1,0]` flower top | `[1,1,0]` | cascade off the hand-cleared bottom |
| 260 | `[1,0,0]` door bottom | `[1,1,0]` | cascade off the removed bottom |

In 132 and 238 the player dug the top and the event the player *sees* is at the
top — but it is not the dig's own particle, which
`Block.spawnDestroyParticles` sends through the player-excluding overload. It
is the cascade: the hand clear of the *other* half with flags 35 (bit 16,
`UPDATE_KNOWN_SHAPE`, is clear, so shape updates propagate) makes the dug half
shapeless, and `updateOrDestroy` destroys it with a null entity. Same visible
packet, different block doing the destroying — the 236 trap, twice more.

What is left in 237 is one `entity_position`, and §0.4 says what that is.
**237 is not work. It is the same instrument residual as 060.**

### 0.2 `560-storing-an-item-in-a-chest` — **harness artefact, and it cannot convert**

Not "may convert under a full corpus". It cannot convert reliably at any
window, and the mechanism is exact.

`ContainerOpenersCounter.recheckOpeners` calls `openerCountChanged`
**unconditionally** — offset 84's `if_icmpeq 167` lands on offset 167, the call
itself, so the no-change path and the change path meet there — and offsets
178-186 re-arm `scheduleRecheck` whenever the count is positive, which is
`Level.scheduleTick(pos, block, 5)` (`scheduleRecheck` offset 6, `iconst_5`).
`ChestBlockEntity.signalOpenCount` offsets 0-13 is
`level.blockEvent(pos, block, 1, newCount)`. **An open chest emits an identical
`block_event` every 250 ms for as long as it is open, forever.**

`090`'s own file already says this and buys it off with
`collapse_repeats = ["block_event"]`. That does not reach `strict`, and the
reason is not that `strict` ignores the list — it is that `collapse_runs`
collapses *identical consecutive* observations **of the projection**, and the
declared projection has already deleted every other kind, so the repeats are
adjacent. The strict projection keeps `block_changed_ack`,
`container_set_slot` and `packet:0x60` between them, **no two repeats are ever
adjacent, and nothing collapses.** That is the whole mechanism, and it makes
every container scenario's strict verdict a function of where a free-running
250 ms timer's edges fall against the step boundaries.

Measured in P2, over the seven scenarios that leave a chest open:

| scenario | vanilla `block_event` by step | ours | agree |
|---|---|---|---|
| 090 | `0:6` | `0:6` | yes |
| 490 | `0:9` | `0:10` | no |
| 560 | `0:1 1:2 2:5` | `0:2 1:1 2:5` | no |
| 561 | `0:1 1:2 2:5` | `0:2 1:2 2:5` | no |
| 601 | `0:1 1:6` | `0:3 1:5` | no |
| 602 | `0:1 1:2 2:5` | `0:2 1:2 2:5` | no |
| 603 | `0:2 1:1 2:1 3:5` | `0:2 1:1 2:2 3:5` | no |

**Six of seven, in one run.** 560's totals are 8 against 8: not one packet
missing, one packet on the wrong side of a boundary. Vanilla's edges land at
61 · 260 · 478 · 728 · 978 · 1228 · 1494 · 1744 ms, ours at 20 · 220 · 470 ·
720 · 970 · 1220 · 1470 · 1720; the step-1 action fires at ~283 ms, and
vanilla's 260 is stamped step 1 while our 220 is stamped step 0.

That 560 and not 561 was the one left over in the treatment run is settled by
elimination, without the treatment traces: **490 and 561 both read strict
`match` in the treatment run**, and all three emit the same
`block.chest.open`, so our sound's content is right and 560's residual is not
the sound. 561 differs from 560 by one slot number. The difference between them
is which side of a boundary a 250 ms edge landed on.

**560 is a harness artefact.** §2 item R1 is the fix and it is one function.

### 0.3 `090-chest-opens-a-screen` — **not measuring what it claims, and worse than run-dependent**

The brief's suspicion is right and the cause is not head-rotation jitter.

Vanilla emits `rotate_head` (`packet:0x53`, id 83) in exactly **two of the 88
scenarios in P1**: `080-spawn-egg-makes-a-mob` (16, both streams) and
`090-chest-opens-a-screen` (8). Of 090's seven on the actor's stream, **six
arrive at `at_ms == 0`** — before the step ran. They are the tail of the
previous scenario. `080-spawn-egg-makes-a-mob` immediately precedes 090 in
recording order, spawns entity 5 (`kind_id` 100) at 76 ms, **emits no
`remove_entities`**, and rotates that mob's head out to 2747 ms. The mob is
still alive and still turning when 090's window opens.

That is not inference. `ClientboundRotateHeadPacket` is
`(varint entityId, byte yHeadRot)` and the undecoded digest covers both, so an
equal digest is an equal entity id. **090's `at_ms == 0` packet
`3aaeca07b4dd0020` is byte-identical to 080's at 2147 ms on the actor and
2179 ms on the observer** — one packet, observed twice, once inside each
scenario's window. All six of 090's zero-millisecond digests share 080's
`3aa…`/`3ab…` id prefix; `180-stairs-make-a-corner-when-two-meet`'s two are
`3b9…`, a different entity, and 180 is strict `match` with them present on both
sides.

Two things then have to fail at once for those packets to land in 090's
projection, and both do:

1. **The `within` bound cannot see them.** 080's anchor is `[-288,-60,0]` and
   090's is `[-320,-60,0]` — 32 blocks apart, against a default `within` of 16
   — and the mob *is* in the placement table, seeded by 080's `add_entity`
   (`compare.rs` line 332, and `starts` accumulates across scenarios at lines
   736-740). But `rotate_head` has no decoder arm, so it travels as
   `packet:0x53` plus a digest with **neither an `entity` field nor an `at`
   field**; `place` returns `None` and `near` returns `true` on the "nobody
   ever told me where this is" branch (`compare.rs:554-556). **An undecoded
   packet is exempt from the spatial bound by construction.**
2. Our server implements no spawn egg, so there is no mob and no head to turn,
   and the count is 7 against 0.

So 090 converted in the treatment run for two reasons that are both about
other scenarios: vanilla happened to emit no `rotate_head` in that run's 090
window, and the lid count happened to agree at 6/6. **Neither is a statement
about chests.** The verdict as written is a coin flip over two independent
phases, and it will start failing again the day spawn eggs land — on both
sides, with different head cadences.

`090` is **untestable as written under `strict`.** §5 lists it. §2 item R2 is
the fix and it is a decoder arm, not a server change.

### 0.4 `060-coral-dries-out-unprompted` — **instrument residual, in both directions**

Not "the subset's leftover ordering". In P2 the *only* difference in 060's
whole strict projection is one `entity_position` on vanilla's actor stream at
5310 ms, for the bystander at `[0,0,5]`. Its four `block_update`, its
`block_changed_ack` and the scheduled dry-out at 3926 ms against our 3628 ms
all agree.

Census of the same packet over all 23 scenarios of P2, actor stream:

| | vanilla | ours |
|---|---|---|
| stray `entity_position` | 3 — 060 @ 5310, 290 @ 598, 360 @ 1296 | 2 — 237 @ 1289, 520 @ 1175 |

Same packet, both directions, never coinciding, roughly one window in eight —
and 290 and 360 both read strict `match` in the treatment run, so it moved.
`PARITY-GAP.md` §0.2 called this the flake tail and named the packet; the
mechanism is now readable.

`ServerEntity.sendChanges` offsets 648-694 emit
`ClientboundEntityPositionSyncPacket` when any of five things holds, and the
fifth is the one that fires here: `wasOnGround != entity.onGround()` (offsets
680-691). `tracker.rs:236-242` already ports that test verbatim, so this is not
a missing rule. What is missing is a *shared input*: the reference and the
subject are recorded in **two separate client sessions** — `ci/t2-gameplay.sh`
records all 23 against vanilla and then all 23 against us — so the harness's
own `on_ground` bit and its timing against the server tick are two independent
draws. No server change can align them.

**060 is not a defect and not a regression.** It is the same residual as 237,
190 and 200, and §2 item R3 is the fix.

### 0.5 The fifth, which the last round could not have seen: `520` is no longer `vacuous`, and it is now a coin flip

`569323e` made `compare::project`'s heartbeat exception read the scenario's
`observe` list on both denominators, which was right, and it converted 520 from
permanently-`vacuous` to `match`. It converted it to a **fair coin**, and the
measurement that would have shown it was in the other pair:

| pair | vanilla actor heartbeats | ours |
|---|---|---|
| P2 (subset control, `e894224`) | 1766 · 4792 ms → **2** | 784 · 3759 ms → **2** |
| P1 (full corpus, `a938d64`) | 0 · 2863 · 5888 ms → **3** | 1753 · 2703 · 4753 · 5719 ms → **4** |

`ServerEntity.FORCED_POS_UPDATE_PERIOD` is 60 (field at the head of the class;
the test is `tickCount % 60` at `sendChanges` offsets 531-538), so the cadence
is 3.0 s and 520's window is 6.0 s. **1.98 periods.** Two independently-phased
servers land on the same integer count only by luck, and P1's vanilla column
shows the third mechanism as well: one heartbeat at `at_ms == 0`, leaked in
from the previous scenario.

P1's 4-against-3 is not evidence about the current tree — its 1753→2703 gap is
950 ms, so that build's cadence was wrong and has since been fixed (P2 measures
2975 ms against 3026 ms). The count instability is what survives.

520 needs `collapse_repeats = ["move_entity_heartbeat"]` and R1's collapse, for
the same reason and with the same falsification: a server that never sends the
heartbeat still fails, because the collapsed projection is one against zero.

## 2. The three instrument defects, ranked first because they are cheapest and because two of them will re-break what just landed

### R1 — `collapse_repeats` cannot reach `strict`, and a free-running timer therefore decides six verdicts

**Mechanism** (§0.2, §0.5): `collapse_runs` is adjacency-keyed and runs on the
projection. Declared projections have already deleted the interleaving kinds;
strict projections have not. Both the chest lid (250 ms,
`ContainerOpenersCounter.recheckOpeners` 167-186) and the tracker heartbeat
(3.0 s, `ServerEntity.sendChanges` 531-538) are unconditional re-arming
broadcasts whose count inside a fixed window is set by phase.

**Fix.** Make `collapse_runs` value-keyed rather than adjacency-keyed for the
kinds a scenario names — keep the first observation of each distinct projected
value of that kind and drop every later duplicate regardless of what sits
between them or which step it landed in — and run it on **both** denominators,
exactly as `569323e` did for the heartbeat exception. Then add
`collapse_repeats = ["block_event"]` to 490, 560, 561 and 601-608, and
`["move_entity_heartbeat"]` to 520.

Checked against P2's numbers: every one of the seven rows in §0.2's table
collapses to one `block_event` per stream on both sides, and 520's 2-against-2
and P1's 3-against-4 both collapse to one against one.

**Trap.** Do not collapse before `renumber_entities` and do not collapse
`fields` the projection discards — `compare.rs`'s existing doc comment on
`collapse_runs` already states both, and the value key must be the *projected*
observation, not the raw `Obs`.

**Negative control.** `470-a-furnace-opens-a-screen-a-chest-does-not` and
`480-a-crafting-table-opens-a-menu-with-no-block-entity` carry zero actor-stream
`block_event` in P2 and must still carry zero — a furnace has no lid. `090`
declared must stay `match`. `520` must fail if the heartbeat is deleted: one
against zero is still a divergence.

**How the resulting scenarios could fail.** A server that never opens the lid,
opens it at the wrong position, sends the wrong `b1` viewer count, or signals a
chest nobody opened, all still diverge. What stops being tested is the repeat
count and the step attribution — and that coverage already lives in
`rustmc_server::containers::tests::the_wire_cadence_is_one_signal_every_check_tick_delay_ticks`,
which measures the *gap* rather than the count. **R1 must not ship without that
test, and 520 needs its equivalent for the 60-tick period.** Say it in the
commit: a collapse without a cadence test is a check that could not fail.

**Cost.** One function in `tools/oracle-runner/src/compare.rs`, one line in each
of twelve check files (490, 560, 561, 601-608, 520), one new unit test.
**Converts 560, 520; unblocks 090, 490, 561, 601-608.**

### R2 — the `within` bound cannot bound a packet the decoder does not decode

**Mechanism** (§0.3): `place` reads `fields["entity"]` and `fields["at"]`; an
undecoded packet has neither; `near(None, …)` returns `true`. The corpus's one
defence against cross-scenario leakage is off for exactly the packets that leak.

Census over P1, both streams, undecoded kinds:

| kind | id | vanilla | ours | scenarios | carries an entity id? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `packet:0x8A` waypoint | 138 | 440 | 0 | 5 | no — a UUID |
| `packet:0x4A` recipe_book_add | 74 | 39 | 0 | 3 | no |
| `packet:0x00` bundle_delimiter | 0 | 32 | 8 | 8 | no |
| `packet:0x53` rotate_head | 83 | 28 | 4 | 5 | **yes** |
| `packet:0x60` set_cursor_item | 96 | 13 | 13 | 8 | no |
| `packet:0x38` move_entity_rot | 56 | 6 | 3 | 4 | **yes** |
| `packet:0x83` update_attributes | 131 | 4 | 0 | 2 | **yes** |
| `packet:0x13` container_set_data | 19 | 4 | 4 | 1 | no |
| `packet:0x6C` set_player_inventory | 108 | 1 | 0 | 1 | no |

**Fix.** Add decoder arms in `tools/oracle-runner/src/trace.rs` for the three
that lead with a varint entity id — `rotate_head` (83),
`move_entity_rot` (56), `update_attributes` (131). Each is a varint id plus a
body the arm may keep as `rest`; the *id* is the whole point, because it is
what `place` needs.

**Trap.** Decoding a kind does not silence it, it *bounds* it. The three
`rotate_head` in 180/235/270 that both servers already emit identically must
keep being compared — they are about the actor, who is at the anchor. The
change must be in `decode`, and `place`'s existing rule that only `add_entity`
seeds the table must not be relaxed; `compare.rs` lines 300-331 record the
measurement that refuted seeding from `entity_position` and it stands.

**Negative control.** `180-stairs-make-a-corner-when-two-meet`,
`235-a-bed-facing-north-puts-its-head-the-other-way` and
`270-sign-takes-a-sixteenth-of-a-turn` are strict `match` in P1 with
`packet:0x53` equal on both sides; they must stay `match` after the arm exists,
which proves the arm decodes rather than deletes. `530` must **not** convert on
R2 alone — its `packet:0x83` is about the tracked player at `[0,0,5]`, inside
the bound, and it is real (S1).

**How it could fail.** A server that sends `rotate_head` for the wrong entity,
or does not send it at all, fails 180/235/270. If it could not, the arm has
deleted the kind instead of decoding it — check by inverting: a build that
suppresses our `rotate_head` must turn those three red.

**Cost.** Three decoder arms. **Unblocks 090; makes 080's leak analysis
repeatable; costs nothing anywhere else.**

### R3 — a broadcast about an entity the scenario never touched is not evidence about the scenario

**Mechanism** (§0.4): the reference and subject traces are two separate client
sessions, so any packet triggered by a client-side input the scenario does not
drive is two independent draws. Measured rate in P2: one stray
`entity_position` per ~8 scenario windows, in both directions.

**Fix.** The same shape as the heartbeat exception `569323e` already added:
drop `entity_position` from **both** projections unless the scenario's
`observe` list names it.

**Trap.** This is the rule most likely to become a check that could not fail,
and the guard is already in the corpus: **`540-a-player-that-leaves-the-ground-is-resynced`
names `entity_position` in its `observe` list.** A server that stopped sending
the packet fails 540 and nothing else changes. Do not widen the rule to
`move_entity` — `080` and `520` read those and there is no positive control
left if they go.

**Negative control.** 540 must stay `diverge`-for-the-right-reason and must
turn red on any build that deletes `entity_position`. 190 and 200 are the
before/after pair: in P1 they read strict `diverge` with
`entity_position 1->0` and `0->1` respectively — the same packet in opposite
directions in one run, which is the pair `PARITY-GAP.md` §0.2 used — and under
R3 they must convert and then **hold across two consecutive runs**. One run
proves nothing here; a coin landing the same way twice on purpose is the only
evidence that the coin is gone.

**How it could fail.** 540. If 540 is ever retired, R3 must be retired with it.

**Cost.** One `filter` line beside the existing heartbeat one. **Converts 237,
150; removes the 31↔35 tail `PARITY-GAP.md` §0.2 measured.**

implementation, and directs that `popResource` not be booked against it.
`dropitem.rs` exists, but it serves the player-throw/Q-drop path
(`world_send.rs:767-768`), not a block-break drop — `destroy_block`
(`shapes.rs:1629-1630`) still constructs no item entity and says so.

### S1 — `530`, three packets, exact order

`ServerEntity.sendPairingData(ServerPlayer, Consumer<Packet>)` emits, and the
order is load-bearing because the projection compares sequences:

* offsets 32-43 — `entity.getAddEntityPacket(this)` → `add_entity` — *we send this*
* offsets 48-52 `ifnull 79`, 55-74 — `ClientboundSetEntityDataPacket(id, trackedDataValues)`, **only when `trackedDataValues != null`**
* offsets 85-117, 120-137 — `ClientboundUpdateAttributesPacket(id, attributes.getSyncableAttributes())`, only for a `LivingEntity` and only when the collection is non-empty
* offsets 163-245, 248-265 — `ClientboundSetEquipmentPacket(id, pairs)` over `EquipmentSlot.VALUES`, **skipping empty stacks** (209-214 `ifne 235`), only when the list is non-empty
* offsets 285-297 and 312-327 — `ClientboundSetPassengersPacket`, both directions
* offsets 363-382 — `ClientboundSetEntityLinkPacket` when leashed

P1's vanilla stream for 530 step 3 is exactly
`bundle_delimiter · add_entity · set_entity_data · update_attributes ·
set_equipment · bundle_delimiter`, at 4299 ms; ours is the same minus the middle
three. `tracker.rs::pairing_bundle` already documents all three as missing and
says why — this closes its own TODO.

**Trap.** The three packets are cheap and their *payloads* are not. Vanilla's
`set_entity_data` digest is `99a4e94964a5df0a`; a `ClientboundSetEntityDataPacket`
with the right shape and the wrong tracked-data list is a divergence that looks
like the fix worked. The list is the work, not the packet.
`getSyncableAttributes` is a filter, not the whole map — sending every attribute
is the same failure in the other packet. Do the list first, the packet second.

**Negative control.** `add_entity`'s digest is already `dc545a7f9dce13f5` on
both sides in P1 and must not move: a refactor of the pairing bundle that
changes `add_entity`'s bytes trades 530 for `080-other-player-is-an-entity`,
`520` and `530`'s own step 2. And `520` reads the same tracked player.

**How it could fail.** A server that sends the three packets empty, or in the
`add_entity · update_attributes · set_entity_data` order, or for a player with
nothing in hand (`set_equipment` is skipped when every slot is empty — 530's
actor holds something, which is why vanilla sends it), all diverge.

### S2 — `040`, one packet, and the table is already on disk

> **PORTED 2026-08-08 (`fb545fb3`, `78e82189`), and the row below is a
> specification of work that is done, not of work to do.** Anyone briefed onto
> S2 should read this marker first and then §18: the packet, the per-connection
> `known` set, the emit site beside `apply_hand` and the generated
> `data/vanilla/recipe_unlocks.json` are all on `main`. What was still missing
> on 2026-08-10 was not a line of the port — it was that **no test in the tree
> reached the emit site**; §18 closes that and records what the corpus still
> owes.

P1: exactly one `packet:0x4A` on the actor at 339 ms, in **step 2**, which is
`hold minecraft:furnace`. Steps 0 (`hold oak_stairs`) and 3 emit none.

`ServerRecipeBook.addRecipes(Collection<RecipeHolder>, ServerPlayer)`:

* offsets 45-56 — `if (known.contains(id)) continue` — **idempotent; a second
  furnace sends nothing**
* offsets 59-69 — skip `recipe.isSpecial()`
* offsets 72-98 — add to `known`, `addHighlight`, collect displays
* offsets 115-137 — **one** `ClientboundRecipeBookAddPacket(entries, false)`
  (`iconst_0` at 133 is `replace`), sent only when the collected list is
  non-empty
* offsets 103-109 — fires `CriteriaTriggers.RECIPE_UNLOCKED` afterwards

What decides the content is data we already ship. In
`oracle-work/vanilla-26.2/generated-data/data/minecraft/advancement/recipes/`,
exactly **two** advancements name `minecraft:furnace` as an
`inventory_changed` item: `decorations/smoker.json` (criterion `has_furnace`,
reward `minecraft:smoker`) and `decorations/furnace.json`, whose
`inventory_changed` criterion is on `#minecraft:stone_crafting_materials`, not
on the furnace. So the packet carries exactly `minecraft:smoker`, once.

The general engine is advancements. The **narrow** mechanism that closes 040 is
a generated table: item → recipes unlocked by an `inventory_changed` criterion
naming it, built at `gen-gameplay-tables.sh` time from the advancement JSON,
plus a per-player `known` set.

**Trap.** `oak_stairs` unlocks nothing, and 040 has the negative control built
into itself at step 0. A table keyed on "the recipe that produces this item"
rather than "the recipes this item unlocks" produces a packet at step 0 and
fails 040 while looking like it works.

**Negative control.** 040 step 0, in the same scenario. Also `562-a-crafting-table-turns-a-log-into-planks`
and `611`, which set items and must not gain a `recipe_book_add`.

**How it could fail.** Emit on every inventory change → fails 040 step 0. Emit
twice for the same recipe → fails, because `known` gates at offset 51. Emit the
furnace recipe instead of the smoker recipe → fails on the payload.

### S3 — `080`, and it is two different mechanisms wearing one row

> **SETTLED 2026-08-08, branch `gameplay-place-sound`. The heading undercounts:
> it is THREE mechanisms.** Place sound, step sound and waypoint share one
> `SoundType` table between the first two and nothing else, and only the second
> and third are on 080's critical path — the place sound converts nothing by
> itself, exactly as the negative control below predicts. Six things this
> section did not have, all read out of the pinned jar and recorded in
> `docs/WORKLIST.md`'s cold-start block:
>
> 1. **`Player.playSound(SoundEvent, float, float)` is overridden and passes
>    `this`** where `Entity`'s passes `aconst_null`. That is why the step sound
>    is on the observer's stream and not the walker's, and `Player.getSoundSource()`
>    makes it `PLAYERS` (7), not `BLOCKS` (4).
> 2. **The two step sounds are predicted, not observed-then-explained.**
>    `moveDist += horizontalDistance * 0.6`, fire when `moveDist > nextStep`,
>    then `nextStep = floor(moveDist) + 1`. 080's two four-block hops give 2.4
>    and 4.8 against 1 and 3.
> 3. **The count is NOT invariant to how the walk is chopped up**, which a unit
>    test asserted and T0 refuted: eight one-block packets give **four** sounds
>    and two four-block packets give two, because `nextStep()` discards the
>    overshoot. 080's "two" is a fact about `hop_to`'s `HOP = 4`.
> 4. **Both `packet:0x8A` bodies are TRACK, not UPDATE**, because
>    `BlockConnection.isBroken()` is `distanceManhattan() > 1` and a four-block
>    hop breaks the connection; the remake sends `connect()` and does not
>    disconnect first, so it costs one packet and not two.
> 5. **Both bodies are reproduced byte-exactly** from the stream codec — digests
>    `48d2aef46e816d05` and `a94195be44c89f19`, `crate::waypoints`' own test.
> 6. **Rule 27 is settled by implementing the transmitter.**
>    `GameRules.LOCATOR_BAR` is `registerBoolean("locator_bar", PLAYER, true)`
>    — `iconst_1` — and `ci/t2-gameplay.sh` never sets it, so both servers run
>    at the default and no reference is silenced.
>
> **MEASURED 2026-08-09, and the row is closed.** Full corpus,
> `ci/t2-gameplay.sh`, tip `65b1e04b`: **declared 60/86 -> 60/86, strict
> 57/86 -> 58/86**, with `080` going `(match, diverge) -> (match, match)` and
> being the **only** verdict change in the corpus. The before-figure is
> `~/rustmc-recipebook`'s run of 2026-08-08 23:06 — the S2 branch now in
> `main` — which records 080 as declared `match` / strict `diverge`.
>
> **The 32 behaved exactly as this section said they would: none of them
> converts**, because all 32 are `observe_from = "actor"` and delete the
> stream the sound lands on. What they gained is real and was measured:
> **26 of the 32 observer streams are now identical to vanilla on event id,
> position, source and volume**, against 32 empty streams before. The six
> that are not each expose a defect *elsewhere*, with the place sound itself
> correct in all six — two placement defects (`170` puts the second slab in
> the block above instead of making a double slab, `250` places one snow
> layer where vanilla places two), two missing `block.piston.extend`
> (`380`, `390`), and two `isSecondaryUseActive` (`552`, `609`, where the
> absent sneak flag makes us flip a lever or open a chest instead of placing
> on it). §6's **`unblocks`** column was the right word; `converts` would
> have been the wrong one.
>
> **A new cost this made visible.** `ServerLevel.playSound`'s
> `volume > 1.0 ? volume * 16 : 16` broadcast distance is not modelled, and
> until a walking sound existed nothing could see that: every sound this
> server played was at a block the actor stood next to. `530` now gets
> **68** step sounds on the observer where vanilla gives **22**, 51 of ours
> beyond 16 blocks. No verdict cost — 530 is strict `diverge` on G5 either
> way — but it is a precondition for any walking check further out than 16
> blocks.

P1's 080 delta is `packet:0x8A 2->0; sound 2->0`, one of each per step, and
`observe_from = "both"` so both are in the projection.

**The sound is `minecraft:block.grass.step` (759), volume 0.15, pitch 1.0** —
`Entity.playStepSound`, `SoundType.getVolume() * 0.15`, on the observer's
stream. It is a consequence of the player *moving* through `Entity.move`, not
of the move packet arriving. The same sound is the whole of `540`'s sound delta
(`observe_from = "observer"`), and it appears five times on the observer's
stream in `551-attacking-from-out-of-range` at z = 16, 12, 8, 4, 3 — one per
block walked — where `observe_from = "actor"` hides all five. 551's own delta
is `entity.player.attack.nodamage` (1304), which is a different item.

**The waypoint is the locator bar.** `ServerWaypointManager.createConnection`
offsets 0-5 are `if (player == transmitter) return` — a player never receives
their own — and offsets 6-13 gate the whole thing on
`GameRules.LOCATOR_BAR`.

That gamerule is the decision. Setting `locatorBar false` deletes 440 packets
across five scenarios in one line — and **setting it on vanilla only is
`docs/ORACLE.md` rule 27 exactly**, a reference silenced by the instrument. The
honest forms are: implement the transmitter, or set the rule **on both servers
and honour it**, paired with a scenario that sets it `true` and asserts the
waypoint. Without that scenario, a server that has never heard of the locator
bar is indistinguishable from one that honours the rule, which is a check that
could not fail manufactured by our own hand.

**Trap.** 080's `observe` list is `["move_entity", "entity_position"]` and
vanilla sends no `move_entity` in its window at all
(`PARITY-GAP.md` §3, third `(b)` case). The declared `match` rests on
`entity_position`, which we produce by relaying the client. Converting 080's
strict verdict does not make 080 measure server-side movement. **Fixing the
strict column here is worth less than the other four and should be ranked
accordingly.**

**Negative control, and it is the largest single one in the corpus.** In P1,
**32 scenarios carry a `*.place` sound on vanilla, all 32 are
`observe_from = "actor"`, and in all 32 the sound is on the *observer's* stream
only** — 020, 030, 040, 060, 100, 120, 130, 131, 140, 150, 170, 180, 190, 200,
210, 220, 230, 235, 239, 240, 250, 270, 300, 370, 380, 390, 410, 440, 450, 460,
552, 609. Zero exceptions. `BlockItem.place` offsets 208-220 pass the placing
player into `Level.playSound`, so `PlayerList.broadcast(except)` (offsets
33-39) hides it from the placer. **A place sound broadcast to everybody
converts nothing and breaks thirty-two actor-stream scenarios in one commit** —
**twenty-one of them** (020, 030, 060, 100, 120, 130, 131, 140, 150, 180, 210,
220, 230, 235, 239, 240, 270, 300, 370, 450, 460) read strict `match` in P1 and
would be bought straight back to `diverge`.

**Cost note, and the reason S3 is worth doing anyway.** The place sound is
`(SoundType.getVolume() + 1.0F) / 2.0F` and `SoundType.getPitch() * 0.8F` —
`BlockItem.place` offsets 223-231 and 232-239, `fconst_1 fadd fconst_2 fdiv`
and `ldc 0.8f fmul`. Checked against the recording: stone volume 1.0 pitch 0.8;
rail `block.metal.place` pitch 1.2, which is `SoundType.METAL`'s 1.5 × 0.8. One
`SoundType` table closes the observer half of **32** scenarios and is the
cheapest sound work left.

### S5 — `602`, and the branch is a loop

`AbstractContainerMenu.quickMoveStack(Player, int)` is **abstract** — every menu
implements its own. `doClick`'s arm, offsets 664-741:

* 664-667 — `if (input != QUICK_MOVE) goto 744`
* 670-674 — `if (slotIndex < 0) return`
* 675-686 — `slot = slots.get(slotIndex)`
* 688-698 — `if (!slot.mayPickup(player)) return`
* 699-706 — `ItemStack moved = quickMoveStack(player, slotIndex)`
* **708-738 — a loop**: while `!moved.isEmpty()` and
  `ItemStack.isSameItem(slot.getItem(), moved)`, call `quickMoveStack` again
* the cursor is never read or written anywhere in the arm

**Trap.** The loop. A one-shot implementation moves one stack's worth and stops;
601 and 603 move a single stack and would pass, and a scenario with a slot
holding more than one destination's worth would not. It is the difference
between "shift-click moves an item" and "shift-click empties the slot".

**Negative control.** `561-clicking-an-empty-chest-slot-changes-nothing` (the
same click as `PICKUP`) and 602's own step 2 must stay silent, while 602's step
3 — the non-empty `QUICK_MOVE` `e894224` added — must speak. Both directions are
in one file, which is what makes 602 a control again.

**How it could fail.** 602's own file states it: "a server that answers every
QUICK_MOVE click with a correction fails at step 2, and a server that answers no
QUICK_MOVE click at all fails at step 3." 603 fails a one-directional stub.

### S4 — `050`, seven packets, and a trap that no amount of correctness clears

> **REFUTED AND CLOSED, 2026-08-08 — read §11 before acting on anything
> below.** `050` cannot convert: vanilla fails it against itself, strict,
> 2 of 2 pairwise comparisons at N = 3. `605` and `606` are newly measured
> unstable on the *gated* denominator; `350` and `500` were already
> declared so. The trap this section names is real and is **narrower than
> the truth**: `add_entity`'s `rest` digest also carries a random spawn
> yaw (`ItemEntity(EntityType, Level)` offsets 39-52), the item's own
> generator advances by six draws and not two, and the difference between
> two vanilla runs of 050 is *which packets exist*, not what is in them.
> `070` held as the control throughout.

P1's vanilla actor stream for 050, in order: `level_event 2001 at [1,1,0] data
3370` (19 ms — **this one `569323e` should now emit**, since the torch is
destroyed by the cascade), `bundle_delimiter`, `add_entity` kind 71 at
`[1.3100386132917947, 1.2204982073363198, 0.2676194821831062]`,
`set_entity_data`, `bundle_delimiter`, a second `set_entity_data` at 59 ms, and
then at 471 ms `take_item_entity` · `container_set_slot slot 36 window 0` ·
`remove_entities`.

`Block.popResource(Level, BlockPos, ItemStack)`:

* offsets 0-11 — `d = EntityType.ITEM.getHeight() / 2.0`
* offsets 12-16 — `RandomSource random = level.getRandom()`
* offsets 18-38, 41-61, 66-86 — **three** `Mth.nextDouble(random, -0.25, 0.25)`
  draws, x then y then z, with `- d` on y (offsets 62-63)
* offsets 89-104 → private `popResource(Level, Supplier, ItemStack)`: gamerule
  `BLOCK_DROPS` at 19-35, `setDefaultPickUpDelay()` at 50-52, `addFreshEntity`
  at 55-58

`ItemEntity(Level, double, double, double, ItemStack)` offsets 23-61 then draw
**two more**, from the entity's *own* `random`, for the x and z of
`setDeltaMovement(r.nextDouble()*0.2-0.1, 0.2, r.nextDouble()*0.2-0.1)`.

Arithmetic check against the recording: x − 1.5 = −0.18996, y − 1.375 =
−0.15450, z − 0.5 = −0.23238, all inside ±0.25. The 471 ms pickup is
`setDefaultPickUpDelay`'s 10 ticks.

**The trap, and it is the largest single one in this document.** `add_entity`'s
`at` and `set_entity_motion`'s `v` are compared byte-exactly and are functions
of a mutable RNG stream. **A correct drop, a correct pickup delay, a correct
inventory packet and a correct removal still diverge on three digits of a
coordinate**, and no implementation of the drop chain converts these scenarios
unless the tick's random consumption is parity-exact.

Which field is poisoned is not the same for every member, and it was checked
rather than assumed. From P1's `add_entity` positions:

| scenario | spawner | `add_entity.at` | RNG-bound field |
|---|---|---|---|
| 050, 350 | `Block.popResource` | `[1.3100386…, 1.2204982…, 0.2676194…]` | **the position** — three `Level.random` draws |
| 500, 605, 606 | `Player.drop` | `[0.0, 1.3199999928474426, 0.0]` — `eyeY − 0.3`, exact | **the motion** — `v = [0.0034792…, 0.0, 0.14368552…]` |
| 070 | `FallingBlockEntity` | `[1.5, 1.0, 0.5]` — the block centre, exact | **neither.** 070 is not an RNG problem at all |

The precedent for what to do is in this tree: `569323e` dropped `sound.pitch`
from the comparison beside the existing `let _seed`, for a field drawn the same
way, and bought the coverage back in unit tests. The equivalent here is to drop
`add_entity.at` **for item entities only** and `set_entity_motion.v`, and to
assert their ranges in a unit test — the `popResource` offset is in
[−0.25, 0.25] on each axis, less half the item's height on y.

Dropping `add_entity.at` unconditionally would be the wrong shape: 070's is
exact and is real evidence, and so is 530's `[0.0, 0.0, 5.0]`.

**And the trap inside the trap:** `place` reads `fields["at"]` at
`compare.rs::Verdict` (`:295`) to seed the entity table, and it runs at line 400, **before**
the projection's `map` at line 476. Dropping the field in `decode` destroys the
entity bound for every item entity in the corpus. It must be dropped in the
`map`, not in `decode`. Get that backwards and the fix converts 050 and
silently unbounds the drop family.

**Negative control.** `010-break-block` — a dig that drops nothing observable —
must stay strict `match`; it is the control that survived the last round and it
is the control for this one. `070-sand-falls-when-unsupported` must **not**
convert on S4: its `add_entity` is exact and its blocker is
`FallingBlockEntity` plus eight `block_update` against our two, so a round that
converts 070 while claiming credit for the drop chain has done something else.
`500-dropping-an-item-throws-it-on-the-floor` must move from `diverge` to a
*different* `diverge` rather than to `match` — its `move_entity` and
`set_entity_motion` are the physics half, and the drop chain alone gives an
item entity no gravity.

**How it could fail.** A server that spawns the item and never lets the player
pick it up fails on `take_item_entity`. One that hands the item over instantly
fails on the 10-tick delay. One that omits the bundle delimiters fails on the
frame boundaries, which P1 shows are two per spawn.

These are not gap members; they fail both denominators, and they are the bulk of
what "remaining gameplay parity" means. Grouped by the one thing that closes
each family, with the anchor read from the jar. Depth here is deliberately
lower than §3 — these are families to scope, not items to start tomorrow.

## 5. Scenarios that are not tests as written

The evidence standard asks for the server that would fail each fix. Where no
such server exists, the honest answer is to say so rather than to specify work.

> **STATUS STAMPED 2026-08-11**, against the tree at `7ccad044` and the corpus
> artefact named in §19. Two of the four rows are **closed by instrument work
> that has since landed** and read `match`/`match` today; the other two stand,
> one of them more strongly than when it was written. The closing rule at the
> bottom of this section has been carried out, and it found a **third**
> instance neither of its two named candidates.

* **`090-chest-opens-a-screen`, under `strict`.** §0.3. Its strict verdict is a
  product of two phases neither of which is about chests, and one of them is a
  mob another scenario left alive. Its **declared** verdict is sound and is not
  affected. R1 and R2 make the strict column meaningful; until both land, 090's
  strict result should not be read as evidence in either direction.
  → **CLOSED.** R1, R2 and R3 landed together in `20b41e34`. 090 is
  `match`/`match` at `7ccad044`. The condition this bullet set — "until both
  land" — is met, and the strict column may now be read.
* **`520-a-standing-player-is-rebroadcast-on-a-timer`, under `strict`.** §0.5.
  6.0 s window, 3.0 s cadence, two independently-phased servers. A count
  comparison at 1.98 periods cannot be a measurement. Its declared verdict is
  fine.
  → **CLOSED.** R1's value-keyed collapse plus
  `collapse_repeats = ["move_entity_heartbeat"]` (`20b41e34`) removed the count
  comparison. 520 is `match`/`match`. Note what did **not** happen: the
  scenario was not made to pass by widening, it was made to stop measuring a
  phase — and the falsification §2 R1 registered still holds, a server that
  never sends the heartbeat fails one-against-zero.
* **`080-other-player-is-an-entity`.** `PARITY-GAP.md` §3 already classified it
  `(b)`; nothing here changes that. It observes `move_entity` and
  `entity_position`, vanilla sends no `move_entity` in its window, and the
  `entity_position` it matches on is one we produce by relaying the client's own
  packet. **It would pass against a server with no server-side entity movement
  at all, which is the server we have.** It is the same shape as
  `PARITY-GAP.md` §0.1's 602 and it should carry the same note until
  `Entity.move` drives players.
  → **CONVERTED, AND THE CAVEAT STANDS UNCHANGED.** 080 is `match`/`match`
  since S3 (`e54ec9ec`). That is a statement about the waypoint and the step
  sound, not about entity movement: this bullet's sentence is still true word
  for word, and 080's green must not be quoted as movement coverage. This is
  the clearest case in the document of **ported and witnessed being different
  claims** — the row converted and the thing the row is named after is still
  unbuilt.
* **`050-torch-falls-with-its-support`, as coverage.** Its `observe` list sees a
  third of what its rig provokes. That is `PARITY-GAP.md` §3's finding and it

  strict column" is refuted — §11 measured 050 strict-unstable against vanilla
  itself, and §16.3 sited the cause upstream of any tick, in the four
  `nextFloat()` draws of `LivingEntity.createItemStackToDrop`. So 050 is not
  merely narrow coverage, it is a **strict column nothing can convert**. It is
  `match`/`diverge` at `7ccad044` and counted under cannot-convert in §19.1.

And one rule the corpus is still missing, carried from `PARITY-GAP.md` §6 and
now with a second instance: **a check that asserts an absence must name a
positive control.** 602 had none and `e894224` fixed it by hand. `470`'s "a
chest does not open a screen" half and `608`'s out-of-range slot are the same
shape and have not been checked for it.

## 7. Figures published here, and their windows

Every count above is a corpus figure, and a corpus figure's window is its
**pair identity, tree, scenario count and stream**, in the way a worldgen
figure's is dimension/seed/radius/centre/chunks/refs. `ci/figures.toml` has no
`kind = "corpus"` yet and lives on `published-figures-audit`, which this branch
is not based on and which the merge queue owns; the entries below are written
to be pasted into it unchanged when the two meet. Nothing under `ci/` was
touched by this branch.

> **STATUS, 2026-08-11: ALL FOUR ENTRIES BELOW ARE UNREGISTERED AND ALL FOUR
> ARE UNREGISTRABLE. DO NOT PASTE THEM.** Checked against the tree at
> `7ccad044` rather than assumed, and there are three separate reasons, any one
> of which is sufficient:
>
> 1. **The schema was never adopted.** `ci/figures.toml` has no `kind =
>    "corpus"` entry and never gained one. What it gained instead is `kind =
>    "corpus-floor"` — two entries, `corpus-floor-n6` and
>    `corpus-floor-n6-gpfloors` — and the header comment above them says in as
>    many words that this section's claim, "ORACLE rule 6 has nothing to say
>    about it", was true of a count of packets and false of a count of
>    scenarios. That correction is already recorded in the fence below; what
>    was not recorded is that the schema it was written for does not exist.
> 2. **Every artefact named below is destroyed.** `pair = "P1"` and
>    `pair = "P2"` were recorded 2026-08-07, and **no gameplay recording from
>    before 2026-08-08 21:26 survives anywhere on the box** — checked across
>    every `~/rustmc*` tree. `oracle-work/gameplay/subset/vanilla.json`, which
>    three of the four name, exists in **zero** trees. This is the same
>    disqualifier `corpus-floor-n6` carries and it should be written the same
>    way: `quotable = false`, `disqualifier = "destroyed"`.
> 3. **A figure whose artefact is gone cannot be re-derived by re-running.** A
>    new corpus run produces a new pair, not P1; a figure's window *is* its
>    pair identity, which this section's own opening sentence says. So the
>    honest disposition is to keep these four as the record of what was
>    published and register nothing.
>
> **What to do with the numbers instead.** Two of the four have since been
> superseded by measurements over artefacts that do survive, and those are the
> ones to quote: the `rotate_head` leak by §9's preimage recovery (all seven of
> 090's are entity 5, recovered outright rather than inferred from a digest),
> and the stray-`entity_position` rate by R3's landing in `20b41e34`. The lid
> step-attribution figure and the undecoded census have no survivor and should
> be quoted, if at all, as history with their date attached.

# about it", AND IT IS WRONG. Corrected 2026-08-09; see §13.** Rule 6 has
# exactly as much to say about a count of scenarios as about a count of
# blocks: two independently recorded vanilla runs disagree about **9 of 88**
# of them, so a corpus count with no floor beside it is a count with a lie in
# its denominator. `ci/figures.toml` now carries `kind = "corpus-floor"` and

pattern `[0-9]+\.[0-9]{4,}%` finds nothing here, and this file is not in its
`docs` list. **The subset numbers 3/23 and 16/23 are deliberately not restated
as a corpus figure** — `569323e`'s own message already says a subset produces no
corpus figure, and repeating it in a document a reader could quote is how the
last five refuted numbers got into circulation.

## 8. What would settle what this could not

Two things are asserted here by elimination rather than by direct measurement,
and each has one run that would close it.

* **560's residual is the lid and not the sound.** Argued from 490 and 561
  reading strict `match` in the treatment run with the same
  `block.chest.open`. The run that settles it directly: re-record the
  cheapest-five subset at `569323e` **without overwriting the traces**, and diff
  560's `block_event` step attribution against vanilla's. One subset run, no
  server change.
* **R1 converts what §2 says it converts.** The collapse arithmetic was done on
  P2's recorded edges by hand. The run that settles it: apply R1 to
  `tools/oracle-runner` alone, re-project the *existing* P1 and P2 traces
  offline, and compare verdicts. **No server and no corpus run is needed** —
  `compare.rs` reads two JSON files, and both are on disk. That is the cheapest
  proof in this document and it should be the first thing the next round does.

## 9. What R1-R3 measured once they were built — 2026-08-07, branch `oracle-instrument-fixes`

Written after the fact, against the same two pairs plus a third, and it
corrects §2 in four places. §2 is left standing rather than edited, because
the arguments that turned out to be wrong are worth reading beside their
refutation.

**Pairs used.** P1 and P2 as §0 defines them, plus **P3** — 86 scenarios,
recorded 2026-08-06 09:41 / 09:58 in `~/rustmc-chain-signs-0806` on the box —
which is the second full-corpus pair §2 R3 asks for and which §0 did not know
about. Every number below comes from `oracle-runner compare` run offline on
those recordings. No server was started and no corpus run was taken.

### The pairs are stale against this branch's own base, and that decides half of it

Both P1 (tree `a938d64`, 02:19) and P2 (tree `e894224`, 07:10) were recorded
**before `569323e`**, which is this branch's grandparent. `569323e` added the
`level_event 2001` emission and the block sounds. So every scenario whose
residual `569323e` closed still shows that residual in these traces, and no
amount of instrument work can convert it offline:

* `237`'s strict projection under R1+R3 is `[level_event, section_blocks_update,
  block_changed_ack]` against `[section_blocks_update, block_changed_ack]`. The
  stray `entity_position` §0.4 measured **is gone** — R3 removed it — and what
  is left is the `2001` we did not yet send. §2 says R3 converts 237; **it does
  not, on any trace on disk, and the reason is the trace and not R3.**
* `560`'s strict projection under R1 goes from 17 against 16 to **10 against
  9**: the eight lid events on each side collapse to one, exactly as §2 R1
  predicts. The one observation left over is vanilla's `sound` 349
  (`block.chest.open`) at index 0. **§0.2's elimination argument — "560's
  residual is the lid and not the sound" — is refuted by direct measurement.**
  It was the sound, and R1 is still right about the lid.
* `090` under R1+R2 goes from vanilla 14 / ours 6 to **vanilla 7 / ours 6**,
  and the single remaining item is the same `sound`.

**The run that settles all three**: one full-corpus recording at this branch's
tip. Nothing else is needed — no server change, no new check.

### Measured conversions

| pair | strict, before | after | converted |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | 35/86 | **37/86** | `190-lever-attaches-to-a-floor-or-a-wall`, `200-ladder-hangs-off-the-wall-behind-it` |
| P2 | 4/23 | **5/23** | `060-coral-dries-out-unprompted` |
| P3 | 32/86 | **35/86** | `150-torch-on-a-wall-faces-out`, `470-a-furnace-opens-a-screen-a-chest-does-not`, `571-a-second-edit-of-the-same-sign-is-ignored` |

**Declared is unchanged in all three pairs** — 56/86, 20/23, 53/86 — and that
is structural rather than lucky: both projection exceptions are reachable only
when `kinds` is `None`, which only `strict` passes.
`neither_projection_exception_can_move_the_declared_denominator` pins it.

**Every one of those conversions is R3.** R1's twelve new `collapse_repeats`
declarations convert **nothing** on any pair, because the scenarios they free
are all blocked on the missing `sound`. R2 converts nothing either. That is the
honest attribution and it is the opposite of what §6's ranking implies.

The three pairs also settle what §2 R3 asked two runs to settle, and the answer
is better than "it holds twice": **the scenarios that convert are different in
every pair**, and in each pair they are exactly the ones that run's coin landed
on. 190 and 200 read strict-`diverge` in P1 and strict-`match` in P3; 150 reads
`match` in P1 and `diverge` in P3; 060 reads `match` in P1 and `diverge` in P2.
R3 converts whichever ones fell, in every pair, and makes nothing worse in any.

### Two corrections to §2's method

* **R1's fix is narrower than §2 specified, deliberately.** §2 asks for "the
  first observation of each distinct projected value … regardless of what sits
  between them". That also collapses `open · shut · open` to `open · shut`,
  which stops distinguishing a chest that was reopened from one that stayed
  shut. The shipped rule keys on adjacency **within the named kind's own
  subsequence**, which removes the defect — dependence on unrelated kinds —
  and gives up nothing: on every trace on disk the two rules collapse exactly
  the same observations, because no lid in this corpus alternates. `step` and
  the timing bucket do leave the key, and leave the surviving observation too;
  §2 is right that they must.
* **§2 R2's named negative control does not exercise the arm.**
  `180`, `235` and `270` are strict `match` before and after — but their
  `packet:0x53` is on the **observer** stream and all three declare
  `observe_from = "actor"`, so it was never in either projection. They prove
  the arm broke nothing; they cannot prove it decodes rather than deletes. The
  control that does is `080-spawn-egg-makes-a-mob`, whose `rotate_head` is
  about an entity at its own anchor: against a subject mutated to name the
  wrong entity, to send no `rotate_head` at all, or to send one with a
  different rotation, 080's strict goes red in all three cases. And rewriting
  `090`'s leaked packets to name the *actor* — a player, never placed, so never
  bounded — puts all seven back into the projection and turns 090 red, which is
  what proves the bound is positional rather than a deletion by kind.

### What §2 R2 got exactly right, confirmed by preimage rather than by digest

§0.3 argued from a byte-identical digest that 090's `rotate_head` are 080's
mob. The entity ids are recoverable outright: the trailing digest is FNV-1a
over two bytes, so the wire body can be searched for by brute force and
accepted only when its digest reproduces the recorded string. Done for all 28
of vanilla's `packet:0x53` and all 6 `packet:0x38` in P1:

* every one of 090's seven is **entity 5**, the mob 080 spawned and never
  removed — six at `at_ms == 0`;
* 180's, 235's and 270's are **entity 1**, the actor;
* our side never emits one for entity 5 anywhere, because there is no spawn egg.

(The search needs the repo's actual multiplier, `0x1000_0000_01b3` in
`trace::digest`, which is **not** the FNV-1a 64-bit prime `0x100000001b3` — an
extra zero group. Harmless as a hash and worth knowing before anyone tries to
reproduce a digest by hand.)

### The audit §2 R2 implies, carried out

`compare::near`'s doc comment now carries it in full. In one line: after R2,
**every kind still undecoded in the corpus is one that no decoder could bound**
— `javap` on the pinned jar shows waypoint identifies by `Either<UUID, String>`,
and recipe_book_add, set_cursor_item, container_set_data, set_player_inventory
and bundle_delimiter carry neither an entity id nor a position. What R2 removed
was the case where the information was on the wire and the instrument declined
to read it. Three narrower instances of the same shape are named there and left
unfixed, the largest being that `place` reads the field named `entity` while
`renumber_entities` walks any `$entity` at any depth — so `take_item_entity`,
which names its two `item` and `taker`, is renumbered and **not** bounded.

## 10. S1, measured — 2026-08-08, branch `gameplay-pairing-data`

### `set_equipment` is not one of the middle three

§3 S1 says P1's 530 stream is `bundle_delimiter · add_entity ·
set_entity_data · update_attributes · set_equipment · bundle_delimiter` and
that "530's actor holds something, which is why vanilla sends it". **The
entity 530 pairs on the actor's stream is the observer, which holds nothing**,
and `sendPairingData` offsets 209-214 skip empty stacks and 238-245 send
nothing for an empty list. Two independent vanilla recordings agree: the
actor's stream at step 3 is `bundle_delimiter · add_entity · set_entity_data ·
update_attributes · bundle_delimiter`, five packets and not six. The
`set_equipment` in that scenario is on the **observer's** stream, about the
actor, which is carrying something a previous scenario put in its hand — and
`observe_from = "actor"`, which `strict` honours, so it is outside the
projection either way.

So S1 is **two** packets for 530, not three, and the `set_equipment` row of
§3's cost estimate is a packet nothing in the corpus asks for.

### `set_entity_data`'s payload, derived and confirmed

`09 03 41 A0 00 00 10 00 7F FF` — accessor 9 (`LivingEntity.DATA_HEALTH_ID`,
defined `1.0f`) as a `FLOAT` (serializer 3) carrying 20.0f, accessor 16
(`Avatar.DATA_PLAYER_MODE_CUSTOMISATION`, defined `0`) as a `BYTE`
(serializer 0) carrying the client's skin-parts byte, then the `0xFF` EOF
marker. Digested with the recorder's own multiplier this is
`99a4e94964a5df0a`, which is what both vanilla recordings carry for **both**
players. `crate::synched` produces exactly those bytes and asserts the digest.

`Avatar` is the 26.2 trap: it sits between `LivingEntity` and `Player` and
declares the main-hand and customisation accessors, so a chain that goes
straight from `LivingEntity` to `Player` puts customisation at 17.

### `update_attributes` cannot be matched byte-exactly, and this is a null

**Vanilla does not reproduce its own `update_attributes` payload between
runs.** Two full-corpus vanilla recordings of the same 86 scenarios, same
box, 37 minutes apart:

```text
                                   ~/rustmc 21:26     ~/rustmc-recipebook 22:03
  530 actor   add_entity           dc545a7f9dce13f5   dc545a7f9dce13f5
  530 actor   set_entity_data      99a4e94964a5df0a   99a4e94964a5df0a
  530 actor   update_attributes    f3317aeea62070e7   2f7b87fd3772f0a3
  530 observer update_attributes   59b3eb39004cdf55   f1d681b2ff0cf619
  530 observer set_equipment       eebac8b6f92a3cd2   eebac8b6f92a3cd2
```

**Both of 530's moved and neither of `spawn-egg-makes-a-mob`'s did**, which
is the more useful result and corrects a first reading of the same census: a
symmetric difference double-counts, and "four of four moved" was two
observations counted twice. A freshly spawned mob's payload is
`594df060bec3e117` in both runs. The two that moved belong to players that
have been in the session for sixty-odd scenarios.

**The observer is the control that makes this a finding rather than a
coincidence.** It performs no scenario step in the whole corpus — it stands,
is repositioned between scenarios, and unsneaks — and it is the entity the
actor's stream pairs. Its syncable-attribute payload still differs between the
two runs. So the difference is not two runs behaving differently; it is
internal state of the reference implementation that no behaviour of ours can
address.

A one-scenario subset shows the other half of it. Run twice on this branch,
vanilla's 530 payload is byte-identical both times and is only three
snapshots:

```text
  03
  1a 3fb99999a0000000 00        movement_speed        0.1,  no modifiers
  0d 4008000000000000 01 ...    entity_interaction_range 3.0
                                  + minecraft:creative_mode_entity_range 2.0
  08 4012000000000000 01 ...    block_interaction_range  4.5
                                  + minecraft:creative_mode_block_range  0.5
```

Three, because those are the only attributes anything had asked
`AttributeMap.getInstance` for by then — `getInstance` is a
`computeIfAbsent`, so the map holds exactly what has been read or modified.
In a full corpus the same player's map has accumulated more, and *which* more,
in *what* probe order, is what the two runs disagree about. Both halves say
the same thing: the payload is a function of the reference's own read history,
not of anything a client could observe.

**The mechanism, from the bytecode rather than from the coincidence.**
`AttributeMap.getSyncableAttributes()` is
`attributes.values().stream().filter(a -> a.getAttribute().value().isClientSyncable()).collect(toList())`,
and `attributes` is an `it.unimi.dsi.fastutil.objects.Object2ObjectOpenHashMap`
keyed by `Holder<Attribute>`. `Holder$Reference` extends `Object` and
declares neither `hashCode` nor `equals`, so the key's hash is the JVM's
identity hash and the map's iteration order is a slot order derived from it.
`ClientboundUpdateAttributesPacket`'s codec is
`composite(VAR_INT, …, AttributeSnapshot.STREAM_CODEC.apply(list(128)), …)` —
a *list*, written in that iteration order. Nothing about that order is a
property of the server; it is a property of the run.

So **no correct server can make 530 strict-`match` while this payload is
compared byte-exactly**, which makes "S1 converts 530" false as §6 rank 4
states it. This is the same class as `add_entity`'s movement, which
`530`'s own check file already records being taken out of the projection for
exactly this reason, and the same class as `remove_entities`' entity list,
which `trace.rs` already canonicalises because "the list a server sends here
is a set with no order the server chose".

### The before-state, and the blast radius, both measured

`oracle-runner explain --strict` on the 2026-08-08 21:26/21:43 pair in
`~/rustmc` — the run that independently reproduces the brief's baseline,
declared 60/86 and strict 56/86 — gives 530's strict projection exactly:

```text
  strict observations: vanilla 6, ours 4
    [0]    remove_entities   step 2   both
    [1]    packet:0x00       step 3   both        bundle delimiter
    [2]    add_entity        step 3   both        rest dc545a7f9dce13f5
 -> [3]    set_entity_data   step 3   vanilla only, rest 99a4e94964a5df0a
 -> [4]    update_attributes step 3   vanilla only, rest f3317aeea62070e7
 -> [5]    packet:0x00       step 3   vanilla only
```

**Two missing observations, not three, and no `set_equipment` anywhere in the
projection** — the instrument says directly what §3 S1 got wrong.
`observe_from = "actor"` and `strict` honours it.

**The blast radius of the `set_entity_data` change is exactly this scenario.**
Searching both traces for `add_entity` with `kind_id 156`, a player is paired
in **one** scenario in the whole corpus — this one, on both streams, in both
servers. Nothing else can move.

### What this changes about §6 rank 4, and the item that replaces it

**S1 as ranked converts nothing, and that is now measured rather than
predicted.** What it does deliver is exact: `set_entity_data`, the one packet
of the three whose payload is a function of state a clean-room server has,
lands byte-identical to vanilla's. `set_equipment` was never in this
scenario's projection. `update_attributes` is the blocker, and it is not a
blocker any server work removes.

The cost line should read **1 packet, 1 call site, converts nothing, and
retires a row** rather than "3 packets, converts 530".

**The instability is established, not suspected, and the project's own
instrument says so.** `ci/selfcheck-kind-stability.py` over the two
full-corpus vanilla recordings, per kind, across all 86 scenarios:

```text
  update_attributes   1 identical, 1 DIFFERS   (spawn-egg identical; 530 differs)
  set_entity_data     8 identical, 0 differ    (530 among the eight)
  add_entity          2 identical, 6 differ    (530 among the two)
  set_equipment       5 identical, 1 differs   (530 among the five)
```

Read the asymmetry the right way round. **A difference between two vanilla
runs is conclusive** — that script's header puts it plainly, "the reference
cannot disagree with itself about its own behaviour" — so N = 2 is enough to
establish that `update_attributes` is not reproducible. It is *agreement* at
N = 2 that is weak, which is what the N = 12 power argument in
`ci/t2-gameplay-selfcheck.sh` is about. So the eight identical
`set_entity_data` verdicts are encouraging and not proof, and the one
differing `update_attributes` verdict is proof.

Within 530 specifically, the only pairing kind that moves is
`update_attributes`. The packet this branch implemented is a reproducible
quantity; the one it did not is not.

**And that still does not convert 530, which is the part worth being careful
about.** The obvious next move — exempt the payload, as `530`'s own check file
already exempts `add_entity`'s movement — only works if this server emits an
`update_attributes` at all, and any payload it emits is invented. The two
possible exemptions come apart exactly here:

* **a tight one** — decode the snapshots and compare them as a *sorted*
  multiset of `(attribute, base, modifiers)`, dropping only the order — leaves
  the content compared, and the content is the set of attributes the reference
  happened to have called `AttributeMap.getInstance` for. This server's read
  sites are different code, so it would not match, and 530 would still
  diverge;
* **a total one** — compare presence and entity only — does convert 530, and
  it converts it on **packet identity alone**, with content vanilla never
  sends sitting behind it. That is the exact failure §3 S1's own trap
  paragraph names, written by the same hand that would be writing the
  exemption.

So the honest position after this branch is: the payload is not comparable,
and 530 is not convertible by S1. Whether the corpus should keep comparing a
quantity vanilla cannot reproduce is a real question and a separate item — it
belongs with R1-R3, which is where this roadmap already puts instrument work,
and it should be decided by whoever owns the projection, not smuggled in by a
server item that needs it to pass. A useful first move for that item, and
cheap: `ci/selfcheck-kind-stability.py` runs on recordings that already exist,
so every future corpus run is another sample for free.

Do **not** meanwhile give this server an invented payload — the complete
supplier set, say — behind a widened projection. It would pass, it would be
content vanilla never sends, and the check that admitted it would be one more
that cannot fail.

### Measured after — 2026-08-08, tree `2677584a`, box Threadripper

```text
  before   CORPUS declared 60/86 match  (20 diverge, 6 absent, 0 vacuous, 0 inert, 0 error)
           CORPUS strict   56/86 match  (27 diverge, 3 absent, 0 vacuous, 0 inert, 0 error)
  after    CORPUS declared 60/86 match  (20 diverge, 6 absent, 0 vacuous, 0 inert, 0 error)
           CORPUS strict   56/86 match  (27 diverge, 3 absent, 0 vacuous, 0 inert, 0 error)
```

Before is the `~/rustmc` run of 21:26/21:43, which reproduces the
`add7297a` gate figure independently. After is `~/rustmc-pairing`,
`T2-GAMEPLAY GREEN`, no regression and no conversion — the totals could not
move, because a **player** is paired in exactly one scenario in the corpus.

`530` before and after, from `explain --strict`:

```text
  before  vanilla 6, ours 4      after   vanilla 7, ours 5
    remove_entities   both         remove_entities   both
    packet:0x00       both         packet:0x00       both
    add_entity        both         add_entity        both
 -> set_entity_data   vanilla       set_entity_data  BOTH, 99a4e94964a5df0a
 -> update_attributes vanilla    -> update_attributes vanilla, c8d6f1fc1001471b
 -> packet:0x00       vanilla    -> set_equipment     vanilla, cf8206d0d3de2b69
                                 -> packet:0x00       vanilla
```

**`set_entity_data` converted at the observation level** — our digest is
vanilla's, in the right place in the sequence, with `add_entity` unmoved.

**And the `after` column carries a correction to this section's own
`set_equipment` claim.** Four full-corpus vanilla recordings now exist for
2026-08-08. 530's actor stream:

```text
  run                       update_attributes   set_equipment
  ~/rustmc        21:26     f3317aeea62070e7    absent
  ~/rustmc-recipebook 22:03 2f7b87fd3772f0a3    absent
  ~/rustmc-recipebook 23:0x c8d6f1fc1001471b    absent
  ~/rustmc-pairing          c8d6f1fc1001471b    cf8206d0d3de2b69
```

Three distinct `update_attributes` payloads in four runs, and a
`set_equipment` that is **present in one run and absent in three**. So "the
observer holds nothing, therefore vanilla sends no `set_equipment`" is right
about the mechanism and wrong as a standing fact: whether that player is
holding anything when 530 runs depends on what earlier scenarios left in its
inventory. `ci/selfcheck-kind-stability.py` over three of the four agrees —
`set_entity_data` identical in all 3, `update_attributes` and `set_equipment`
differing.

**Which settles the item.** It is not only that `update_attributes`'s payload
is irreproducible; the *set of kinds* vanilla puts in 530's projection is
run-dependent too. A scenario whose reference cannot reproduce its own
observation sequence cannot be converted by making the subject more correct.
