## 11. What S4 measured — 2026-08-08, branch `gameplay-drop-pickup`

**§3 S4 is refuted. `050` cannot convert, and neither can any of the four it
was said to unblock.** Not because the drop chain is hard to port — the
bytecode is short and §3 S4 reads it correctly — but because **vanilla does not
reproduce itself on any member of this group**, under the projection each
member actually uses. A check the reference fails against itself is a check
nothing can pass, and five of the six scenarios S4 names are in that state.

This was measured before a line of the port was written, which is the only
reason it cost an hour instead of a night.

### The instrument, and why it needed no corpus run

`ci/selfcheck-recompare.sh` compares **saved recordings** under today's
comparator. Three full-corpus vanilla recordings existed on the box from three
independent gate/corpus runs earlier the same evening — 21:26, 22:49 and 23:24,
vanilla 26.2, protocol 776, superflat, seed 20260803, sayer-desktop — and none
of them had to be re-taken. Recordings, not servers, so no corpus lock and no
fifty-minute wait.

**The control that makes this admissible.** One of the three trees carries a
modified `tools/oracle-runner/src/trace.rs` (S1's work), so its recording was
taken by a different decoder. Every finding below therefore also appears in the
**N = 2 run over the two recordings whose `trace.rs` is byte-identical**
(md5 `2ee9a949065defb31a0851f3ff8ca2df`). Both runs are quoted; they agree.

```
N = 3   declared 5, measured 9, 77/86 reproduced   strict reproduced 75/86
N = 2   declared 5, measured 9, 77/86 reproduced   strict reproduced 75/86
```

### Re-taken after the rebase, because the instrument moved underneath it

Every figure above was first measured against `main` at `78e82189`. While this
branch was out, `main` reached `05c9a2d3` and **`tools/oracle-runner/src/trace.rs`
gained 52 lines** with S1's work — so the decoder that produced those numbers
is not the decoder in the tree. Re-run on the rebased tree, same three
recordings, unmodified comparator:

```
declared 77/86 reproduced, strict 75/86        — identical
050 torch-falls-with-its-support   strict-unstable 2/2   — identical
605 / 606                          unstable 2/2          — identical
```

The only difference in the report is that 605 and 606 now print as `declared
unstable` rather than `NEWLY UNSTABLE`, which is this branch's own entries in
`gameplay-unstable.toml` being read. Nothing measured moved.

**Both projection experiments were re-taken on the rebased comparator too**,
and both reproduce to the line: the minimal exemption is still output-identical
to the unmodified comparator (declared 77/86, strict 75/86, 050 strict-unstable
2/2, 605/606 2/2), and the maximal one still gives `r1↔r2` declared 80 / strict
75 and `r1↔r3` declared 82 / strict 79, with 050 strict `diverge` then `match`
and 605/606 declared `match` in both pairs. `070` and `010` stay `match`/`match`
in every configuration.

One line of the maximal run is worth quoting because it is the aggregator
grading this branch's own work: it prints **`NO LONGER UNSTABLE
container-click-throw-drops-one-item … gameplay-unstable.toml is stale`** for
both new entries. That is correct and is the point — retiring those two
entries is exactly what a landed exemption would be for, and the file is only
"stale" in a world where the exemption exists. It does not, so they stay.

### The six scenarios S4 names

| # | scenario | S4 claimed | measured, vanilla against itself |
|---|---|---|---|
| 050 | `torch-falls-with-its-support` | **converts** | **strict-unstable 2/2 (N=3), 1/1 (N=2)** |
| 350 | `a-dropped-item-goes-into-your-inventory` | unblocks | declared-unstable 2/2 — already declared, 25/25 at N=26 |
| 500 | `dropping-an-item-throws-it-on-the-floor` | unblocks | declared-unstable 2/2 — already declared, 25/25 at N=26 |
| 605 | `container-click-throw-drops-one-item` | unblocks | **NEWLY declared-unstable 2/2** |
| 606 | `container-click-throw-drops-the-whole-stack` | unblocks | **NEWLY declared-unstable 2/2** |
| 070 | `sand-falls-when-unsupported` | **must not move** | reproduces exactly — see below |

**070 is the control and it holds.** Its `add_entity` is
`at [1.5, 1.0, 0.5]`, `kind_id 51`, `rest dc54fa7f9dce24f3` and its two
`set_entity_data` are `rest 4a1c13d7c89129f2` — **byte-identical in all three
recordings**. A `FallingBlockEntity` draws nothing. §3 S4's table said 070 is
not an RNG problem and that is confirmed rather than assumed.

### 050 is worse than a moved field: the packet *kinds* differ

The three recordings' actor streams for 050 after the level_event, the bundle
and the block updates:

| run | `add_entity.at` | tail |
|---|---|---|
| 21:26 | `[1.5010000371078718, 1.3451466702515162, 0.33035867811299463]` | `set_entity_motion` @717 · `entity_position` @717 — **no pickup** |
| 22:49 | `[1.4345694950813481, 1.3337653178364803, 0.301286070595617]` | `take_item_entity` · `container_set_slot` · `remove_entities` @514 |
| 23:24 | `[1.7447043981040906, 1.3369571664200635, 0.5488946489436081]` | `set_entity_motion` @734 · `entity_position` @766 — **no pickup** |

The three `Level.random` draws in `Block.popResource` decide where the torch
lands; where it lands decides whether it is inside the actor's pickup box when
`setDefaultPickUpDelay`'s ten ticks expire; and that decides whether three
whole packet kinds exist. `gameplay-unstable.toml` already says exactly this
about **350** — "one run picked the item up and the other did not" — and 050's
*strict* projection is a superset of 350's *declared* one, so 050 inherits it
whole. That is the part §3 S4 missed: it read 050's `observe` list, saw block
kinds only, and did not notice that the column it was trying to move is the
column with no `observe` list at all.

**A projection change cannot rescue it.** §3 S4 proposes dropping
`add_entity.at` for item entities and `set_entity_motion.v`. Dropping fields
cannot equalise two streams that differ in which packets they contain.

**Nor can a longer window, and that is worth saying because it is the obvious
next idea.** 050 takes `scenario::default_settle`, 750 ms, and the three runs'
item events land at 514, 717, 734 and 766 ms — so the boundary sits inside the
interesting region and adds a *third* source of variance on top of the
bimodality. Widening it does not remove the bimodality:
`350-a-dropped-item-goes-into-your-inventory` runs the same rig at
`settle_ms = 3000` and is declared unstable at **25/25, N = 26**, with
`gameplay-unstable.toml` recording the cause as "one run picked the item up and
the other did not". Four times the window, same failure.

### And the field §3 S4 named is not the only one — `rest` carries a random yaw

`add_entity`'s `rest` for the same item is `43ab4a7db81697d4`,
`41e3ca7e2dd677dc`, `2f4a5a803acde955` — three runs, three values. The decoder
consumes the id, the uuid, the type, the position and the movement, so `rest`
is only `xRot`, `yRot`, `yHeadRot` and `data`. For an item those should be
four constants. They are not, and the bytecode says why:

```text
ItemEntity(EntityType, Level):
  21-36   bobOffs = this.random.nextFloat() * 3.1415927f * 2
  39-52   setYRot(this.random.nextFloat() * 360.0f)
```

**Every `ItemEntity` gets a random spawn yaw**, from its own unseeded
`RandomSource`, before the five-argument constructor has set a position. So
even with `at` and `v` dropped, every item `add_entity` in this corpus still
diverges on `rest`.

**Correction to this section, made the same night it was written.** The
paragraph above first claimed this yaw as a new finding that "settles what
`gameplay-unstable.toml` could only guess at". It is not new and that file was
not guessing: its entry for 500 has carried
`setYRot(random.nextFloat() * 360.0F)`, offsets 44-52, since **2026-08-05**,
where it is the reason a pre-registered prediction of 25/25 → 0/25 came back
25/25. Withdrawn. What is actually new here is narrower and is in our own
source rather than in the reference: `dropitem.rs` **contradicted** that entry
in a comment claiming to have read the constructor, and this server really did
announce every dropped item at yaw zero. A finding recorded in one file and
denied in another is the same defect as a stale caveat list, and it is the
reason this correction is written out instead of edited away.

It also refutes a comment in **our own source**. `dropitem.rs` said, in as many
words, that `ItemEntity`'s constructor "sets a position, an item and a velocity
and **no rotation**, so both stay at zero", and that this was "checked in the
bytecode rather than assumed". It was not. Fixed in this branch.

### The draw account in §3 S4 is short by two

§3 S4 says `ItemEntity(Level,double,double,double,ItemStack)` offsets 23-61
"draw **two more**" from the entity's own random. It draws **four**, because
the five-argument constructor's first instruction is `invokespecial` on the
two-argument one:

```text
  entity random: nextFloat  (bobOffs)
                 nextFloat  (yRot)          <- the one this account omits
                 nextDouble (delta x)
                 nextDouble (delta z)
```

`Level.random`'s three `Mth.nextDouble(-0.25, 0.25)` draws in `popResource`
happen **before** the private `popResource`'s `BLOCK_DROPS` gamerule check
(offsets 12-89 against 19-35), so a level with block drops off still advances
the level stream by three. Both facts are needed by whoever ports this and
neither is reachable from the position alone.

### What this leaves

* **`050` is a check that cannot pass on strict, and it should be recorded as
  one.** `gameplay-unstable.toml` is a declared-projection file and 050's
  declared projection is stable, so the entry does not belong there as the file
  is shaped today. The instrument item is a *strict* column in that file, which
  `ci/selfcheck-aggregate.py` already computes and prints under "strict
  reproducibility, reported and not gated".
* **605 and 606 are newly measured unstable on the gated denominator** and are
  not in the declared file. They are the same `ItemEntity` yaw. Confirming them
  at N = 26 needs a real selfcheck, not a recompare — the box's 26-run corpus
  did not survive the disk failure — so they are reported here and not added.
* **Two more came back newly unstable and are not S4's:**
  `a-player-that-leaves-the-ground-is-resynced` (2/2) and
  `closing-a-crafting-table-returns-the-grid-contents` (1/2).
* **Porting `Block.popResource` converts nothing.** It remains correct work for
  a server that should drop items, and §3 S4's bytecode account (as corrected
  above) is what to build it from — but it must not be booked against 050, and
  it carries a real regression risk that nothing in this round could measure:
  a new item entity in every cascade window leaks into the *neighbouring*
  scenario's box exactly as `compare::place`'s doc comment records 500's item
  doing (12 of 12 of 520's observations in one run, 34 of 42 of 060's in
  another).

### The projection change §3 S4 costed, built and measured — it half-works, and the half it cannot reach is the half that matters

Arguing that dropping fields cannot equalise streams holding different packets
is a tautology, so it was built instead. In a throwaway tree, never committed:
the **maximal** version of §3 S4's proposal — not just `add_entity.at` for item
entities and `set_entity_motion.v`, but the whole of `rest` on an item
`add_entity` and the whole of `set_entity_motion` — dropped in `project`'s
`map`, after `place` has read `at`, exactly where §3 S4 says it must go.
Then the same three recordings through the same comparator.

Reference `r1` (21:26), subject `r2` (22:49, **the run that picked the torch
up**) and `r3` (23:24, which did not):

| pair | comparator | declared | strict | 050 strict | 605/606 declared |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| r1↔r2 | as shipped | 77/86 | 75/86 | diverge | diverge |
| r1↔r3 | as shipped | 79/86 | 77/86 | diverge | diverge |
| r1↔r2 | + exemption | 80/86 | 75/86 | **diverge** | **match** |
| r1↔r3 | + exemption | 82/86 | **79/86** | **match** | **match** |

**Read the 050 column.** The exemption converts the pair of runs that agree
about the pickup and leaves the pair that disagrees exactly where it was. That
is not an argument that the bimodality is what remains; it is the bimodality,
isolated, with every field difference removed around it. 050 goes from
strict-unstable 2/2 to strict-unstable 1/2 and stays a check nothing can pass.

**And the version §3 S4 actually costed is a no-op.** The table above is the
*maximal* exemption. The minimal one — drop `add_entity.at` for item entities
and `set_entity_motion.v`, and nothing else, which is §3 S4's proposal word for
word — was built and measured on the same three recordings and produced output
**identical to the unmodified comparator**: declared 77/86, strict 75/86, the
same four `NEWLY UNSTABLE` names, 050 strict-unstable 2/2, 605 and 606 still
2/2. Not "a small improvement": no line of the report moved.

The reason is the yaw. `at` and `v` are *named* fields, and `rest` — the
catch-all digest of every byte the decoder did not name — still holds
`add_entity`'s three rotation bytes, one of which is a fresh
`nextFloat() * 360` per item. An exemption that leaves `rest` in place removes
nothing from an item's comparison. So the costing in §6 rank 8 was wrong twice
over: the projection change it priced does not work, and the one that partly
works still does not reach 050.

**And a result that was not predicted: 605 and 606 reproduce under it, 2/2 on
the gated denominator.** Their whole instability is the item's `add_entity`,
and they carry no pickup, so an exemption of this shape really would unblock
them — which is half of what §3 S4 claimed for it. It is *not* landed here and
the reasons are stated rather than left implicit:

* it converts nothing on its own — 605 and 606 fail today because this server
  spawns no item entity on a container throw at all, so the server work still
  has to happen behind it;
* it is a comparator change and therefore moves every scenario's denominator,
  which needs a full corpus run to gate, and this branch's one run was already
  queued against the unmodified comparator;
* the experiment hardcodes `kind_id == 71`. A landed version has to read
  `minecraft:item`'s id out of `data/vanilla/entity_types.json` rather than
  from a recording, or it silently stops firing the next time the registry
  moves.

**The negative controls held in all four configurations.**
`070-sand-falls-when-unsupported` and `010-break-block` are `match`/`match`
everywhere — 070 because its entity is `kind_id 51` and the exemption is
narrow, 010 because it drops nothing observable. `spawn-egg-makes-a-mob` and
`water-spreads` stay unstable 2/2, so the exemption did not quietly widen into
a comparator that cannot fail.

### The blast radius of the item yaw, and the Rule 7 audit that goes with it

An unreproducible field is only safe to leave alone if nothing is *passing*
over it. Counted over the full-corpus recording taken at 21:26 (`main`,
`add7297a`, declared 60/86, strict 56/86), scenarios carrying an
`add_entity` with `kind_id 71` on either side:

```
scenario                                       declared  strict   van ours
a-dropped-item-goes-into-your-inventory        absent    diverge   2   0
container-click-throw-drops-one-item           diverge   diverge   2   0
container-click-throw-drops-the-whole-stack    diverge   diverge   2   0
dropping-an-item-throws-it-on-the-floor        diverge   diverge   2   2
torch-falls-with-its-support                   match     diverge   2   0
```

**Five of 86, and they are exactly S4's five.** The single `match` is 050's
*declared* verdict, and it is a match because 050's `observe` list is three
block kinds — the field is excluded by the check, not survived by luck. So no
check in this corpus is passing over an item's random yaw, and fixing the yaw
in `dropitem.rs` could not have broken one.

It also bounds the change that landed: `dropping-an-item-throws-it-on-the-floor`
is the only scenario where **we** emit an item `add_entity` at all, and it
diverges on both denominators before and after.

### 350 is not rescued either, and its second cause is not the yaw

Under the maximal exemption `350-a-dropped-item-goes-into-your-inventory`
converts on `r1↔r3` and still diverges on `r1↔r2`, so something other than the
item's fields is moving. Unlike 050 it is **not** the pickup — 350 runs at
`settle_ms = 3000` and all three recordings picked the torch up (462, 477, 469
ms). The raw streams offer two candidates and this round did not separate them:

* **`container_set_slot`'s `state` counter reads 2, 3, 2** across the three
  runs. It is `AbstractContainerMenu`'s state id, incremented per menu sync,
  and how many syncs precede the pickup is not a property of either server.
* **In `r2` the pickup straddled a tick boundary**: `take_item_entity` at 477
  ms with `container_set_slot` and `remove_entities` at 509 ms, where `r1` and
  `r3` put all three in the same millisecond. A 32 ms split moves the `when`
  bucket of two of the three.

Both are instrument-visible and neither is behaviour. Separating them is one
`--json` diff away for whoever next needs 350, and it is written here rather
than guessed at because 350's declared entry in `gameplay-unstable.toml`
attributes the whole thing to `Block.popResource`'s position draws, and on this
evidence that is at most the larger of two causes.

### The corpus run that settles it — declared 60/86, strict 57/86, unchanged

The prediction registered in `f9ffc755` before the run: this branch converts
nothing and moves nothing, `declared 60/86, strict 57/86` before and after,
050 still strict-`diverge`. **Measured, and it is exactly that.**

`ci/t2-gameplay.sh`, corpus 86, vanilla 26.2 protocol 776, superflat, seed
20260803, sayer-desktop, 2026-08-09 02:19-03:11, on this branch at
`66f4288e` — which is `main` at `05c9a2d3` plus this branch's work and
therefore **before S3 landed**, so 57/86 rather than 58/86 is the right
denominator to read it against. S3's `080` conversion is not this branch's and
is not in this figure on either side.

```
CORPUS  declared  60/86 match   (20 diverge, 6 absent, 0 vacuous, 0 inert, 0 error)
CORPUS  strict    57/86 match   (26 diverge, 3 absent, 0 vacuous, 0 inert, 0 error)
```

| # | scenario | declared | strict | `missing_kinds` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 010 | `break-block` | match | **match** | — |
| 050 | `torch-falls-with-its-support` | match | **diverge** | — |
| 070 | `sand-falls-when-unsupported` | diverge | diverge | `add_entity` |
| 350 | `a-dropped-item-goes-into-your-inventory` | absent | diverge | `add_entity` |
| 500 | `dropping-an-item-throws-it-on-the-floor` | diverge | diverge | `set_entity_motion` |
| 605 | `container-click-throw-drops-one-item` | diverge | diverge | `add_entity` |
| 606 | `container-click-throw-drops-the-whole-stack` | diverge | diverge | `add_entity` |

**Every one of those is where it was before this branch.** `050` did not
convert, the four it was said to unblock did not move, and **`070` held** —
declared `diverge`, strict `diverge`, still `we never sent: add_entity` for
`kind_id 51`. 070 is the control that says the change did what it meant to and
nothing else, and 010 is the control that says a dig with nothing observable
to drop is still a strict match.

The run also printed the five inherited `BETTER` lines for `container-click-*`.
**Those are `main`'s conversions, not this branch's**, and they are not locked
into `gameplay-baseline.toml` here — this branch converts nothing and has no

## 12. `040`'s step attribution was a coin flip, and the window is where it lived — 2026-08-09, branch `chat-commands`

`chat-commands` gated RED on exactly one scenario and it was not a payload
failure:

```
REGRESSED  stairs-and-furnace-face-apart: was match, is now diverge
  at 4:  vanilla {"fields":{"rest":"7a679a94549f118e"},"kind":"packet:0x4A","step":3,...}
         ours    {"fields":{"rest":"7a679a94549f118e"},"kind":"packet:0x4A","step":2,...}
```

The digest agrees. S2's port is right, the generated `recipe_unlocks.json`
table is right, and the only difference is which step the packet was
attributed to.

### The hypothesis that was briefed, and why it is wrong

The brief's hypothesis was that this branch's command tree changes the
login/join sequence and so shifts a later packet's attribution by one on one
side. **It does not, and the refutation needed no new run.** Six full-corpus
recordings were already sitting on the Threadripper — `~/rustmc`,
`~/rustmc-droppickup`, `~/rustmc-integrate`, `~/rustmc-pairing`,
`~/rustmc-placesound`, `~/rustmc-recipebook` — spanning four branches, two
bases and both corpus denominators. Every one of them holds scenario 040 and
every one of them carries `packet:0x4A` with `rest = 7a679a94549f118e` on the
actor:

| recording | vanilla `at_ms` | vanilla step | ours `at_ms` | our step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rustmc` (86) | 345 | 2 | — | — |
| `rustmc-droppickup` (86) | 322 | 2 | 329 | 2 |
| `rustmc-pairing` (86) | 381 | **2** | — | — |
| `rustmc-placesound` (86) | 335 | 2 | 317 | 2 |
| `rustmc-recipebook` (86) | 333 | 2 | 330 | 2 |
| `rustmc-integrate` (88) | **383** | **3** | 329 | 2 |

§3 S2's own P1 reading adds a seventh: 339 ms, step 2.

The hold is issued at t = 321 ms, `Step::Hold` returned a 60 ms window, and so
the step 2/3 boundary sat at **381 ms** — *inside* vanilla's spread. Vanilla's
latency after a hold is 1..62 ms across those seven readings, a 61 ms range
that is one 50 ms tick of phase plus the wire. Ours is 1..15 ms, because this
server answers a `set_creative_mode_slot` on the network thread rather than
hopping to a tick. Six readings landed inside the hold's own step; the seventh
landed 2 ms past the boundary. `rustmc-pairing` at 381 ms and
`rustmc-integrate` at 383 ms are the two sides of the same coin, two runs
apart, on branches that have nothing to do with each other.

`git log main..HEAD -- ci/checks/gameplay/040-*.toml` is empty and
`crates/rustmc-server/src/recipe_book.rs` is untouched on this branch.
**040's attribution was always a coin flip with roughly a one-in-six tail, and
this branch is simply the run that lost it.**

### No server-side change could have fixed it

Vanilla's tick phase is neither observable to the client nor controlled by it.
A subject that quantised its own answers to 50 ms to "match vanilla's cadence"
would still race the reference, because the two servers' tick loops have
independent phase against the recorder's clock. The fragility is in the
window, and the window is the only place it can be removed.

### The fix, and what it is not

`Step::Hold` now returns 250 ms instead of 60 ms — which is what `place`,
`dig`, `use` and every other action step already return, so this makes `hold`
ordinary rather than special. Five ticks against a measured worst case of
62 ms, with enough margin left to survive a loaded box.

**It is not a widened projection.** Nothing is dropped, nothing is made
optional, no bound is loosened: the packet must still appear, on both sides,
at the same step, with the same digest, and 040's negative control at step 0
(`oak_stairs` unlocks nothing) is untouched. What changes is that the recorder
now listens long enough for the reference to answer inside the step that asked
the question. The trap named in §3 S1 — widening until the comparison can no
longer fail — is the opposite move; this one makes the comparison *able to
mean something*, because a check whose verdict is set by tick phase was not
measuring the server.

Cost: 146 hold steps across the corpus x 190 ms = about 28 s per recording.

### `Step::Look` had the identical defect — MEASURED AND REPAIRED, see §17

*Superseded 2026-08-09 by branch `step-look-timing`. The paragraph below is
kept as written because the reasoning in it was right and the caveat on it
was the important part; what it could not say is now measured.*

> `Step::Look` also returns 60 ms, and every argument above applies to it word
> for word: a look is answered by the reference on a tick, so anything vanilla
> says in reply is the same coin flip. It is left at 60 ms only because no
> scenario has been *measured* failing on it and this change was gated on a
> single corpus run, where two simultaneous window changes could not be told
> apart. **This is a known, unfixed, named fragility, not a clean bill of
> health.** The next agent to see a step-attribution divergence on a scenario
> whose previous step is a `look` should change the 60 to 250 and stop looking
> for a server bug.

**It has now been measured, and it never needed a new run to do it.** Nine
full-corpus vanilla recordings were already on the box, every one of them
recorded at `look = 60`, so the ensemble spans no change to the constant in
question. The reference's answer to a look arrives **32 to 192 ms** after it,
and **45 of 71 arrivals landed outside the 60 ms window** that was supposed to
contain them. `Step::Look` now returns 250 ms.

### The null, stated plainly

**The repair moves no corpus score, because a pure rotation never reaches
`observe_from = "actor"` — and every look-bearing scenario in the corpus is
`observe_from = "actor"`.** That is the finding. It is not a disappointing
side-note to the repair; it is the answer to the question §12 left open.

Three facts carry it, each measured or read from the jar rather than assumed:

* All **five** look-bearing scenarios declare `observe_from = "actor"`.
* `ChunkMap$TrackedEntity.updatePlayer` returns early on
  `player == this.entity`, so the mover is never in `seenBy` and a pure
  rotation is broadcast to observers only.
* `strict` keeps `observe_from` as well — it drops the `observe` kind list,
  not the client — so the flipping cells are outside **both** denominators,
  not merely the declared one.

**This retires the prediction in the quoted paragraph above.** It told the
next agent to expect a *divergence* on a scenario following a look, and to
change the 60 to 250 when they saw one. No such divergence can occur, so an
agent following that instruction would have waited for a signal that cannot
arrive. The fragility was real and **mis-sited: latent, not imminent.** It
becomes live the first time a look-bearing scenario observes the observer,
and seven scenarios in the corpus already declare
`observe_from = "observer"`.

**The deliverable is therefore `ci/step-window-audit.py`, not the constant.**
A one-line constant change that moves no score is not evidence it was right —
it is evidence the instrument could not see the defect, which is exactly what
was true here for the whole life of the corpus. The audit is the thing that
can see it: it measures every step boundary against the reference's own
answer latency, over recordings that already exist, in seconds, and it
refuses an ensemble that spans a change to the constant being audited. §17.

### The before-run settles it without needing the fix at all

The gating red was re-run on the **same branch with the harness unchanged**,
rebased onto `main` (`0544dfec`), 2026-08-09 03:58-04:34, Threadripper, corpus
88, seed 20260803:

```
CORPUS  declared  62/88 match   (20 diverge, 6 absent, 0 vacuous, 0 inert, 0 error)
CORPUS  strict    60/88 match   (25 diverge, 3 absent, 0 vacuous, 0 inert, 0 error)
T2-GAMEPLAY GREEN
```

**No `REGRESSED` line, and `040` came back `match` on both denominators.** The
run 28 minutes earlier, on the same corpus and the same code, reported
`declared 61/88, strict 59/88` with `REGRESSED stairs-and-furnace-face-apart`.
The whole difference between a red gate and a green one is one packet's tick
phase, and the `+1` on both denominators is 040 alone.

That is the diagnosis proved rather than argued: **a scenario whose verdict
changes between two runs of one tree is not measuring the server.** It also
means the honest "before" figure for this item is a distribution and not a
number — 61 or 62 declared, 59 or 60 strict, depending on the flip — which is
exactly the state the fix removes.

### Measured after — 2026-08-09 04:36-05:13, Threadripper, corpus 88

```
CORPUS  declared  62/88 match   (20 diverge, 6 absent, 0 vacuous, 0 inert, 0 error)
CORPUS  strict    60/88 match   (25 diverge, 3 absent, 0 vacuous, 0 inert, 0 error)
T2-GAMEPLAY GREEN
```

**Zero blast radius, and that is checked rather than asserted.** The
per-scenario verdicts of the before-run and the after-run were compared row by
row on both denominators: 88 names in each, **0 rows moved**. Nothing else in
the corpus notices a 190 ms wider hold — including the scenarios R1 says a
free-running timer decides, `490`, `520`, `560`, `561` and `601`-`608`, which
between them carry two to four holds each and were the standing risk of this
change. The same five inherited `BETTER container-click-*` lines print, and
they are still `main`'s S5 conversions and still not locked in here.

040 itself, after:

```
vanilla  step 2, at_ms 538      rest 7a679a94549f118e
ours     step 2, at_ms 516      rest 7a679a94549f118e
```

The hold is now issued at ~510 ms and the boundary sits at ~760 ms, so the
margin went from **-2 ms** to about **+220 ms** on the side that was losing.

## 13. The corpus floor — ORACLE rule 6, mechanised. 2026-08-09, branch `corpus-twin-protocol`

**The gameplay corpus had no rule 6 and the cost was three agents in one
night.** `ci/checks/gameplay-unstable.toml` was the right idea and the wrong
process: a declared list of checks the reference fails against itself,
populated ad hoc by whichever agent last tripped over an entry. §10 rediscovered
`530`, §11 rediscovered `050`, and the `chat-commands` branch rediscovered a
step boundary at 381 ms sitting inside vanilla's own 322-383 ms arrival spread
— each by hand, each from recordings that happened to be lying around, and the
third one read as a branch regression before it was understood.

The worldgen differ has had `--twin` for months and every figure in
`docs/PARITY.md` is quoted beside a floor. This is the same discipline on the
other instrument.

### The protocol

`ci/corpus-floor.sh` reads **recordings that already exist** —
`oracle-work/gameplay/vanilla.json` in any tree that has run a corpus — and
compares every pair. Seconds, not the five hours `ci/t2-gameplay-selfcheck.sh`
costs at N = 26, so a floor can be re-measured on a branch instead of once a
fortnight by whoever had the time. Three pieces are new in `oracle-runner`:

* **`project`** dumps one trace's per-scenario projection. `compare` answers
  "do these two agree"; a stability measurement asks *how many distinct things
  the reference says*, which no set of pairwise verdicts recovers. §10 needed
  that reading by hand — "four recordings, three distinct payloads".
* **`Lens::BoundaryBlind`** is the same projection with `step` and the timing
  bucket blanked. Those two fields are **ours**. A disagreement that survives
  them is vanilla saying different things; one that does not is our own step
  boundary landing inside vanilla's spread.
* **`collapse_repeats_with_times`** filters the arrival times by the same rule
  as the projection, so a millisecond figure cannot name the wrong packet on
  the thirteen checks that declare a collapse.

### How many runs, and why the number is not the answer

`p_hide(N) = 1 - alpha^(1/N)` is the largest minority rate that still produces
N identical runs more often than alpha. At alpha = 0.05: N = 2 gives 77.6%,
N = 3 gives 63.2%, **N = 6 gives 39.3%**, N = 12 gives 22.1%, N = 26 gives
10.9%, and the corpus's own smallest measured rate — `chest-opens-a-screen` at
1 in 26 — needs **N = 77** (`(1 - 1/26)^76` is 0.0508, just outside alpha),
about fifteen hours of vanilla boots.

So the honest answer is that **stability is not declarable at any N this
project can afford**, and a protocol claiming otherwise would be the defect it
exists to prevent. What is affordable is a floor with its N attached and its
resolving power printed beside it. Six is what the box had; the number that
travels with the figure is `p_hide`, not the six.

Two further choices, both of which could have been abused and are not:

* **All pairs, not run-1-against-the-rest.** "Two independent vanilla runs
  agree" is literally what rule 6 says, and all-pairs is its symmetric
  estimator with no privileged reference. 15 comparisons from 6 runs.
* **The power exponent is the run count, never the pair count.** 15 pairs from
  6 runs are not 15 independent samples, and feeding 15 into `(1-p)^C` would
  make every absence look resolved. `ci/selfcheck-aggregate.py` has always used
  `runs - 1`, so the rates already declared there stay valid arithmetic.

### What it measured — twice, on two ensembles that share nothing

**`twin-homog-20260809`** is the published one: six cold boots of the pinned
jar from ONE tree with ONE recorder, `SELFCHECK_RUNS=6
ci/t2-gameplay-selfcheck.sh`, Threadripper, 2026-08-09, corpus 88.

```text
CORPUS FLOOR  9/88 scenarios do not reproduce between two vanilla runs
              8 reference (vanilla's) + 1 silent (ours); 79 reproduced
              N = 6 recordings, 15 pairwise comparisons, p_hide 39.3%
              HOMOGENEOUS: one recorder (9fda808c) took all 6 recordings
  cross-check OK — `compare` and `project` agree on all 88 scenarios
```

**`nightly6-20260809`** is the control: six full-corpus recordings from six
*different* trees — `rustmc` / `recipebook` / `pairing` / `placesound` /
`droppickup` / `integrate` — with three *different* recorder digests, corpus
86. No recording and no recorder is shared with the first.

| scenario | homog | hetero | distinct | class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `080-spawn-egg-makes-a-mob` | 15/15 | 15/15 | 6 | reference |
| `350-a-dropped-item-goes-into-your-inventory` | 15/15 | 15/15 | 6 | reference |
| `500-dropping-an-item-throws-it-on-the-floor` | 15/15 | 15/15 | 6 | reference |
| `606-container-click-throw-drops-the-whole-stack` | 15/15 | 15/15 | 6 | reference |
| `605-container-click-throw-drops-one-item` | 14/15 | 15/15 | 5 | reference |
| `water-spreads` | 14/15 | 14/15 | 5 | reference |
| `370-swapping-to-the-offhand-shows-on-both-channels` | 8/15 | 12/15 | 2 | reference |
| `611-closing-a-crafting-table-returns-the-grid-contents` | 8/15 | 12/15 | 2 | reference |
| `540-a-player-that-leaves-the-ground-is-resynced` | 8/15 | 8/15 | 2 | **silent — ours** |

**The set is identical and the rates are not, and that is the honest shape of a
floor at N = 6.** Nine names, the same nine, the same classes, out of two
ensembles with nothing in common but the jar. What both support is that these
nine do not reproduce; what neither supports is a second decimal place, and the
two rate columns are the size of that uncertainty rather than an argument about
it. The seven names §10 and §11 found by hand are all here; `605`/`606` are
raised from 2/2 at N = 3.

`ci/t2-gameplay-selfcheck.sh`'s own aggregation over the same six recordings,
which asks the different and narrower question of whether the *declared* list
is right, run 1 against runs 2..6:

```text
6 runs, declared 8, measured 8, 79/88 reproduced, 1 did not and are ours
strict reproduced 77/88
SELFCHECK GREEN: vanilla reproduces itself everywhere it is declared to
```

### §11 IS CORRECTED ON `540`, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE POINT OF THE PROTOCOL

§11 reports `540` under "two more came back newly unstable", at 2/2 from N = 3.
It stopped short of writing an entry, and the reason it gives is that N = 3
cannot support a **rate** — not that the classification was in doubt. The only
file such a finding lands in is `ci/checks/gameplay-unstable.toml`, which means
"the reference cannot reproduce this". **It is not a fact about vanilla**, and
at N = 6 the split is visible:

```text
  r1  3   entity_position [0,0,3] rest e3e08e2b2ee20519
          entity_position [0,0,3] rest e3e07e2b2ee20366
          move_entity     d=[0,0,-12288] rest af72d84c8601b62c
  r2  3   identical to r1, byte for byte
  r3  3   identical to r1
  r4  3   identical to r1
  r5  0 observations
  r6  0 observations
```

Four runs agree to the last bit; two produced nothing whatever. A reference
that varied its behaviour would not agree *perfectly* on the runs where it
spoke, so the quantity that moved is on our side of the wire — the walk did not
happen, or the observer was not watching.

**And the same 4:2 comes out of the other ensemble with a different pair
silent.** The block above is `twin-homog-20260809`: one tree, one recorder, one
binary, six cold boots, silent in r5 and r6. `nightly6-20260809` — six trees,
three recorders — is also 8/15 with two silent, and there they are r1 and r4.
So it is neither a decoder difference nor a property of any one tree. It is a
coin this harness tosses on every run, at about one in three.

This is the same coin that killed the N = 26 selfcheck at report-5 on
2026-08-05, when `540` came back `vacuous` "the first time both sides took the
same branch". Twice now it has been read as vanilla's, because the only reading
available was pairwise and pairwise cannot see that four of six runs agree
perfectly. It is ours, and it is now a `[[harness]]` entry — a repair order
that goes red the moment all six recordings speak, rather than a fact that
would have sat in the file forever.

**The near miss is the argument for the protocol, not against §11.** N = 3
under-powering a rate is exactly the caution this project asks for, and it is
what kept the entry out. What no amount of caution supplies is the *reading*
that four runs are byte-identical and two are empty — that needs the
projections, not the verdicts, and nobody had them.

**`silent` is a measured class, not a judgement:** every run that spoke said
the byte-identical thing and the rest said nothing. It joins `boundary` as the
two classes that are ours.

**And the lens is sound in one direction only, which this section states rather than
glosses.** `boundary` is *proof* the disagreement is ours. `reference` is not
proof it is vanilla's — it proves only that it is not the boundary class. `540`
is exactly that case: the lens called it `reference` and the `silent` test
caught it. The `field` and `why` on an entry are still a human reading
bytecode, and they are what makes the claim.

### The knife edge, which is the half a flap cannot reach — and it measured §12's repair

A step boundary with less than one server tick of slack in front of it is not a
boundary, it is an unmeasured coin. That fires without any flap having
happened, which is the whole point: `040-stairs-and-furnace-face-apart` had
never flapped when §12's branch lost the toss on it.

**On the published ensemble the knife-edge set is empty across all 88
scenarios**, and 040's tightest boundary is **217 ms** — over four ticks,
between steps 1 and 2 in r3. That is the repair, measured from outside, by an
instrument that was not told it had happened.

The control ensemble is the interesting one, because it straddles the repair.
Four of its six recordings were taken with `Step::Hold` returning 60 ms and two
with 250 ms — read out of each tree's own `client.rs`, since the trees on the
box carry no `.git`. 040's `packet:0x4A` arrives at 333 / 335 / 345 / 381 / 531
/ 538 ms and the first step-3 block update at 416 / 463 / 466 / 470 / 784 /
791, and the tightest boundary is:

```text
  60 ms hold  (r1..r4)    35 ms   <- under one tick
  250 ms hold (r5, r6)   253 ms   <- five ticks
```

A margin taken across that mixture would have published a fragility the tree
had already fixed — the stale-caveat failure, manufactured by the instrument
that exists to prevent it. So a margin is measured inside the largest
one-recorder subset and the generated file records which runs and which
recorder digest it came from.

The margin is now standing in `ci/checks/gameplay-floor.toml` and adjudicated
in both directions, so the next window that gets shortened says so before it
costs a run — and §12's own closing paragraph, which had to compute
"-2 ms to about +220 ms" by hand, is the arithmetic this replaces.

### What stops this being a way to make scenarios stop failing

That is the only thing this could have been, and every clause below exists
against it. `ci/corpus-floor-falsify.sh` runs fifteen injections — against the
real measurement, and against a synthetic ensemble it writes itself so it still
runs when no recordings survive a disk failure. **15 passed, 0 failed** on both
routes, and it runs in `ci/t0.sh`.

* **A corpus verdict cannot be excused.** `ci/t2-gameplay.sh` does not read the
  declared list at all; case 11 asserts it. The floor is printed *beside* the
  score and never subtracted from it.
* **The mechanism refuses to mark a stable scenario.** `break-block` — the
  check whose unexplained `match -> diverge` between two runs of an unchanged
  pair is the reason `ci/t2-gameplay-selfcheck.sh` exists at all — put through
  the promoter and hand-declared at a maximal 15/15, against the real
  measurement:

```text
$ ci/corpus-floor.py emit floor.json --only break-block
# REFUSED  break-block: 1 distinct projection over 6 runs and 15 pairs —
#          the reference reproduced it. There is nothing to declare.
exit 2

$ ci/corpus-floor.py adjudicate floor.json --declared <with the entry pasted in>
  NO LONGER UNSTABLE  break-block — 1 distinct projection(s) in 6 runs;
    declared 15/15, so 5 independent runs miss it with probability
    (1 - 15/15)^5 = 0^5 = 0 <= alpha = 0.05; this ensemble had the power to
    see it; the entry is stale
CORPUS FLOOR FAILED
exit 1
```

  The rate is a declaration and can say anything. The distinct-projection
  count is a measurement, and for that name it is 1. Falsifier cases 4 and 5.
* **A repair order cannot be filed as a fact, or a fact as a repair order.**
  Cases 6 and 7, both directions, and a name in both tables is refused
  outright (case 8).
* **An entry with no rate fails closed** (case 9) — an exemption that switches
  itself on when its own input is missing is the defect class this whole
  protocol catalogues.
* **Removal by measurement works.** Case 2 is a real entry deleted, and it
  comes back `NEWLY UNSTABLE`; case 3 is a stale name at a rate this N could
  resolve, and it comes back `NO LONGER UNSTABLE`. A `[[harness]]` entry whose
  scenario stops flapping is `HARNESS REPAIRED` and red until deleted.
* **The evidence is generated, not written.** `ci/checks/gameplay-floor.toml`
  carries the ensemble, the sha256 of every recording, the distinct count and
  the first difference, and `adjudicate` re-derives all of it. A stale floor is
  a red (case 10).
* **An entry must be a cause and not a rate.** `class`, `measured`, `why` and
  `field`/`repair` must be present and must not still be a placeholder, in
  either table and before any arithmetic. `emit` supplies every number and
  prints those as `TODO` on purpose, so an entry pasted from it unfinished does
  not stand (case 14), and one with no `class` at all — a repair order filed as
  a fact by omission rather than by assertion — does not either (case 15).
* **The diagnostic lens is unreachable from a gate** (case 12).
* **Rule 7 on the instrument itself.** The floor comes from
  `oracle-runner project` and every gate figure from `oracle-runner compare`;
  they share `compare::project`, which is exactly the kind of "cannot drift in
  principle" that this project has been wrong about before. One pair is done
  both ways on every run and the two answers must agree over the scenarios both
  recordings contain, or the script exits 3. On r1/r2: `compare` reported 10
  non-match, the projection 8, and the two extras were precisely the two
  scenarios those recordings predate.

### The heterogeneity control, which §11 did by hand

Recordings from different trees were taken by different recorders, so a
disagreement between two of them is not automatically vanilla's. §11 handled
that by quoting "the N = 2 run over the two recordings whose `trace.rs` is
byte-identical". The ensemble now carries each run's recorder digest and every
measurement reports the largest homogeneous subset beside the full set; a flap
the homogeneous subset had the pairs to see and did not is labelled
`recorder-suspect` and is not promotable. In this ensemble the subset is three
recordings and **none of the nine is suspect**.

**It paid out on its first run, and not on the axis it was built for.** The
three recorder digests are not three decoders; they are two hold windows. Read
out of each tree's own `client.rs` — the trees on the box carry no `.git`, so
the commit could not be asked for — four of the six recordings return 60 ms
from `Step::Hold` and two return 250 ms. Nothing in the flap measurement moved,
which is the reassuring half. The *margin* moved by a factor of seven, and a
knife-edge warning taken across the mixture would have published a fragility
§12 had already repaired. See the knife-edge section above.

Two smaller holes in the same control, both found by pointing it at the input
it was about to be given rather than by reasoning about it:

* `ci/t2-gameplay-selfcheck.sh`'s recordings carry no `.prov`, because they
  never leave the tree that made them. Every one of them would have come back
  `recorder_digest = unknown` — and those recordings are the *best* input this
  instrument can have, N cold boots of one recorder. A recording under `$ROOT`
  now resolves to `$ROOT`.
* `unknown` was a **group**. Every unstamped recording would have landed in one
  homogeneous subset and the run would have printed `1 distinct recorder` while
  meaning `I could not tell` — a control that checked nothing, reported as a
  control that passed. An unidentifiable recorder is now unique to its own run,
  and the report says `NO HOMOGENEITY CONTROL` and that nothing in it is
  promotable.

### What this does not do, and what would

It does not replace `ci/t2-gameplay-selfcheck.sh` and is not meant to. That
script controls the recorder and boots the servers; this one reads whatever
recordings exist. The published measurement here is in fact *made of* that
script's recordings, which is the arrangement to keep: the expensive half is
the recording, and it should be paid for once and read by both.

What it still cannot do is resolve a rate below about **39%** at N = 6, and no
affordable N fixes that — 1 in 26 needs 77 runs. So a scenario this reports as
reproducing is not a scenario shown to be stable, and the report says so on
every run rather than leaving it to a reader.

Two things would move it, in order of value:

1. **`540`'s silence.** Two of six runs record nothing, in both ensembles, with
   a different pair silent each time. That is a coin this harness tosses at
   about one in three and nobody has looked at the mechanism. It closes when
   six recordings all speak — `ci/corpus-floor.py adjudicate` then prints
   `HARNESS REPAIRED` and stays red until the `[[harness]]` entry is deleted.
2. ~~**`Step::Look` still returns 60 ms**~~ — **CLOSED 2026-08-09, branch
   `step-look-timing`; measured, repaired to 250 ms, §17.** The margin
   instrument reported the knife-edge set as empty and that reading was
   correct and not reassuring: the set is empty because every look-bearing
   scenario observes the actor, and vanilla answers a look only to the
   observer. The boundary was being crossed on **45 of 71** arrivals the whole
   time, outside every projection where nothing could see it.
3. **`ci/t2-gameplay.sh`'s recording stamp has no `recorder=` field**, so a
   `vanilla.json` from another tree is grouped by hashing that tree's sources
   *now*. Two recordings taken from one tree at two different commits then hash
   the same and are grouped as one recorder — precisely the confound the
   grouping exists to catch, and precisely what the four-against-two hold-window
   split in `nightly6-20260809` was. The fallback is labelled `tree-now:` in the
   generated file so it cannot be mistaken for a stamp, and
   `ci/t2-gameplay-selfcheck.sh` writes a real one as of 2026-08-09. Adding the
   line to `assert_recording` is three characters of work and a fifty-minute
   corpus run to gate, so it belongs to the next branch that is running one
   anyway.
---

## 14. The container throw, and an exemption one byte wide — 2026-08-09, branch `gameplay-container-throw`

**§11 left `605` and `606` as the only reachable thing in S4's family and said
they need both halves — a comparator exemption and the server work — because
neither converts anything alone. Both are here.** What is different from the
experiment §11 costed is how narrow the exemption turned out to be able to be,
and that is the part worth reading: the projection loses **one byte, on one
entity type**, and gains three fields that were previously only inside a
digest.

### The arm, from the bytecode

`AbstractContainerMenu.doClick` dispatches on `ContainerInput` in six tests,
and the offsets §3 S4 and `click.rs` quoted for the earlier arms were from the
*inside* of the shared `PICKUP`/`QUICK_MOVE` arm rather than from the
dispatch. Corrected against `javap -p -c -constants` on the pinned jar:

```text
    0- 11  QUICK_CRAFT           -> 547
  547-572  PICKUP or QUICK_MOVE  -> 1079     (QUICK_MOVE re-tested at 664)
 1080-1083 SWAP                  -> 1385
 1386-1389 CLONE                 -> 1449
 1449-1608 THROW                 -> 1611
 1612-1615 PICKUP_ALL            -> 1873
```

The `THROW` arm:

```text
 1456-1463  if (!getCarried().isEmpty()) goto 1611      the cursor guard
 1466-1467  if (slotNum < 0) goto 1611                  SLOT_CLICKED_OUTSIDE lands here
 1483-1499  n = (button == 0) ? 1 : slot.getItem().getCount()
 1501-1509  if (!player.canDropItems()) return
 1510-1522  taken = slot.safeTake(n, Integer.MAX_VALUE, player)
 1524-1532  player.drop(taken, true)
 1533-1539  player.handleCreativeModeItemDrop(taken)
 1540-1542  if (button != 1) goto 1608
 1545-1605  while (!taken.isEmpty() && isSameItem(slot.getItem(), taken)) { ... }
 1608       goto 1873 — past the slot.setChanged() at 1071
```

Three things in that a reading of the scenario's `about` line does not give:

* **`n` is computed once, at 1491-1499, and the loop re-uses it.** A secondary
  throw of a stack of two is therefore **one** `safeTake(2, MAX)` and **one**
  item entity carrying two — not two entities of one. A transcription that
  looped `safeTake(1, MAX)` leaves the same inventory behind and puts an extra
  `add_entity` on the wire, and `606` would catch it.
* **`Player.canDropItems()` is `iconst_1; ireturn`** and `ServerPlayer` does
  not override it, so the two `return`s at 1509 and 1574 are unreachable.
  `Player.handleCreativeModeItemDrop` is a bare `return`, likewise not
  overridden. Both are omitted rather than transcribed as `if (true)`, and
  named so their absence does not read as a missed line.
* **`Player.drop(ItemStack, boolean)` is `drop(itemStack, false, bl)`**
  (offsets 0-7), so the container throw and the DROP_ITEM key reach
  `LivingEntity.drop` with the *same* two flags — `dropAround = false`,
  `traceItem = true`. They are one call and `crates/rustmc-server` now shares
  one function between them.

`Slot.safeTake` is `tryRemove` with `Optional.empty` flattened to `EMPTY`,
plus `onTake`. `Slot.onTake` is a bare `setChanged()` and is a no-op for every
slot this server has; the one override that does something is
`ResultSlot.onTake`, which consumes the crafting grid. Throwing a crafted item
straight out of a crafting table would empty the grid in vanilla and does not
here — a gap, recorded in `click.rs` rather than guessed at, and unreachable
from the corpus.

### The exemption is one byte, and naming four fields is what makes it one byte

§11's experiment dropped the whole of `rest` from an item `add_entity` (and
`at`, and the whole of `set_entity_motion`). This branch drops neither `at`
nor `rest`. Instead `tools/oracle-runner/src/trace.rs` **names** the four
values that used to be the anonymous tail —
`ClientboundAddEntityPacket.write` ends `xRot` (byte), `yRot` (byte),
`yHeadRot` (byte), `data` (varint) and then `return` — and
`compare::project`'s `map` removes exactly `y_rot`, and only when `kind_id` is
`minecraft:item` read out of `data/vanilla/entity_types.json`.

**Why that is the right width, measured rather than argued.** The FNV digest
`rest` carries is invertible over four bytes, and the four recorded tails on
the box reverse to:

| recording | tail | xRot | yRot | yHeadRot | data |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vanilla `500` 21:26 | `5644ba7bab1f265b` | 0 | **206** | 0 | 0 |
| vanilla `605` 21:26 | `df14ea7c25c7050e` | 0 | **245** | 0 | 0 |
| vanilla `606` 21:26 | `22320a7b57b73d00` | 0 | **223** | 0 | 0 |
| ours `500` 21:43 | `dc545a7f9dce13f5` | 0 | **0** | 0 | 0 |

Three of the four bytes are constant zero for every item vanilla spawns, and
the fourth is `ItemEntity(EntityType, Level)` offsets 39-52,
`setYRot(this.random.nextFloat() * 360.0F)`. Dropping `rest` would have
stopped comparing three real values in order to reach the one that cannot be
compared. (The fourth row is also the receipt for `dropitem.rs`'s yaw defect
that §11 fixed: our item really was announced at yaw zero.)

`070`'s falling block does **not** reverse over four bytes, and that is the
expected answer rather than a loose end: `FallingBlockEntity`'s
`getAddEntityData()` is a block-state id, so its `data` varint is several
bytes long. Its four values are now named too, and none of them is exempt.

**What still fails if the server is wrong.** An item's `add_entity` compares
`kind_id`, `at`, its normalised entity index, `x_rot`, `y_head_rot`, `data`,
its step and its `rest`. `at` is the field this must not lose: the 21:26/21:43
recordings put vanilla's item and ours at `[0.0, 1.3199999928474426, 0.0]`
relative, **identical to the last bit**, so it is real evidence about
`getEyeY() - 0.30000001192092896` and about the widened `1.62f`. The
prescription in `docs/WORKLIST.md`'s `gameplay-drop-pickup` cold-start block
says to drop it; that is the one instruction here that was not followed, and
the reason is in the recording.

What stops being tested is that the angle is *drawn*, and
`rustmc_server::dropitem::tests::every_dropped_item_gets_a_random_spawn_yaw`
already claims it: a hundred spawns, every yaw in `[0, 360)`, more than 90
distinct — an assertion a server writing a constant fails. That is the same
trade `569323e` made for `sound.pitch`.

### Measured — 2026-08-09, corpus 88, Threadripper

Two full corpus runs on the same box in the same morning, `ci/t2-gameplay.sh`,
vanilla 26.2 protocol 776, superflat, seed 20260803. Before is `main` at
`cd521254`, 07:40-08:17; after is this branch, 10:04-10:47.

```
before   CORPUS  declared  62/88   strict  60/88     T2-GAMEPLAY GREEN
after    CORPUS  declared  64/88   strict  60/88     T2-GAMEPLAY GREEN, no REGRESSED
```

**Row by row, 88 names on both denominators: 2 rows moved, and they are the
two.**

```
container-click-throw-drops-one-item         declared diverge -> match   strict diverge
container-click-throw-drops-the-whole-stack  declared diverge -> match   strict diverge
```

### Both halves were necessary, and that is measured rather than argued

§11 said neither half converts anything alone. The exemption's contribution is
separable for free, because a comparison of *saved* recordings costs seconds:
the after-run's own `vanilla.json` and `rustmc.json` were re-compared by a
comparator with the exemption removed and nothing else changed — patched in
`~/rustmc-throwdev`, never committed, exactly as §11's experiment was.

| | decoder | exemption | server | declared | strict | rows moved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | old | no | old | 62/88 | 60/88 | — |
| **D** | new | no | **new** | 62/88 | 60/88 | **0 of 88** vs A |
| **C** | new | **yes** | new | **64/88** | 60/88 | **2 of 88** vs D |

* **A → D is zero.** Naming four fields that were previously one digest is
  output-neutral over the whole corpus — as it must be, since both sides are
  recorded by the same decoder — and **the server work alone converts
  nothing**, which is the half §11 predicted and the half a reader would
  otherwise have to take on trust.
* **D → C is two rows.** The exemption's entire effect on 88 scenarios is the
  two scenarios it was built for. It is not a projection widened until the
  comparison stopped failing; there was nothing else in the corpus for it to
  reach.
* The other direction needs no run: before the server work this server emitted
  **no `add_entity` at all** for a container throw — the before-run reports
  `we never sent: add_entity` — and no exemption on a field can rescue a
  packet that is absent.

### What the two streams actually look like now

`605`, actor channel, declared projection, after:

```
vanilla  step5  add_entity  {"at":[0.0,1.3199999928474426,0.0],"data":0,"entity":8,
                             "kind_id":71,"rest":"cbf29ce484222325",
                             "x_rot":0,"y_head_rot":0,"y_rot":80}
ours     step5  add_entity  {"at":[0.0,1.3199999928474426,0.0],"data":0,"entity":4,
                             "kind_id":71,"rest":"cbf29ce484222325",
                             "x_rot":0,"y_head_rot":0,"y_rot":-85}
both     step5  container_set_slot  {"slot":0,"state":6,"window":12,"rest":"67414a774c80560f"}
```

Every field agrees but `y_rot`, and the raw entity id which `renumber_entities`
resolves. `rest` is `cbf29ce484222325` on both sides — the FNV basis, i.e. the
digest of an *empty* tail, which is the decoder saying it consumed the whole
body.

`606` is the same packet with `y_rot` −32 against −125, and its slot correction
is `af72e84c8601b7df` — the empty stack — where `605`'s is
`67414a774c80560f`, one stone. **That pair is the branch, pinned:** `button 0`
leaves one stone behind and `button 1` leaves none, out of the same rig, and a
server that hardcoded either answer fails the other.

### `070` held, and it held visibly

```
diverge  sand-falls-when-unsupported
         we never sent: add_entity
         vanilla {"at":[1.5,1.0,0.5],"data":118,"entity":0,"kind_id":51,
                  "rest":"cbf29ce484222325","x_rot":0,"y_head_rot":0,"y_rot":0}
```

Its `y_rot` is **still in the projection** — the exemption tests
`minecraft:item` and a falling block is `minecraft:falling_block` — so this is
the control shown rather than asserted. `data` is `118`, the block-state id
`FallingBlockEntity.getAddEntityData()` returns, which is also why 070's tail
never reversed over four bytes the way an item's does. `010-break-block` is
`match`/`match`, unmoved.

`500-dropping-an-item-throws-it-on-the-floor` moved from `diverge` to a
*different* `diverge`, exactly as §3 S4's negative control predicted: its
`add_entity` now matches, and it fails on `we never sent: set_entity_motion`
with vanilla's `v = [-0.00647012146737469, 0.0, 0.138985533785021]`.
`350` is `absent`/`diverge` and `050` is `match`/`diverge`, both unmoved.

### One claim in our own harness that this run refuted

`trace.rs`'s `add_entity` arm said, in the paragraph justifying the movement
exemption, that **"no check compares an entity's movement value against
vanilla's on the wire any more"**, because `EntityType.trackDeltas()` is false
for ten types "and the corpus's only observer of that kind is check 500, whose
entity is an ITEM, for which vanilla structurally never emits one."

The list of ten is right and the conclusion inverts it. `ITEM` is **not** one
of them, so its `trackDeltas` is true and vanilla sends `set_entity_motion` for
every dropped item — which is 500's own first difference in this very run, and
`605`/`606` carry four each. So that value *is* compared, by exactly one check,
and it is four fresh `nextFloat()` draws, which is one of the reasons 500 is
declared unstable. Corrected in place with the receipt. A structural
impossibility that the reference recording refutes on its own first line is the
same defect as a stale caveat list.

### Are they still unstable? No, on the gated denominator — measured

The brief for this item asked for this as a result in its own right, and the
answer is that the two entries `gameplay-drop-pickup` added to
`ci/checks/gameplay-unstable.toml` on 2026-08-08 are **gone, and gone for the
right reason**.

They were removed **before** the run rather than after it, which is the
convention `070`'s removal set: a run in which the exemption did not work
reports `NEWLY UNSTABLE container-click-throw-…` and exits non-zero, instead
of quietly agreeing with a file that was edited to match. It did not.

`SELFCHECK_RUNS=2 ci/t2-gameplay-selfcheck.sh` (11:17-11:53), then
`ci/selfcheck-recompare.sh` over **three** recordings, all taken by this
branch's decoder: `r1` and `r2` from that selfcheck, and `r3` = the 10:04
corpus run's own `vanilla.json`. Three cold vanilla servers, 2 pairwise
comparisons:

```
container-click-throw-drops-one-item         declared 0/2    (was 2/2)
container-click-throw-drops-the-whole-stack  declared 0/2    (was 2/2)
both, strict                                 2/2
3 runs, declared 5, measured 7, 81/88 reproduced
3 runs, strict reproduced 77/88
```

**The strict flap is not the yaw and no projection here reaches it.** It is
`set_entity_motion` and `move_entity` for the item — vanilla's four
`nextFloat()` velocity draws and then `ItemEntity.tick` moving it — which is
the same field 500 is declared for.

**Two `NEWLY UNSTABLE` names came back and neither is this item's, and they
are the same two §11 reported**: `a-player-that-leaves-the-ground-is-resynced`
at 1/2 and `closing-a-crafting-table-returns-the-grid-contents` at 1/2, where
§11 had 2/2 and 1/2 from different recordings under a different comparator on
2026-08-08. **They reproduce across two independent measurement sessions on
two days**, which is a stronger statement than either session made alone, and
it is why `ci/t2-gameplay-selfcheck.sh` exits non-zero on this branch. They
are still not absorbed: neither mechanism has been read out of the jar, and
`gameplay-unstable.toml`'s own test for absorbing rather than reporting is
that it has been. The selfcheck is not part of the gate — its own header calls
it a background instrument — so this does not gate anything, and saying so is
not the same as dismissing it.

### What this leaves

* **`ci/checks/gameplay-baseline.toml` is ratcheted for these two and for
  nothing else.** The five inherited `BETTER container-click-*` lines are
  `main`'s S5 conversions and have now gone four rounds unlocked, because each
  agent in turn has correctly declined to take credit for somebody else's
  work. The cost of that convention is now visible and is written into the
  file: five real conversions have no ratchet under them, so a regression in
  any of them prints `BETTER` on the next run and nothing at all on the run
  after.
* **The container-click family's remainder is not `doClick`.** `SWAP`
  (1080-1385), `CLONE` (1386-1449), `PICKUP_ALL` (1612-1873) and `QUICK_CRAFT`
  (0-547) are still declined, and 604/607/608/611 are what would measure them
  — but `605`/`606`'s *strict* residual is `ItemEntity.tick`, which is the
  same wall `500` and `350` are behind and is much larger than any remaining
  arm.

  > **⚠ THE SENTENCE ABOVE IS WRONG ON BOTH HALVES AND §16 MEASURES IT.**
  > `605`/`606`'s strict residual is **not** `ItemEntity.tick`: the first
  > divergence between two vanilla runs is the item's *spawn* velocity on
  > `set_entity_motion`, drawn from four `nextFloat()`s in
  > `LivingEntity.createItemStackToDrop` before the entity has ticked at all.
  > And it is not a wall that can be climbed from here — vanilla fails it
  > against itself on **15 of 15 pairs**, so no repair to any tick can convert
  > these two under strict. The attribution was an inference from a shape, and
  > ORACLE rule 9 is the rule it broke.
* **`Slot.onTake` is a gap with a name.** It is a bare `setChanged()` for
  every slot this server has, except `ResultSlot`, which consumes the crafting
