**Rank 0 is not padding and it is not a conversion.** It converts nothing, and
it is above the three because without it none of the three can be shown to work
without a fifty-minute corpus run under a box-wide lock. §19.4 is what it is.

### 19.4 The coverage hole — and the briefed version of it is wrong in the one way that matters

The finding carried into this work was: *`Session` has 12 `Option` fields and 5
test construction sites, and `placement`, `shapes`, `sound_types`, `ticks`,
`placed_by` and `recipes` are `None` at all five.*

**Audited against the tree. The twelve is right, the five is wrong, and the
correction is the whole point:**

> `Session` has **12** `Option` fields and **six** construction sites — **five
> in tests and one in production**. The six named fields are `None` at all five
> test sites and `Some(…)` at the production site.

The production site is
`crates/rustmc-server/src/status.rs::serve_connection` (`:989`, function at
`:627`, reached from `status::listen` at `:322`), and it loads every table from
`data/vanilla/*.json`, logging a named console line on each failure rather than
defaulting silently. There is no builder and no `Default` — deliberately, per
the comments at `world_send.rs::water_at` (`:8214`) and `plugin_tick_lock.rs:227`.

**Why the missing sixth site changes the finding rather than decorating it.**
"`None` at all five" invites the reading that six mechanisms are unwired. They
are not: production wires all six. What is true, and is the actual hole, is
narrower and sharper:

**No test in this repository ever constructs a `Session` with those six tables
present.** So the *connection-loop wiring* — the step between a table that
works and a table that is reached — is witnessed by nothing but
`ci/t2-gameplay.sh`, which costs fifty minutes and serialises on a box-wide
lock. Every one of the six callees is well covered on its own:

| field | module | `#[test]` fns |
|---|---|---|
| `placement` | `crate::placement` | 29 |
| `shapes` | `crate::shapes` | 31 |
| `ticks` | `crate::ticks` | 9 |
| `recipes` | `crate::recipes` | 9 |
| `placed_by` | `crate::placedby` | 6 |
| `sound_types` | `crate::sound_types` | **3** |

**This is not six untested mechanisms. It is one untested joint, six times
over** — and that is a much cheaper thing to fix and a much easier thing to
miss.

**`sound_types` is the sharp one, and it is sharp for a stated reason.** It
gates S3, which §3 records as `PORTED` and converted; `080` is `match`/`match`
today. So a row this document calls closed is held up by a joint no test
crosses, behind the module with the fewest tests of the six. `IcebergFeature`
was green for a week on exactly this shape. **`PORTED` is a claim about the
port. `witnessed` is a different claim and this document should stop letting
the first imply the second.**

**The item, and it is rank 0 above.** One construction site — a sixth `Session`
literal, in a test, with those six fields `Some(…)` — exercising one placement
that needs `placement` + `placed_by` + `shapes`, one scheduled tick, one
recipe, and one sound. **Its negative control is built into its shape:** flip
any one of the six back to `None` and the assertion for that mechanism must go
red. A test that stays green with a field set to `None` has not crossed the
joint it exists to cross, and that is the failure to look for, because it is
the failure the other five sites already have.

### 19.5 `607` is a check that cannot fail, and it is passing

`607-container-click-pickup-all-gathers-matching-stacks` reads **`match` on
both denominators**, 7 observations against 7, at `7ccad044`.

`crates/rustmc-server/src/click.rs` documents `PICKUP_ALL` (1612-1873) and
`QUICK_CRAFT` (0-547) as **not implemented** (`:734`, `:740`), and
`click.rs::do_click` (`:1395`) declines every input it has not transcribed —
`if input != ContainerInput::Pickup { return false; }`.

**Read out of the recording rather than argued.** 607's final step *is* the
measured `pickup_all` click, and at that step:

```text
vanilla   step 6   no container_set_slot, no container_set_content, no open_screen
ours      step 6   no container_set_slot, no container_set_content, no open_screen
```

Both sides silent, so the projections agree and the verdict is `match`. Vanilla
is silent because the client's own prediction was correct and needed no
correction. **We are silent because we declined the click and never noticed our
menu had diverged from the client's** — and the scenario ends there, so nothing
ever asks either server what it thinks the slot holds.

The check's own `about` line names the falsification it believes it has: *"a
server that maps every `ContainerInput` it does not specifically implement onto
a plain `PICKUP` would instead merge the cursor's stone INTO the clicked slot"*.
That falsification is real and this server does not commit it — it declines
rather than approximating, which `click.rs` argues for explicitly and correctly.
**The check has no falsification for the case that actually obtains: a server
that does nothing at all.**

This is the AGENT-BRIEF lens applied and paying out: *a gate reading zero is not
evidence until you prove the gated code runs.* 607 is one of the 64, and it is
one of the 64 for a reason that is not about this server's containers.

**What would fix it, in one line of the check and no code:** a seventh step
that reads the slot back — any click whose correction depends on what
`PICKUP_ALL` did. Vanilla answers from a swept menu, we answer from an
unswept one, and the check goes red until the arm exists. **Do not edit the
scenario on the strength of this paragraph** — §-hazard: a scenario that looks
wrong is a finding with its own row, which is what this is. It is filed here,
for the owner of the corpus.

**And the count this changes.** 607 is not moved out of the 64 by this section,
because moving it would be a verdict change and this branch takes no verdict.
What is recorded is that **the 64 contains one row whose `match` is not
evidence about this server**, and that `604` — the `SWAP` arm — is therefore
the container family's only honest open row.

### 19.6 What is unknown, and what is a null

**Marked `unknown`, deliberately, rather than guessed:**

* **`400`, `440` and `410`'s mechanisms.** All three diverge on content; 400
  and 440 report no missing kinds at all and 410 reports
  `section_blocks_update`. §4 files 400 under sounds and 440 under
  neighbour-update counts, and **both attributions are now doubtful** — 400 has
  no missing `sound` and the neighbour updater is measured sound. Nothing here
  replaces them, and a `--json` diff is one command for whoever takes them.
* **Whether `430`'s `block_event` is reachable at all before its placement
  defect is fixed.** Its first divergence is `note_block[instrument=basedrum]`
  against vanilla's `harp`, which is upstream of every packet the §4 row names.
  The order of those two repairs is not established here.
* **The tip that produced the 64/60 figure.** The recording's `.prov` carries
  `commit=unknown`. Five independent runs agree on the number, which is why it
  is quoted; the SHA behind it is not recoverable from the artefact and is
  recorded as unknown rather than inferred from the tree's mtime.
* **A `block_event` of ours that nothing currently grades.** In 607's actor
  stream at `7ccad044` we emit
  `block_event {"at":[33,0,0],"b0":1,"b1":255,"block":201}` where vanilla emits
  nothing. `[33,0,0]` is one `WORKSPACE_SPACING` away — the *next workspace's*
  chest — and `b1: 255` is a viewer count no chest has. It costs no verdict
  today because `compare::near` bounds it out on its own `at` field, which is
  the bound working as designed. **Whether it is a stale `Openers` entry
  surviving a workspace change or a signed-byte defect in the count is not
  established here**, and it is recorded because a packet that is only harmless
  by virtue of a spatial filter is one filter change away from being counted.

**Nulls, so nobody re-runs them:**

* **Do not look for a remaining instrument-defect scenario.** There is none.
  R1-R3 landed in `20b41e34`, `4eb45f51` closed `540`'s comparator silence, and
  every one of the 28 remaining rows is either ours or below its own floor.
  Measured, not argued.
* **Do not re-derive §7's four `kind = "corpus"` figures.** Their artefacts
  are destroyed — no gameplay recording before 2026-08-08 21:26 survives on the
  box, and `oracle-work/gameplay/subset/vanilla.json` exists in zero trees — and
  the schema they were written for was never adopted.
* **Do not open an item on `power.rs::update_neighbors_at`.** It is a faithful
  port and none of the four scenarios §4 files against it is blocked on it.
* **Do not price the other 182 use sounds off 420.** The extract's `sound`
  column is a boolean; each is a hand-ported constant.
* **Do not read `080`'s `match` as entity-movement coverage.** §5's caveat is
  untouched by S3's conversion and is restated there.

## 20. The corpus scored 0 of 88 against us because nobody had measured its denominator — 2026-08-10, branch `corpus-coverage-audit`

**Both of this project's instruments ran out of resolving power in the same
night, and the gameplay one ran out from the top: every scenario the corpus can
decide, we already pass.** An instrument that cannot fail is not evidence, so
the item was to grow the corpus — and the first thing the item needed was a
number nobody had: how big the gap is.

**Two floors are live in this tree on two ensembles, and the published one is
the older.** The brief quoted *7 of 88 … 7 vanilla's own nondeterminism, 0
ours* and cited `docs/PARITY.md` §4.1. §4.1 says **9 of 88**, and both numbers
are correct:

```text
  9 of 88   twin-homog-20260809   published in PARITY.md 4.1 and ci/figures.toml
  7 of 88   yrot6-20260809        16.2, after 605/606 were retired on recordings
                                  that carry y_rot; the two-name difference is
                                  exactly those two checks
```

So the brief's *number* is the current best one and its *citation* is to the
section that still carries the superseded one. This is the standing rule about
floors doing its job rather than a mistake by anybody: **a floor belongs to the
ensemble that produced it**, so the two do not merge and the newer does not
silently replace the older in a section that names a different ensemble. It is
recorded here because the next agent to read §4.1 will meet the same trap, and
because it sharpens what this item must not do — see 20.6. The substance the
item rests on is untouched at either value: **0 of them are ours.**

### 20.1 The set difference, and why it needed a new instrument

`ci/corpus-coverage.py` counts our own sets against each other: which decoder
kinds a check projects, which `Step` verbs nothing uses. That is the inside
question, and it cannot answer the outside one. Every set it reads comes from
our own sources, so a mechanism vanilla has and this harness has never heard of
is invisible to it — and **100% of a small set reads exactly like 100% of a
large one**.

`ci/corpus-surface.py` supplies the denominator, from the pinned jar's own
`GameProtocols` registration order. Measured 2026-08-10, sayer-desktop, 88
checks, 17 vanilla recordings (`~/rustmc*/oracle-work/gameplay/vanilla.json`):

```text
  clientbound   141  in the protocol            GameProtocols, pinned jar
                 57  named in rustmc-proto
                 12  dropped as housekeeping    trace::is_housekeeping
                 38  legible                    a trace::decode arm
                 91  opaque                     packet:0xNN, body digested
                 30  observed by >= 1 check
                 36  EMITTED by vanilla during a corpus run
                 28  emitted AND observed       <- the corpus's real reach

  serverbound    69  in the protocol
                 27  named in rustmc-proto
                 21  client.rs can send         <- the harness's vocabulary

  behaviour     use_without_item  11 of 39 implementations, 13 of 184 blocks
                set_placed_by      4 of  7 implementations,  6 of  50 blocks
                the corpus holds 39 distinct items, and has no verb that
                places a block it does not hold
```

**The `emitted` column is a measurement and it is the one that matters.** Two
thirds of the clientbound surface is unreachable from a creative superflat with
two players and no mobs, so counting boss-bar, map and resource-pack packets as
gaps is arithmetic rather than information. What vanilla *did* send while the
88 ran is not a judgement about reachability; it is the reachable set, sampled
seventeen times.

Three tiers of blindness, and they do not have the same fix. **housekeeping**
is dropped before any decoder sees it. **opaque** is not invisible at all — the
whole body is digested into `rest`, so a check naming the kind compares every
byte, more strictly than a decoded packet, at the cost of a failure that says
only "these bytes differ". **unobserved** is legible with no check projecting
it, which is a decoder arm that reads as coverage and is not.

**Count implementations, not runtime classes.** `use_without_item.json` records
each block's runtime class, so `TrappedChestBlock`, `CopperChestBlock` and
`WeatheringCopperChestBlock` are three rows and none of them declares
`useWithoutItem`; all three inherit `ChestBlock`'s, which `090` covers. Same for
`SmokerBlock` and `BlastFurnaceBlock` under `AbstractFurnaceBlock`,
`DropperBlock` under `DispenserBlock`, `WeatheringCopperDoorBlock` under
`DoorBlock`. The naive count is 12 of 47 and the honest one is 11 of 39; the
eight that vanish are inheritance, not coverage, and the naive number would have
sent somebody to write three chest checks that exercise one method. The script
walks the superclass chain in the jar and collapses the column itself.

**It is also a proto drift detector.** Every id it derives is cross-checked
against `rustmc-proto`'s own constants and it exits 2 on disagreement. There is
none: all 57 clientbound and 27 serverbound constants we carry agree with the
jar on the number. One alias is declared — our `BUNDLE_DELIMITER` is the jar's
`BUNDLE`, id 0.

### 20.2 Stability can be pre-screened for free, and it already ruled a candidate out

A new check must read stably across independent vanilla runs or be declared
unstable with its rate. The instrument for that was
`ci/t2-gameplay-selfcheck.sh` at about five hours of vanilla boots — which is
what makes the discipline tempting to skip.

For the cheapest class of new coverage the cost is avoidable entirely. **A kind
vanilla already emits inside a window the corpus already records has already
been sampled once per recording on the box.** `ci/corpus-surface.py
--recordings` reports, per kind and per scenario, the count in every run and
whether it moved. Over 17 recordings:

```text
  packet:0x60  SET_CURSOR_ITEM       stable in all 8 scenarios, n = 17 each
  packet:0x00  BUNDLE                stable in all 8 scenarios, n = 17 each
  packet:0x13  CONTAINER_SET_DATA    stable at 4, n = 17
  packet:0x6C  SET_PLAYER_INVENTORY  stable at 1, n = 17
  update_attributes                  stable at 2 in both scenarios, n = 17
  packet:0x8A  WAYPOINT              stable in 4 rigs; absent from 16 of 17
                                     runs of one; 362/364/366 in water-spreads
  rotate_head                        stable at 1..2 in three rigs; present in
                                     9/17, 2/17 and 16/17 runs of three others
  move_entity_rot                    stable in two rigs; 1..2 in a third
```

**So "observe `rotate_head`" is not a property of the kind — it is a property
of how much the rig moves**, and the pre-screen says so before a check exists
to ask. That is the candidate it removed from the top of the ranking below.

It is a pre-screen and not a substitute: it can only speak about rigs that
already exist. A new rig still has to be recorded.

### 20.3 The ranking

Ordered by behaviour reached per unit of cost. "Cheap" here has a hard
constraint that is not obvious and that this directory's README pays for
already: **`ServerPlayer.nextContainerCounter` and
`AbstractContainerMenu.incrementStateId` are per-player and live as long as the
session**, and one actor plays every scenario in a corpus run. A new check that
opens a menu, or writes the actor's own inventory, is a statement about every
check before it. Appending at the end of corpus order costs nothing; inserting
anywhere else re-numbers the four existing menu checks and breaks them.

**Tier 1 — free coverage. No new verb, no new substrate, and the stability is
already measured.** Four packet types vanilla emits inside windows the corpus
already records, stable across 17 runs, observed by no check:

| | packet | seen | why it is worth having |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `0x60 SET_CURSOR_ITEM` | 221, 8 scenarios | 34 checks drive `container_click` and none can tell a server that moved the item into the cursor from one that moved it nowhere. This is the load-bearing half of ORACLE rule 27: the harness claims an empty carried item so that silence cannot be read as agreement, and `set_cursor_item` is the exact channel that corrects the claim |
| 2 | `0x13 CONTAINER_SET_DATA` | 68, 1 scenario | furnace data slots — the only channel by which a container's non-slot state reaches a client |
| 3 | `0x6C SET_PLAYER_INVENTORY` | 17, 1 scenario | single-slot player inventory updates |
| 4 | `0x00 BUNDLE` | 544, 8 scenarios | the delimiter. Observing it measures *grouping* — which packets vanilla considers one atomic client-side update — and nothing else in the corpus can see that at all |

**Tier 2 — `useWithoutItem`, 28 uncovered implementations.** Ranked by blocks
reached, with the menu-counter constraint applied:

```text
  FlowerPotBlock          39 blocks   no menu   writes the actor's inventory
  ShulkerBoxBlock         17 blocks   MENU      + a block_event animation
  FenceGateBlock          12 blocks   no menu   reads a second input (facing)
  AnvilBlock               3 blocks   MENU
  DispenserBlock           2 blocks   MENU      covers DropperBlock too
  DaylightDetectorBlock    1 block    no menu   moves a redstone signal
  RedStoneWireBlock        1 block    no menu   cross/dot toggle
  ComposterBlock           1 block    no menu   level-sensitive
  DragonEggBlock           1 block    no menu   TELEPORTS AT RANDOM — unstable
                                                by construction; a check for it
                                                must declare its rate or not
                                                exist
  16 further menu openers  1 block ea MENU      barrel, ender chest, hopper,
                                                loom, beacon, brewing stand,
                                                enchanting table, cartography
                                                table, grindstone, lectern,
                                                smithing table, stonecutter,
                                                crafter, ...
  LightBlock, MovingPistonBlock, CaveVinesBlock, CaveVinesPlantBlock,
  SweetBerryBushBlock, RespawnAnchorBlock       substrate-limited, see 20.5
```

The sixteen menu openers are **one indivisible item in corpus order**, for the
reason the README already gives about the four that exist: each carries a window
id that is a statement about the ones before it, so no subset of them can reach
`match`.

**Tier 3 — the harness's own vocabulary. 48 of 69 serverbound packets cannot be
sent at all**, and each is a harness item rather than a scenario item. Ranked:

| | packet | what it unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `0x1A INTERACT` | right-clicking an **entity**. The corpus has zero entity-interaction coverage and no way to write any. Biggest single hole on this axis |
| 2 | `0x0D CLIENT_TICK_END` | a real client sends it every tick. The harness never does, so **every movement measurement in this corpus was taken under a condition no real client produces** — that is a premise worth falsifying before it is worth fixing |
| 3 | `0x1F MOVE_PLAYER_POS_ROT` | the harness only ever sends pos and rot separately; a real client sends the combined packet, so our combined handler is exercised by nothing |
| 4 | `0x2A PLAYER_COMMAND` | sprint start/stop, leave bed, elytra |
| 5 | `0x24/0x25 PICK_ITEM_FROM_BLOCK/_ENTITY` | middle-click, and the only path that synthesises an item from a block state |
| 6 | `0x11 CONTAINER_BUTTON_CLICK`, `0x27 PLACE_RECIPE`, `0x14 CONTAINER_SLOT_STATE_CHANGED` | the rest of the container protocol |
| 7 | `0x06/0x08/0x0A` chat ack, signed command, session update | chat security, a whole subsystem |

**Tier 4 — two projections with nothing behind them.** `damage_event` and
`set_health` are each named by two checks and occur **0 times in all 17
recordings**. Creative players are invulnerable, so `550`/`551` project four
kinds and are decided by one (`sound`). This is not a defect and `550`'s own
header is honest about the reach question — but the two dead kinds are exactly
the shape this project keeps paying for, and the fix is a survival target, not
a wider projection.

### 20.4 What was written, and what it measured

Five checks, at the top of tiers 1 and 2, chosen so that four of the five need
no menu and none of them re-numbers an existing check:

```text
  700  a-fence-gate-opens-when-right-clicked
  701  a-fence-gate-opened-from-behind-turns-to-face-you
  710  a-daylight-detector-inverts-when-right-clicked
  720  a-container-click-puts-the-item-in-your-cursor
  790  a-flower-pot-empties-when-right-clicked
```

**Every mechanic was read out of the jar before its rig was written, and two of
the five would have been dead without it.** `FlowerPotBlock.useWithoutItem`
opens `if (isEmpty()) return CONSUME` and puts nothing on the wire, so `790`
has to pot a dandelion in setup or the gate refuses it as `inert` —
the potting is load-bearing, not decoration. And
`DaylightDetectorBlock.useWithoutItem` falls through to a **menu** unless
`player.mayBuild()`; the creative substrate satisfies it, so `710` reaches the
`INVERTED` cycle rather than the branch that would have entangled it with the
window counter.

**`700` and `701` are a pair and the second is not optional.**
`FenceGateBlock.useWithoutItem` reads two inputs — the current `open`, and the
player's facing, which it can use to *rewrite* `FACING`, something a door never
does. `700` opens the gate from the front, where that branch is not taken. A
server implementing the method as "cycle OPEN" passes it for ever. `701` is the
same rig with the player turned round, differing in exactly the property being
claimed.

**`790` is numbered last and must stay last.** `Player.addItem` writes the
actor's own inventory, and the actor is one connection that plays the whole
corpus, so both the window-0 state-id chain and the free-slot layout are
inherited by every check after it. A new check must not be numbered above 790
without moving it. *(2026-08-11: the state-id chain half no longer reaches the
comparison — it is rebased — so the rule now rests on the free-slot layout
alone. It rests on it perfectly well, and the rule is unchanged in force.)*

### 20.5 What is unreachable with the current harness, and what it would need

Ranked by what the fix costs, because these are the items whose natural next
move — "write the scenario" — produces a check that measures nothing and is
refused by the gate. Three of them are already written down in
`ci/checks/gameplay/README.md`; they are gathered here with the rest so that
the ranking above has an explicit complement rather than an implied one.

| gap | what it costs | needs |
|---|---|---|
| **survival mining** — `Step::FinishDig` is declared, correctly numbered, and used by **zero** checks | one packet's whole handler | a **survival player**. In creative, `handleBlockBreakAction` takes the `instabuild` branch and returns before `destroyPos` is assigned, so `STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK` never matches and the only packet on the wire is the ack the action itself forced — the definition of `inert`. Measured by `ci/finish-dig-probe.sh`, not reasoned. **Substrate change, not a check** |
| **damage** — `damage_event` and `set_health` are projected by two checks and occur 0 times in 17 recordings | two dead kinds in a live projection | a **non-creative target**. Creative players are invulnerable. Same substrate item as the row above, and doing one does the other |
| **entity interaction** — `0x1A INTERACT` cannot be sent | the whole right-click-an-entity surface, currently zero | a **harness verb**. `client.rs` has `ATTACK` and not `INTERACT`; they are separate packets in 26.2 |
| **`SmallDripleafBlock` / `TallSeagrassBlock`** — the last two `setPlacedBy` second-block classes with no placement check | 2 of 7 implementations | **somewhere to stand that superflat does not provide.** `SUPPORTS_SMALL_DRIPLEAF` is exactly `clay` and `moss_block` from the jar's own datapack, and the other arm wants water above; the seagrass wants water. **Substrate, not a check** |
| **client tick accounting** — `0x0D CLIENT_TICK_END` is sent by every real client every tick and by this harness never | unknown, and that is the point | nothing but the packet. **This is the cheapest item on the list and the one with the largest unknown behind it**: every movement measurement in this corpus was taken under a condition no real client produces. Falsify before repairing — it may change nothing |
| **combined movement** — `0x1F MOVE_PLAYER_POS_ROT` | our combined handler is exercised by nothing | a harness verb; `walk` and `look` already exist and send the two halves separately |
| **the 105 clientbound types vanilla never emitted here** | most of the protocol | **not verbs — worlds.** Mobs, weather, other dimensions, advancements, boss bars, maps, trades. A creative superflat with two players cannot reach them and no scenario will change that |

### 20.6 The floor has to be re-measured, and it must not be quoted beside the old one

`ci/checks/gameplay-floor.toml` carries `scenarios = 88` and
`ci/figures.toml` registers `9 of 88 … twin-homog-20260809`. Adding checks
makes neither wrong and neither stale in the dangerous sense — **a floor
belongs to the corpus and the ensemble that produced it**, which is the same
rule that keeps 9 and 7 both true above. What it does make is *inapplicable*:
`ci/corpus-floor-report.py` prints `STALE DENOMINATOR: measured over 88
scenarios, this run has N` and withdraws nothing else, which is the correct
behaviour and is warn-only by design.

So the corpus this branch ends with needs its own floor, measured on its own
ensemble, registered with its ensemble id, its recorder count, its N and its
`p_hide` — and reported **beside** the old rather than as a movement from it.
`9 -> N` would be a difference between two corpora and two ensembles quoted as
if it were a change in vanilla's reproducibility.

`ci/check-figures.py` will not catch that: its `corpus-floor` kind requires
`ensemble`, `runs`, `pairs`, `scenarios` and `alpha` to be *present*, and does
not compare `scenarios` against the tree. The mechanical check is not the
check here, exactly as the brief's hazard list says of `quotable`.

### 20.7 The five verdicts, and the two that had to be broken before they could be believed

`ci/t2-gameplay-subset.sh` over the five, 2026-08-10, sayer-desktop,
`~/rustmc-coverage`, vanilla 26.2 protocol 776 on `:25896` against ours on
`:25897`. **A subset verdict is not a baseline entry** — `ci/checks/gameplay-baseline.toml`
may only be written from the full gate, per that file's own closing paragraph —
so these are stated here as what the checks read, and the baseline is written
from the full-corpus run in §20.8.

```text
  700  a-fence-gate-opens-when-right-clicked                match
  701  a-fence-gate-opened-from-behind-turns-to-face-you     diverge
  710  a-daylight-detector-inverts-when-right-clicked        diverge
  720  a-container-click-puts-the-item-in-your-cursor        match
  790  a-flower-pot-empties-when-right-clicked               diverge
```

**Three diverges, and all three are ours.** They are named and ranked below and
deliberately **not repaired on this branch**: a repair here would move the
number the branch exists to measure, and the coverage figure would stop being
reproducible from its own commit.

* **`701` — `use_without_item` is a state→state table and cannot express a
  player-dependent rewrite.** This is the structural one and it is worth more
  than the check. There is no hand-written `FenceGateBlock` port anywhere in
  `crates/rustmc-server`; the toggle comes from
  `crate::useblock::use_without_item`, whose whole signature is
  `(table, state) -> Used` and which resolves one `HashMap` lookup keyed on the
  full state string. The player is not an argument and is not in scope. So the
  `facing` rewrite at the jar's offset 65 — `setValue(FACING, player.getDirection())`
  when the current `FACING` is its opposite — is not merely unimplemented, it is
  **inexpressible in the table's shape**, and what the generated
  `data/vanilla/use_without_item.json` holds instead is the probe player's own
  direction baked in as a constant. That constant is `south`, which is why
  `700` (player facing south) reads `match` on the very branch that `701`
  (player turned round) reads `diverge` on. `700` and `701` were written as a
  pair for exactly this and the pair paid out on its first run.
* **`710` — the daylight detector's `INVERTED` cycle is absent.** Vanilla
  answers `inverted=true`, we answer `inverted=false`: the state is unchanged
  and we emit one fewer `block_update` than vanilla (2 against 3).
* **`790` — the flower pot's `useWithoutItem` is absent entirely.** We send no
  `block_update` for the pot at all, only the `block_changed_ack` the action
  itself forced, and no `container_set_slot` for the plant handed back. This is
  the largest of the three by blocks reached: 39 blocks share that one
  implementation.

**The two `match`es were then shown able to go red, because on this project a
green is not evidence until the code it gates has been proved to run.** Both
breaks were applied at once — the rigs are independent scenarios, so neither
can mask the other — measured in one subset run, and reverted in the same turn;
the tree is clean of them and `git diff` was empty before the next run started.

| check | break | verdict under the break |
|---|---|---|
| `700` | `crate::useblock::use_without_item` returns `Used::Pass` for any state containing `fence_gate` | `diverge` — vanilla `open=true`, ours `open=false` |
| `720` | the `Reply::SetCursor` arm of `world_send::send_reply` drops its send | `diverge` — `we never sent: packet:0x60`; vanilla has it at index 3, "ours said nothing more" |

Both moved. Neither check is measuring its instrument.

**And the falsification turned up a defect the verdict could not: `700`'s
`about` line overclaimed, and `701` carries the same limitation.** Both declare
`observe_from = "actor"` and list `"sound"` in `observe`, and `700`'s prose
said it "plays the wood type's own open sound". It cannot see that sound. In
the recording vanilla emits exactly one for the scenario and it is
`who = "observer"`; the jar says why, at offset 162 of
`FenceGateBlock.useWithoutItem`:

```text
   117: aload_2                     // Level
   118: aload         4             // the acting Player  <- THE EXCLUDED ENTITY
   120: aload_3                     // BlockPos
   130: WoodType.fenceGateOpen()  / 140: fenceGateClose()
   143: getstatic SoundSource.BLOCKS
   162: invokevirtual Level.playSound:(Entity;BlockPos;SoundEvent;SoundSource;FF)V
```

`Level.playSound`'s leading `Entity` is the player **excluded** from the
broadcast — the same local slot 4 that `getDirection()` reads at offset 45. So
a correct server sends the actor nothing here, and an actor projection can
never see the sound in either direction. What the kind still buys is one-sided
and real: a port that broadcast the sound to everybody, which is what you write
if you miss the excluded-entity argument, is caught here and nowhere else in
the corpus. Both files now say that instead, and `700`'s `about` was rewritten
to claim the silence rather than the sound. **The harness's
`we never sent: sound` advisory prints on any diverge in these two and does not
mean vanilla sent one to the actor** — it did not, and reading that line as a
missing observation is how this would have been "fixed" in the wrong direction.

No verdict moved as a result: the kind fires on neither side, so the
falsification above stands over the corrected files unchanged.

### 20.8 The full-corpus run, and the five baseline entries it earns

`./ci/t2-gameplay.sh`, 2026-08-11, Threadripper, `~/rustmc-cov3`, branch
`corpus-coverage-audit` rebased onto `main` `1f8f3813`. Vanilla 26.2 protocol
776 on `:26612` against ours on `:26613`, superflat, fresh world, corpus lock
taken as role `run` and uncontended. Projection `proj:b385528330fee646`.

```text
  CORPUS  declared  71/92 match   (16 diverge, 5 absent, 0 vacuous, 0 inert, 0 error)
  CORPUS  strict    67/92 match   (23 diverge,  2 absent, 0 vacuous, 0 inert, 0 error)
```

**The denominator is 92, and every document that led here said 93.** This
branch was written against 88 and adds five checks; between then and now
`water-spreads-cascade` took `main` from 88 to 87 by parking
`160-water-spreads.toml` in `ci/checks/gameplay/open/`, where nothing loads
it. 87 + 5 = 92. The number is not inferred: the harness prints
`recording 92 scenario(s)` at the top of its own recording pass, and `diff` of
this tree's check directory against `~/rustmc-cov2`'s 93 returns exactly one
line, `160-water-spreads.toml`. **The 93 in the brief, in §20.6 above and in
this branch's first cold start is wrong wherever it appears**, and the
arithmetic that produced it was right on the day it was done.

The five verdicts, from the full gate and therefore admissible as baseline
entries in a way §20.7's subset run was not:

```text
  700  a-fence-gate-opens-when-right-clicked                match
  701  a-fence-gate-opened-from-behind-turns-to-face-you     diverge
  710  a-daylight-detector-inverts-when-right-clicked        diverge
  720  a-container-click-puts-the-item-in-your-cursor        match
  790  a-flower-pot-empties-when-right-clicked               diverge
```

Before those lines were written the gate refused all five by name —
`not in the baseline — a new check must record what it currently does` — and
that refusal is the instrument working, not a failure to be routed around.

**`720` changed verdict against §20.7 and against the reading this branch had
recorded but never committed, and the explanation attached to that reading
does not survive.** §20.7's subset said `match`; an uncommitted full-corpus
reading taken on the 93-corpus under the older projection
`proj:58380c9e4cbeae81` said `diverge`, and attributed it to window-id drift
inherited from `closing-a-crafting-table-returns-the-grid-contents` — vanilla
opening at `window = 17` where we opened at `18`, with every later menu opener
riding the same drift. On this tree `720` reads `match` with **no first
difference at all under either lens**, and the crafting table's own surviving
diverge carries `window = 0` on both sides and is a missing observation
(`ours said nothing more` at slot 36, state 6), not a window-id offset. The
chain the attribution rested on is not present, so it cannot be carried
forward even as a caveat.
`609-sneaking-with-a-block-in-hand-does-not-open-a-chest` went
`diverge -> match` in `main` between the two runs and is the obvious suspect;
it is named here as a suspect and not as a measurement, because nothing in
this run attributes the change and rule 9 says a reading of code does not move
one.

**What is written for a check that is strict-unstable, and why that is a
distinction rather than an exemption.** The N = 6 selfcheck reports strict
reproducibility separately from declared, and on this corpus eleven names do
not reproduce strictly. It does not follow that eleven checks get a weaker
baseline entry, because **`[expect]` was never a strict claim**:
`compare::Baseline::check` reads `Outcome::verdict`, the declared reading, and
never reads `Outcome::strict`, which the type documents as "the same
comparison with nothing projected away". So all 92 checks — the eleven
included — carry an ordinary `[expect]` line written from the declared reading
of this run, and **nothing is exempted from the ratchet**.

The difference between that and an exemption list is falsifiability, and it is
mechanised rather than argued. The declared projection is **one comparator
applied to all 92 scenarios**, and it has an identity: change what it drops
and `proj:b385528330fee646` changes with it, `ci/corpus-floor-report.py`
prints `STALE PROJECTION`, and the floor stops being quotable beside the score
until somebody re-measures. An exemption list has no such handle — it is
per-name, it suppresses the comparison for exactly the scenario somebody found
inconvenient, and nothing downstream can tell an exempted scenario from a
passing one. That is this project's recurring defect stated precisely: a check
that cannot fail and is passing. The strict reading is not discarded either;
it is printed beside the declared one on every run (`67/92` above), and where
a name's instability is vanilla's own it is registered in
`ci/checks/gameplay-unstable.toml` with its ensemble, its N and its measured
rate. Eleven names are **measured**, not waived.

92 checks and *this* tree's binary. That is what makes the result a
measurement at the current size under the current comparator rather than a
carried-over number: `--checks` decides which checks are projected, so the
93-scenario recordings yield 92 apiece, `PROJECTED 92/92` on every one of the

`proj:b385528330fee646`, re-derived from the binary rather than declared.

`ci/checks/gameplay-floor.toml` is re-stamped from it and both standing

`proj:58380c9e4cbeae81` against a run comparing under
`proj:b385528330fee646`. **The floor is 7 of 92 and it is quotable beside

them vanilla's own, none of them ours.

> above is superseded, not wrong — it was a correct reading of these same six
> recordings under the projection one commit earlier.

**It must not be read as unchanged from the 7 of 88 it replaces, and the equal
digit is a coincidence that hides a swap.** The superseded reading, quoted
here in full so that it has somewhere to live that a re-stamp cannot
overwrite:

    floor = 7 of 88, ensemble gpfloors-homog6-20260809, projection proj:58380c9e4cbeae81

That was a correct measurement of a different corpus on a different ensemble
under a different comparator, and it is kept beside this one rather than
deleted, in the convention `corpus-floor-n6` already set. One name leaves and
one arrives:

* **`water-spreads` leaves**, because it is parked and this corpus does not
  contain it. `ci/corpus-floor.py adjudicate` says `NOT IN THIS RUN — no
  usable pair in this ensemble`, which is the honest reading: it was not
  measured stable, it was not measured.
* **`a-flower-pot-empties-when-right-clicked` arrives**, `NEWLY UNSTABLE`, 9/15
  pairs, 2 distinct projections, class `reference`. It is one of the five
  checks this branch added, so the corpus grew and its floor grew with it —
  which is the expected direction and worth stating plainly, because a
  coverage item that added five checks and moved no floor would be the more
  suspicious result.

The other five re-measure with the same names and different rates, because
this is a different ensemble at the same N: `a-player-that-leaves-the-ground-is-resynced`
8 -> 5 flaps, `closing-a-crafting-table-returns-the-grid-contents` 11 -> 9
(3 -> 2 distinct), `swapping-to-the-offhand-shows-on-both-channels` 11 -> 9
(3 -> 2 distinct). Same N, same 15 pairs, genuinely different sample — the
rule that a floor belongs to the pair of runs that produced it, restated for
the corpus.

**`710` was going to be declared unstable and the corpus ensemble refuted it,
which is the sharper half of this section.** §20.7's `ci/subset-stability.sh`
run measured `a-daylight-detector-inverts-when-right-clicked` at 5/15 pairs,
class `reference`, and a `[[unstable]]` entry for it was drafted from that
rate. On the corpus ensemble it is 0/15 pairs, 1 distinct projection, class
`stable`. The refutation is admissible rather than merely contradictory
because **this ensemble had the power to see the claimed rate**: at 5/15,
missing it in all fifteen pairs has probability `(1 - 5/15)^15 = 0.0023`,
comfortably under `alpha = 0.05`, so `ci/corpus-floor.py adjudicate` would
have printed `NO LONGER UNSTABLE ... the entry is stale` and gone red on the
entry the day it landed. The entry is therefore not written, and the reason is
recorded in `ci/checks/gameplay-unstable.toml` where the next person to
re-measure a 5/15 rate will find it.

The mechanism is consistent with both readings rather than with either alone.
`DaylightDetectorBlock.useWithoutItem` recomputes `POWER` from the level's sky
light, a function of the world's day/night tick; the subset ran five checks
alone within seconds of a cold boot, where boot jitter in that phase is the
whole signal, while the corpus reaches the scenario some sixty scenarios in
along a path identical in all six runs. **A subset is not the corpus, and this
branch already knew that about verdicts** — `ci/checks/gameplay-baseline.toml`
has said since 2026-08-03 that a baseline entry may only be written from the
full gate, after three `animate` entries were written from a subset and the
full corpus called them `vacuous`. The same rule holds for *stability* and had
not been written down anywhere. It is now.

**`608-container-click-with-an-out-of-range-slot-changes-nothing` is not this
branch's and was not touched.** For the record, because its bucket was asked
about: it reads `match` on this run, and on this ensemble it does not flap at
all — 0/15 pairs, 1 distinct projection, class `stable`. This ensemble is
single-recorder, so it cannot reproduce the recorder-suspect split that put
`608` in that bucket (5/15 overall against 0/10 inside the homogeneous
subset); measuring 0/15 across a homogeneous 15 is the same reading that split
was pointing at, and corroborates the recorder-suspect diagnosis rather than
disturbing it.

**A green figures gate found nothing here, and that is a defect in the ledger
rather than a clean bill.** `ci/figures.toml`'s `corpus-floor-n6-gpfloors`
adjudicates the superseded 7-of-88 against `ci/checks/gameplay-floor.toml`
with `artefact_claim = "floor = 7"`. Re-stamping that file to a different
measurement of a different corpus under a different comparator left the string
`floor = 7` in it, so `ci/check-figures.py` went on reporting `FIGURES GREEN`
over a figure whose artefact had been replaced wholesale. A claim string that
is one digit cannot distinguish two sevens. The entry is repointed at this
section, whose text names the ensemble and the projection alongside the
number, and the successor is registered with the ensemble id as its claim
string so that the next re-measure moves it.

## 21. The corpus has a denominator now, and it is not 92 — 2026-08-11, branch `corpus-vanilla-coverage`

**`72/92 declared, 68/92 strict, floor 4/92` is a score against a set we
wrote.** Ninety-two is the number of scenarios that exist, not a measure of
vanilla, so the corpus score says how much of our own corpus we pass and
nothing whatever about how much of vanilla the corpus even looks at. Asked
"how far from finished", the honest answer until this section was *there is no
denominator*. §20 measured the gap between our checks and our harness's own
vocabulary; this measures the gap between the corpus and **vanilla**.

`ci/vanilla-reach-census.py` produces the denominators, `ci/jarcallgraph.py`
is the substrate it needs, and the one rule both obey is that **not one
denominator may come from our tree**. Everything below is read out of the
pinned `server-26.2.jar` — Mojang's `generated/reports/`, `GameProtocols`' own
packet registration, and the profiler section names Mojang compiled into the
server's tick path. Our side supplies numerators only, and every numerator is
a measurement off the six vanilla recordings of ensemble
`coverage92-selfcheck-n6-20260811`, not a reading of our source. **No vanilla
was booted and the box-wide corpus lock was never taken**: the whole item is
static, over the jar and recordings already on disk.

### 21.1 Three units, and the answer moves 55x between them

```text
  UNIT 1  clientbound play packet types     (GameProtocols, 141 registered)
             36  vanilla EMITTED during the corpus
             31  named by >= 1 check          31/141 = 21.99%
             29  emitted AND named            29/36  = 80.56%

  UNIT 2  vanilla's own per-tick sections   (the jar's profiler, 120 named)
              8  PROVABLY OFF        a game rule this harness sets shuts them
             33  PROVABLY UNPOPULATED per-mob, for a mob no recording held
             79  unclassified — UNKNOWN, not covered
                                             41/120 = 34.17% provably never run

  UNIT 3  vanilla's registries            (reports/registries.json)
             sound_event         29 / 1968     1.47%
             block               43 / 1196     3.60%
             block_state         87 / 32366    0.27%
             entity_type          4 / 158      2.53%
             block_entity_type    1 / 49       2.04%
             menu                 3 / 25      12.00%
             item                 — / 1537     not legible (see 21.4)
```

Line those up as "what fraction of vanilla does the corpus touch" and the
answer is **80.56%, 21.99%, 65.83%, 3.60%, 2.53% or 1.47%** depending only on
which unit you pick — a **55x** spread between the most and least flattering,
over one corpus, one ensemble and one jar. **The spread is the finding.** A
single number here is a choice of unit, and the choice is worth more than the
measurement; this is the same defect as §15's "a floor is a number under a
comparator", moved from the comparator to the denominator.

The two ends are worth naming, because both will be quoted:

* **80.56%** is the flattering end and it is not wrong, it is narrow. Its
  denominator is *what the corpus provoked*, so a mechanic the corpus cannot
  reach is scored as absent from the denominator rather than as a gap. It
  measures how well the checks read what the harness already makes vanilla
  say.
* **1.47%** is the brutal end and it is not the right headline either. 1,968
  sound events are not 1,968 systems. A registry entry is an enumeration, not
  a mechanism.

The unit closest to "systems" is UNIT 2, whose denominator is Mojang's own
decomposition of a server tick, and it reads **34.17% provably dead, 65.83%
unknown** — where *unknown* means unknown and must never be read as covered.

### 21.2 Two sharp negatives, and both are the harness's own doing

The 41 provably-dead tick sections are not an estimate. They come from two
rules that can each be checked against the jar:

* **A game rule the harness sets shuts the section.** `ci/t2-gameplay.sh` sends
  `advance_time false`, `spawn_mobs false`, `random_tick_speed 0`,
  `advance_weather false` and boots with `difficulty=peaceful`,
  `spawn-monsters=false`, `generate-structures=false`, `gamemode=creative`,
  `spawn-radius=0`, `--level-type flat --radius 2`. The script **parses those
  out of `ci/t2-gameplay.sh` rather than copying them**, because a table of
  "the gamerules we set" maintained beside the script that sets them is a
  caveat list and this project's caveat lists lag their code. Eight sections
  fall: `naturalSpawnCount`, `filteringSpawningChunks`,
  `shuffleSpawningChunks`, `tickSpawningChunks`, `spawner`, `customSpawners`,
  `randomTick`, `weather`.
* **A per-mob section for a mob no recording ever held.** `add_entity` is
  recorded for every entity that enters view, so absence over six runs is
  evidence rather than silence — and the corpus's worlds contained exactly
  four entity types in every run: `player`, `item`, `falling_block`, `pig`.
  Thirty-three `<mob>Brain` / `<mob>ActivityUpdate` sections therefore never
  ran: allay, axolotl, breeze, camel, copper golem, creaking, frog, goat,
  happy ghast, hoglin, nautilus, piglin, piglin brute, sniffer, tadpole,
  villager, warden, zoglin, zombie nautilus and armadillo.

**The gate verifier carries both controls.** `thunder` is asserted as gated by
`advance_weather` and the verifier *refuses it* — its real gate is the weather
*state*, which `advance_weather=false` freezes, not the rule field — so it
stands in the output as the positive control that this check can fail. And the
run dies outright if `advance_weather` ever verifies for `randomTick`. What
the verifier is: a staleness guard that catches a renamed game rule (26.2
renamed all four, and a stale id silently cost this project a whole corpus once)
and a section that has moved. What it is not: a data-flow proof. It cannot
separate two rules read in the same method, and `ServerChunkCache.tickChunks`
reads both `SPAWN_MOBS` and `RANDOM_TICK_SPEED`.

### 21.3 The instrument that collapsed, kept rather than deleted

The obvious way to join the two halves is a call graph: for each tick section,
which clientbound packets can its code construct, and were any of them ever
emitted? It is built, it runs in seven seconds, and **it has essentially no
resolving power.** `invokevirtual` on `Entity`/`Level`/`BlockState` resolves to
every subtype, vanilla's tick graph is one giant strongly-connected component,
and a section as specific as `wardenBrain` comes out able to reach **51 of the
139** packet types whose class is resolvable. It calls **6** sections dark
where the two sharp rules above call **41**, and its darks are
`look`, `players`, `send chunks`, `timeSync`, `weather`, `world border`.

It is printed under `--weak`, with the collapse stated, rather than deleted.
An instrument that could not separate is a finding about the instrument, and
the next agent should not spend a turn rebuilding it. The over-approximation
is the *safe* direction — an over-approximated edge set can only add packets
to a section's reachable set, so a section it calls dark is dark under any
sound resolution — which is exactly why the tier it produces is small and
useless: soundness bought at the cost of every bit of discrimination.

### 21.4 What this number cannot say

**It cannot say that a system is tested.** Every positive tier here is
*presence*, not coverage. A packet observed once is not a mechanic checked; a
block seen change state once is not a block whose behaviour is compared; and
UNIT 2's 79 `unclassified` sections are 79 sections about which this census
has **no information at all** — not 79 sections that ran. The only claims that
are load-bearing are the negatives, and they are negatives about *this
harness's world*, not about vanilla: the corpus does not run mob AI because
the harness spawns no mobs, not because mob AI is small.

**It cannot price its own blind spot.** Every numerator is measured through
one recorder, on one world — creative superflat, radius 2, peaceful, no
structures — over one ensemble of six runs. A mechanism the harness has no
verb for is invisible to all three units simultaneously, and nothing here
bounds how much that is. That is the opposite of conservative: the units agree
with each other partly because they share a blind spot.

**Items are not censused at all, and that is the recorder, not vanilla.** An
`ItemStack` lives inside the undecoded tail that `trace::observe` digests into
`rest`, so the 1,537-entry item registry has no honest numerator from these
recordings. A zero there would be a reading of the instrument.

**Twelve clientbound packet types are excluded from `emitted` by
construction.** `trace::is_housekeeping` drops keep-alives, chunk payloads,
light, tab list and advancements before any decoder sees them, and vanilla
certainly sends most of them every run. Counting them as never-emitted
understates `emitted` by up to twelve, which is the conservative direction;
`--housekeeping-emitted` prints the other bound and it moves **29/36 = 80.56%
to 29/48 = 60.44%**. Both are printed rather than one being chosen.

**And it has no floor, in the sense every other figure in this repository
carries one.** A floor is the disagreement between two innocent runs of the
same thing, and there is nothing here for two runs to disagree about: this is
a census, not a comparison, so ORACLE rule 6 has no premise to fire on. **That
costs the claim the thing a floor buys — a statement of resolving power — and
it must not be silently omitted.** What stands in its place is a
reproducibility reading, printed by the script: the same census run over each
recording separately gives

```text
  sound_event         per-run 27..28    pooled 29
  block               per-run 43..43    pooled 43
  entity_type         per-run  4..4     pooled  4
  block_entity_type   per-run  1..1     pooled  1
  menu                per-run  3..3     pooled  3
```

so only `sound_event` moves between runs of the same vanilla, by one or two
out of 1,968. Quote that spread beside any number from this section. A census
with no spread stated is a census asserting a stability it did not measure.

### 21.5 Ranked — the largest systems with zero corpus evidence

The point of a denominator is a work order, and a coverage figure that does not
produce one is decoration. Ranked by the size of the vanilla surface the corpus
has **no evidence** of touching, with the unit each surface is enumerated in by
Mojang printed beside it, because these numbers are not comparable across rows:

```text
   1. sound emission              1939 sound events        one packet type, an enormous vocabulary
   2. block behaviour             1153 blocks              32,279 block states unseen
   3. mob AI and mob behaviour     154 entity types        33 per-mob tick sections provably never ran
   4. block entities                48 block entity types  only `sign` has ever been observed
   5. container menus               22 menu types          3 of 25 ever opened
   6. natural + custom spawning      6 tick sections       gamerule spawn_mobs=false
   7. random ticks, growth, fire     1 tick section        gamerule random_tick_speed=0
   8. weather and thunder            1 tick section        gamerule advance_weather=false
```

Read as work, that ranking says something the corpus score cannot: **rows 6-8
are the cheapest and they are cheap because they are ours.** Six of the eight
provably-dead gate closures are game rules `ci/t2-gameplay.sh` sets, so
spawning, random ticks and weather are one harness change away from being
*reachable* — not one scenario away from being covered, but reachable, which
is the precondition nothing else on the list has. Rows 1-5 need new verbs and
new scenarios, and row 2 is where the leverage is: `use_without_item` scores
**16 of 184 blocks but 14 of 39 classes** (`ci/corpus-surface.py`), so the
block surface is 4x better covered by class than by block and the honest
ranking of row 2 depends on which of those two a reader means.

**What closes this item is not a bigger number here.** It is the next
measurement being taken *with* a denominator: any claim of the form "the
corpus covers X" that does not name its unit is now refusable on sight.

#### 21.5.1 Two corrections to the ranking above — 2026-08-19, branch `mobs-tick-surface`

The ranking is left as written because it was right about what it could see,
and because two later branches tested it. Both results belong beside it.

**Rows 6 and 8 are not cheap; they are dead ends, and both were tried.**
`origin/corpus-dark-systems` built exactly the "one harness change" this
section calls for — `[[gamerule]]`, applied down the reference's console fifo
for a scenario's own measured window — and pushed all three rows through it on
2026-08-12:

```text
   7. random ticks       OBSERVABLE   780, 0/15 pairs at N = 6
   8. weather            NULL         reference projection empty in all 6 runs
   6. natural spawning   NULL         15/15 pairs, 6 distinct projections
```

So of the three "cheapest" rows, **one became a check and two are nulls with
numbers.** Weather's floor is arithmetic: `RAIN_DELAY` is
`UniformInt.of(12000, 180000)`, a ten-minute minimum against an eight-second
window, redrawn per boot. Spawning's is the spawn yaw — `EntityType.create`
offset 103, `getRandom().nextFloat() * 360.0f`, unseeded — and §94.9 measures
what that costs: `080`'s projection agrees with itself in **0 of 120** pairs,
and there is no subset a spawn check could project and reach `match` on
without a field-exemption decision this project has twice declined to make.
**Reachable was the precondition, and it was not sufficient.** Do not re-rank
rows 6 and 8 as cheap on the strength of this section alone.

**Row 3's denominator is 158, not 154.** Two independent derivations from the
pinned jar agree — `origin/entity-parity`'s reach census and
`ci/mob-tick-census.py`'s reading of `EntityTypes`' static initialiser — and
the sharper split is the one that says what the row is about: **86 of the 158
are in a spawning category, 72 are `MobCategory.MISC`, and the jar declares
114 subtypes of `Mob`.** The hierarchy behind row 3 is 115 classes declaring
**3,870 methods**. This server declares three `EntityKind` constants and none
of them is a mob, so row 3's true state is not "no corpus evidence" but
"nothing to have evidence of".

## 22. `use_without_item.json` is 122/184 a reading of the probe and 17/184 wrong — 2026-08-11, branch `golden-probe-audit`

`data/vanilla/use_without_item.json` is generated by `UseGolden`, which drives
**one** player at every block state and writes down what happened. That player
has a facing, a position, a game mode, an ability set and a permission set, and
`BlockState.useWithoutItem(level, player, hit)` is handed it. Where a block
reads it, the recorded row is a fact about **that player**, and the table states
it as a fact about the block.

Nothing could ever have contradicted it. The only thing that could is a probe in
another stance, and no such probe existed — which is this project's signature
defect (§20, ORACLE rule 7) in a new place: a golden table that cannot fail.

**This table has exactly one source and its neighbours feed nothing.** Every
cell comes from `BlockState.useWithoutItem`; `useItemOn` and `use` generate no
golden table in this tree — `ci/gen-gameplay-tables.sh` derives its list from
the `data/vanilla/…` literals the crates open, and there is no `use_item_on`
among them. So the audit below is complete for the table and says nothing about
the blocks whose `useItemOn` swallows an empty-handed click before
`useWithoutItem` is ever reached. That is a coverage question and a separate
one.

> **BOTH HALVES OF THAT PARAGRAPH ARE NOW OUT OF DATE, AND IT IS LEFT STANDING
> BECAUSE IT WAS TRUE WHEN THE AUDIT WAS TAKEN.** §23 built
> `data/vanilla/use_item_on.json` the same day, and branch
> `gameplay-790-flower-pot` (2026-08-12) made `crate::useitemon` its first
> consumer — so a `data/vanilla/use_item_on.json` literal *is* now among the
> ones the crates open, the derived required set went 19 tables to 20, and
> every tree regenerates it. Read the paragraph as a statement about the
> `use_without_item.json` audit's own scope, which is unchanged, and not as a
> statement about what this tree generates.

### The two numbers, and why neither is the answer alone

**`ci/probe-reads.py` — static, over the pinned jar.** For every class in the
table, the declaring `useWithoutItem`, and every method within the block
packages the player can be carried to; a **read** is an invoke on an
entity-typed receiver whose descriptor returns something other than `void`, so
a value comes back into the block's own frame and can steer a branch, an
argument or the return. `Player.awardStat` is not a read at all.

    122 of 184 rows, 34 of 47 block classes

**`UseGolden.STANCES` — empirical, eleven further players.** A third sweep
beside the eight seeds (`random`) and the two faces (`faceSensitive`): every
state is re-probed under every stance and `probeDependent` is set when the
recorded row moved.

    17 of 184 rows move when the player does

The static number is an upper bound and must not be quoted as a defect count.
The sweep is exact for the axes it turns and blind to the ones it does not. Both
are published because the *pair* is the finding: 105 rows read the probe and do
not move, and knowing which is which is the difference between a list to port
and a list to worry about.

The containment is the consistency check between them, and it holds: every one
of the 17 is inside the 122. `ci/probe-reads.py` prints a refusal if it ever
stops holding, because a moved row the static walk called clean would mean the
walk has a hole.

### The 17

| class | rows | axis |
|---|---|---|
| `FenceGateBlock` | 12 | `facing_east`, `facing_north`, `facing_west`, `adjacent_south` |
| `ComparatorBlock` | 1 | `no_build` |
| `DaylightDetectorBlock` | 1 | `no_build` |
| `RedStoneWireBlock` | 1 | `no_build` |
| `RepeaterBlock` | 1 | `no_build` |
| `LightBlock` | 1 | `game_master` |

`FenceGateBlock` is the shape of it. It compares `player.getDirection()` against
its own `FACING` and flips the gate to face the player when they disagree —
`aload 4; invokevirtual Player.getDirection` at offset 43, feeding the
`if_acmpne` at 62. The table holds 384 fence-gate rows of which exactly 48
change `facing`, and all 48 are `north -> south`, because the probe faced south.
It is right for one quarter of the circle.

### The other 105, decomposed, because "probe-dependent" is not "wrong"

| | rows | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| every cell a refusal | 38 | all `FlowerPotBlock`. Constant because **unmeasured**, not because it is constant |
| some cells refusals | 16 | `BedBlock`, whose `startSleepInBed` reaches `environmentAttributes` |
| fully measured and constant | 51 | 48 of them containers: `Player.openMenu` returns an `OptionalInt` that is `pop`ped at **25 of its 26 call sites in the jar**, the exception being `Merchant.openTradingScreen`, which is on no block's use path |

The 38 are the honest bad news of this section. `FlowerPotBlock` reads
`Player.addItem`, and the stance that would turn that axis — `full_inventory` —
is itself unavailable, because `new ItemStack` needs item components and
`Bootstrap.bootStrap()` does not bind them. It is reported in
`probeStancesUnavailable` and pinned in the allowlist rather than degraded to a
silent copy of `base`, which would have reported the axis clean on no evidence.

### The probe's facing was a die roll, and its range hid it

`LivingEntity`'s constructor is `setYRot(random.nextFloat() * 6.2831855f)` — a
uniform [0,1) times **2 pi**, into a field measured in **degrees**. A freshly
constructed player therefore faces somewhere in [0, 6.283) degrees; two runs
here gave 0.522 and 5.360.

Every one of those values is inside `Direction.fromYRot`'s southern bucket,
[-45, 45). So `player.getDirection()` has always answered `SOUTH`, the table has
always been stable, and the randomness was invisible **because its range was
narrower than its only consumer's resolution**. Had that constant ever been
`360.0f`, `use_without_item.json` would have churned nondeterministically and
looked like a broken dumper. `base` now pins `yRot` to 0 and throws if a
constructed player faces anything but `SOUTH`, which is what makes `base` a
stated stance rather than a lucky one.

The two-run `cmp` in `ci/use-golden.sh` is what caught it, the moment the dumper
started writing the number down. An instrument that records its own conditions
is how a condition nobody set becomes visible.

### The refusal, which is worth more than the audit

`ci/use-golden.sh` will not write the table when `ci/checks/use-probe-dependent.toml`
does not already know what the sweep found: a new probe-dependent block, a
listed block whose axes changed (compared for **equality**, not membership — a
block wrong in a new way is as red as a new block), a listed block that stopped
being probe-dependent, a stance count that shrank, or a stance that became
unavailable. The last two matter most: a sweep that quietly stops sweeping
reports every row as constant, which is this check wearing its own uniform.

`ci/check-use-probe-falsify.sh` runs six injections against a synthetic fixture
with green controls either side and one against the real table — 9 of 9, under a
second, no jar and no box — and is gated in `ci/t0.sh`. A refusal that lives
inside a generator most trees never invoke is a refusal nobody would notice had
stopped working.

**What this section does not do is fix anything.** No block was converted. The
17 are a list for whoever ports them; converting on suspicion is what the
measurement exists to make unnecessary.

## 23. The other half of the right-click: `use_item_on.json`, and the two bindings it needed — 2026-08-12, branch `golden-useitemon-axis`

`§22` audited `use_without_item.json` and found that 17 of its 184 rows are a
reading of the probe. This section is about a different problem with the same
table: **there was never a second one.**

`ServerPlayerGameMode.useItemOn` offers a right-click to the block **twice**,
and `use_without_item.json` is the second offer. From the pinned jar:

```text
  145      r  = state.useItemOn(stack, level, player, hand, hit)
  152-157  if r.consumesAction()                    -> r
  179-187  if r instanceof TryEmptyHandInteraction && hand == MAIN_HAND
  196          r2 = state.useWithoutItem(level, player, hit)
```

Offset 196 only runs when offset 145 returned `TRY_WITH_EMPTY_HAND`. A `PASS`
or a `FAIL` from offset 145 **skips it**, so the existing table cannot say
whether the rule it describes ran at all. Two branches arrived at that gap
independently — `gameplay-block-interactions` found that porting
`FlowerPotBlock.useWithoutItem` converts nothing because the *potting* is a
`useItemOn`, and `gameplay-item-use-group` pinned the ordering and stopped at
the same wall. `data/vanilla/use_item_on.json` is offset 145.

### Two bindings, both of which every earlier measurement went through

Neither is a nicety; the table cannot exist without the first and is silently
blind without the second.

* **Item components.** `new ItemStack(item)` reads
  `Holder.Reference.components()`, which `Bootstrap.bootStrap()` alone does not
  bind. `use_without_item.json` carried exactly **39** `Components not bound
  yet` refusals for it — 38 `FlowerPotBlock` and, the one nobody had named,
  **`minecraft:composter`**. `UseGolden.bindItemComponents` runs the
  initializers a real server runs from
  `ReloadableServerResources.updateComponentsAndStaticRegistryTags`: **141
  pending registries apply and all 1,537 items mint a stack.** The 39 refusals
  are now measured rows — `potted_dandelion` writes `flower_pot` with flags 3,
  `composter[level=8]` writes `composter[level=0]` — and `use_without_item.json`
  went from 199 refusals to **160**.
* **Item tags.** `ItemStack.is(TagKey)` answers *false* for every item in the
  game with no tags bound, and does not throw. Five of the twenty-five
  `useItemOn` classes read the whole of their rule through one:
  `NoteBlock` (`NOTE_BLOCK_TOP_INSTRUMENTS`), `ChiseledBookShelfBlock`
  (`BOOKSHELF_BOOKS`), `CakeBlock` (`CANDLES`), `LecternBlock`
  (`LECTERN_BOOKS`) and the two copper golem statues (`AXES`). Bound from
  Mojang's own datagen output, **recursively** — item tags nest, and a flat
  `Files.list` misses every nested one.

**The prediction that came with the first of those was refuted.** §22 named
binding components as "the single highest-value follow-up" on the grounds that
it "would turn that axis" — `full_inventory`, unavailable because it needed an
`ItemStack`. It is available now and **it turns nothing**: the sweep still finds
17 of 184, the same 17, and `ci/checks/use-probe-dependent.toml` needed only its
`unavailable` list emptied. What binding bought was the 39 refusals, not the
axis. The blind spot was real and the thing behind it was not.

### The table

| | |
|---|---|
| blocks whose class overrides `useItemOn` | **163**, over 25 classes and 4,537 states |
| blocks skipped, and falsified rather than assumed | **1,033**, against the whole item registry |
| item axis | **1,537** — the registry, not a list |
| grid | 92,101,730 probes, plus 1,587,721 for the control |
| run time | ~95 s, twice, `cmp`-identical |

The item axis is the whole registry and not a hand-written set of "relevant"
items, because a hand-written set is the thing that silently loses a member —
this project has already paid for one, `copper_hoe` being the seventh hoe where
six were expected. Each state is emitted as one `default` cell plus the
exceptions grouped by identical answer, which is a **compression of the
measurement and not a sampling of it**: 1,537 × 4,537 pairs are probed and
15,070 of them differ from their state's default.

The blocks that are *not* probed are decided by walking each block's superclass
chain for a declared `useItemOn` — the same walk virtual dispatch performs, so
exact rather than approximate. That is still a decision about what not to
measure, so the dumper probes all 1,033 of them against all 1,537 items and
**throws** if any answers anything but `TRY_WITH_EMPTY_HAND`.

### What it covers, and the refusal that says so

* **94 blocks fully measured**, including all **39** `FlowerPotBlock` blocks —
  which is the whole of the blocker two branches named. `flower_pot` + each of
  38 pottable items writes the matching `potted_*` at its own position with
  flags 3, returns `SUCCESS` and consumes the item; every `potted_*` answers
  `CONSUME` without writing. `790`'s conversion is a table lookup now.
* **68 blocks refuse on every state**, and the refusal is new and deliberate.
  Ten classes open with
  `if (!(level.getBlockEntity(pos) instanceof XBlockEntity)) return PASS`, and
  this harness's world is a `HashMap` of block states holding no block
  entities. Recording that `PASS` would be this project's signature defect with
  no disguise — a plausible empty answer for a method the harness does not
  model, stated as a fact about the block. **The ask itself is the refusal.**
* **1 block is `random`** and keeps no cells: `minecraft:composter`, whose fill
  is a draw from the level RNG. Found by the seed sweep, which runs only on the
  pairs whose probe touched `TableLevel.getRandom` — exact, not a screen.

### The probe columns, and what `useItemOn` reads that `useWithoutItem` does not

**25 of 163 rows move when the player does**, on **two** axes, and both are
axes the other table never turned:

* **`game_master`, 8 rows** — cake, four cauldrons, flower pot, composter,
  respawn anchor. `ItemStack.consume(n, player)` is
  `if (entity == null || !entity.hasInfiniteMaterials()) shrink(n)` and
  `Player.hasInfiniteMaterials` is `abilities.instabuild`, so **every rule that
  takes the item off you reads the probe's ability set.** What moves is
  `stackAfter`, not the block write. These are not a debt to be ported away:
  the row is right for a survival player and right for a creative one, and the
  consumer has to read `instabuild` itself.
* **`no_build`, 17 rows** — every candle. `CandleBlock.useItemOn` is
  `if (stack.isEmpty() && player.getAbilities().mayBuild && LIT) { extinguish(); }`.
  That one is a real debt.

Two further axes exist here that `use_without_item.json` has no column for, both
because `useItemOn` is handed things `useWithoutItem` is not:

* **face — 18 blocks.** `NoteBlock` gates its entire rule on
  `hit.getDirection() == UP`. §22 measured the face as nearly dead on the other
  table; it is not dead here.
* **hand — 5 blocks.** `ShelfBlock.useItemOn` opens with
  `if (hand.equals(OFF_HAND)) return PASS`, and the cauldrons and the lectern
  move too. A table taken in one hand states a fact about that hand.

### The static half, and the two holes it had

`ci/probe-reads.py` bounds the same question from above, out of the bytecode:
which rows sit on a rule that reads the player *at all*. On this table it is
**140 of 163 rows, 24 of 28 block classes** — an **upper bound** and unquotable
as a defect count, and a much weaker bound than its
sibling's, because 68 of the 163 refuse on every state and a refused row reads
nothing it can be charged for. It is worth having for the direction it bounds:
23 rows are certified probe-independent from the bytecode.

**It did not agree on the first run, and that is the finding.** The walk called
seven rows clean that the sweep measures moving — cake, the four cauldrons, the
composter and the flower pot — and `ci/probe-reads.py` refused rather than
printing a warning, which is what golden-probe-audit built it to do. Two holes,
both invisible from the `useWithoutItem` table it was written against:

* **The package fence.** The walk stopped at
  `net/minecraft/world/level/block/`, because leaving it swept in
  `Level.playSound` → `PlayerList.broadcast` reading every *other* player. But
  `useItemOn` is handed the stack, and `ItemStack.consume(n, player)` is
  `if (entity == null || !entity.hasInfiniteMaterials()) shrink(n)` — a read of
  the clicking player, in `world/item/`. Fenced out was half of what this table
  is about. `world/item/` and `core/cauldron/` are inside the walk now;
  `Level` and `PlayerList` are in neither and stay out.
* **The functional interface.** `AbstractCauldronBlock.useItemOn` is two calls,
  `Dispatcher.get(stack)` and `CauldronInteraction.interact(...)`.
  `CauldronInteraction` is a functional interface, `interact` resolves to
  itself, it has no body, and the walk stopped with the whole cauldron
  behaviour on the far side. A lambda body is reachable in bytecode only from
  the `invokedynamic` that creates it, so the edge is recovered by descriptor —
  narrow rather than wild, because this descriptor matches 21 methods in the
  jar.

Re-run against `use_without_item.json`, the corrected walk reads
**123 of 184 rows, 35 of 47 block classes** — the same **upper bound**, one
more than §22's 122. That number is
superseded rather than wrong; what actually moved in that table is its
decomposition, and it moved a lot. §22 reported 38 of its 105 constant rows as
"constant because every cell is a refusal". After the component binding there
are **zero** such rows, and "fully measured and constant" went 51 → 90.

### Did the refusal machinery generalise?

**The checker did; the allowlist did not, and could not.**
`ci/check-use-probe.py` reads `use_item_on.json` unchanged, because
`UseItemOnGolden` writes `probeDependent`, `probeAxes`, `probeUnknown`,
`probeStances` and `probeStancesUnavailable` with the same names and meanings —
it sweeps the same `UseGolden.STANCES` over the same `UseGolden.HarnessPlayer`,
in the same `UseGolden.TableLevel`. That is a property of the *dumper* rather
than a generalisation of the checker, so it is checked rather than asserted:
`ci/check-use-probe-falsify.sh` runs its green control against both real tables
and refuses if the two allowlists' `[meta]` blocks ever disagree about how wide
the sweep is.

`ci/probe-reads.py` needed a real change and got one: the method name and
descriptor are now read off the table's own `what` field, and its refusal
decomposition sees through the `default`/`except` compression. One walk, two
tables, and the containment refusal is live on both.

The allowlist is necessarily a second file — its entries are per block and the
two tables share none of them.

### What this does not do

**Nothing was converted.** `790` is not closed and no block was ported. The
table plus its refusal is the deliverable, and the reason is §22's: a table
built to make one check pass is the defect this project keeps finding. The
single next item is the `790` port, which now needs no new golden data at all.
