## 36. Eighty unknowns were seventy sections that run, and "provably never run" was measuring the wrong thing — 2026-08-12, branch `corpus-tick-sections`

**§21's UNIT 2 classified 40 of vanilla's 120 per-tick profiler sections and
left 80 `unclassified`, and §21.4 is blunt about what that word means: 80
sections about which the census has *no information at all*.** §26 moved it 79
→ 80 by retiring one negative. Eighty unknowns under a 33.33% headline is the
largest soft spot the census had left, and it is the one that decides whether
"provably never run" is a floor or a fiction.

It is a fiction, and not by a little. Classified with an instrument that can
produce a *positive*, the same 120 sections read:

```text
   63  RUNS                  every gate on its chain is discharged
    7  RUNS PERIODICALLY     gated on a tick counter or an entity-id stagger
    1  PROVABLY NOT ENTERED  a game rule this harness sets
   33  PROVABLY NOT ENTERED  per-mob, and no recording held that mob
    8  UNDECIDED             the named gate decides it and nothing here can
    8  UNDECIDED             no chain found at all within the gate budget

  -> 70/120 = 58.33% provably ENTERED         (§21 could prove this of none)
  -> 34/120 = 28.33% provably NOT entered     (§21 said 41/120 = 34.17%)
  -> 16/120 = 13.33% undecided without booting something
```

`ci/tick-section-classify.py`, over the pinned `server-26.2.jar` and the six
recordings of ensemble `coverage92-selfcheck-n6-20260811`. Five seconds. **No
vanilla was booted and the box-wide corpus lock was never taken**, per the
pattern §21 set. The census stamp is
`jar=183c0499c5f8 recordings=a9dff28db35c(n=6) census=cca2bab79417 corpus=93`
— note `census=cca2bab79417`, which is §21's own digest: `ci/jarcallgraph.py`
and `ci/vanilla-reach-census.py` are imported here and neither is modified, so
nothing in this section re-stamps anything in that one.

### 36.1 The instrument: what must happen, not what might

§21.3 built a reachability instrument, watched it collapse, and kept it under
`--weak` with the collapse stated. The reason it collapsed is worth restating
because this section is its mirror: an over-approximated call graph can only
say a section *might* run, and "might" over a graph where `wardenBrain` reaches
51 of 139 packet types is worth nothing.

**Dominance answers the other question, and it is the question with an
answer.** A profiler `push` that post-dominates its method's entry — every path
from entry to every `return` passes through it — cannot be skipped. Chain that
from `MinecraftServer.tickServer` through call sites that are themselves
unskippable and the result is a *proof* that the section is entered, not an
inference that it may be. The chain is reported rather than a boolean, because
between `tickServer` and a push there is a sequence of decisions vanilla makes
and the useful output is that sequence:

```text
$ ci/tick-section-classify.py --why naturalSpawnCount
naturalSpawnCount: server tick
  premise  MinecraftServer.pauseWhenEmptySeconds()   MinecraftServer.tickServer@15
  premise  MinecraftServer.pauseWhenEmptySeconds()   MinecraftServer.tickServer@62
  premise  Iterator.hasNext()                        MinecraftServer.tickChildren@133
  premise  parameter #2 of tick                      ServerChunkCache.tick@56
  premise  TickRateManager.runsNormally()            ServerChunkCache.tickChunks@56
```

Loops, `if`s and lambda call-backs are all decisions and all appear: a
`for (level : levels)` surfaces as its `Iterator.hasNext` test, which reads as
"the collection is non-empty", which is what it means. **A gate chain is not a
verdict.** A section RUNS only when every gate on it is discharged by something
outside the jar, and the discharges are enumerated, each with a falsifier, in
`PREMISES` — the run refuses if any of the checkable ones stops holding.

Three conservatisms, each of which costs the positive tier members:

* **A polymorphic call is not crossed.** 2,746 call sites resolve to more than
  one method and the walk stops at every one, because over-approximation is the
  safe direction for a negative and the unsound direction for a positive. Where
  the receiver is `this` it is crossed exactly — an `aload_0` receiver in a walk
  rooted at a class the recordings named has a known runtime type — which is
  what an operand-stack simulation is in this file for, and it is why the pig
  walk reaches `LivingEntity.aiStep` at all.
* **Exception handlers are edges.** A `catch` that rejoins after a push gives a
  path that skipped it. `--no-exc-edges` prints the other reading.
* **The gate budget is finite.** Eight sections have no chain within it and are
  reported as undecided rather than as absent.

### 36.2 The buckets, and what would move a section out of each

| bucket | n | falsifier |
|---|---|---|
| RUNS | 63 | any gate on its chain stops being discharged — a scenario that sends `/tick freeze`, a debug level type, a tick on which the level or chunk collection is empty, or a player-less window longer than `pause-when-empty-seconds` |
| RUNS PERIODICALLY | 7 | a scenario shorter than the counter's period; these are entered on a fixed *fraction* of ticks (tick parity, entity-id stagger, autosave interval), never on all of them |
| PROVABLY NOT ENTERED — game rule | 1 | a scenario re-enabling the rule for its own window, which §26's `[[gamerule]]` mechanism now makes a one-line change |
| PROVABLY NOT ENTERED — per-mob | 33 | one `add_entity` for that mob in any recording |
| UNDECIDED — named gate | 8 | the named condition observed to hold: a teleport, a portal, an explosion, a spawn-eligible chunk, a thundering sky |
| UNDECIDED — no chain | 8 | a wider gate budget, or an instrumented boot |

**The discharged premises are these, and they are not assumptions of
convenience** — each is either checked against the jar or measured over the
recordings, and `PREMISES` carries the falsifier for every one:

* *the server is not paused for emptiness* — `MinecraftServer.tickServer`
  returns early when it is, which is why **nothing whatever in vanilla's tick
  is unconditional in the absolute sense**; both harness players stay connected
  across every scenario;
* *the collection being iterated is non-empty* — levels, loaded chunks,
  players, connections;
* *the tick is neither frozen nor stepping* — checked by parsing
  `ci/t2-gameplay.sh` and every `ci/checks/gameplay/**.toml` for a `/tick`
  command, not by asserting there is none;
* *the level is server-side, and is a `ServerLevel`* — the pinned jar contains
  no `net/minecraft/client/` class at all and declares exactly one subtype of
  `Level`, both checked;
* *`ServerLevel.tick` passes `tickChunks = true`* — read off the constant at
  the call site;
* *the entity is alive when it ticks* — and this one is measured per entity
  type, see 36.4.

### 36.3 The correction: five of the seven "provably off" sections are entered every tick

This is the load-bearing part and it contradicts §21.2 directly. Of the seven
sections §21 counts as shut by a game rule this harness sets — §26 having
already retired `randomTick` from the eight — **five are entered on every
tick**, one survives, and one is undecided:

```text
  naturalSpawnCount        RUNS          push is the 2nd instruction of its method
  filteringSpawningChunks  RUNS          after the join of the SPAWN_MOBS branch
  shuffleSpawningChunks    RUNS          after the join of the SPAWN_MOBS branch
  tickSpawningChunks       RUNS          after the join of the SPAWN_MOBS branch
  weather                  RUNS          popPush at offset 49 of ServerLevel.tick
  customSpawners           NOT ENTERED   ifeq on GameRules.SPAWN_MOBS       <- survives
  spawner                  UNDECIDED     ServerLevel.canSpawnEntitiesInChunk()
```

**The mechanism is one line long: vanilla pushes the profiler section and
*then* tests.** `ServerChunkCache.tickChunks` opens with
`push("naturalSpawnCount")` and reads `GameRules.SPAWN_MOBS` forty bytes later;
`ServerLevel.tick` reaches `popPush("weather")` at offset 49 and the game rule
is consulted inside `advanceWeatherCycle`; `ServerLevel.tickThunder` pushes
`thunder` at offset 32 and tests `isRaining` at 38 and `isThundering` at 42.
The same shape holds for `server gui refresh`, which is entered every tick and
iterates an empty `tickables` list under `--nogui`, and for `gameTests`, which
tickets a ticker with no tests in it.

So the section is entered, and *nothing happens inside it*. §21's negatives
were true claims about **work** attached to a denominator counting
**sections**, and the two are not the same thing. Two axes, stated separately
from here on:

* **entry** — was the profiler section pushed. That is what UNIT 2's
  denominator enumerates, and the corrected figure is 28.33% never entered.
* **work** — did the code inside it do anything. §21.2's six spawning rows are
  substantially right on this axis and this section does not disturb them: with
  `spawn_mobs=false` no mob is spawned by any of the five, whatever their
  profiler section did.

**Why §21's verifier passed a claim that is wrong.** Its own docstring says so
in advance: `rule_is_gated` walks a *neighbourhood* — does the section's code,
within three static hops, read `GameRules.<RULE>` — and it is documented there
as "a staleness guard, not a data-flow proof". `tickChunks` does read
`SPAWN_MOBS`, so the pair verified; the read simply does not gate the push. The
guard was doing exactly its stated job and the conclusion drawn from it was
larger than the job. This is ORACLE rule 7 paying out for the fifteenth time,
and the payout is unusually clean: the instrument had already written down what
it could not do.

**`thunder` stands, and for a better reason than it was standing on.** §21
keeps it as the positive control its verifier refuses, on the grounds that its
real gate is the weather *state* rather than the rule field. The bytecode says
the push is not gated by anything at all — it is entered whenever `tickThunder`
is called, which is whenever a chunk is in entity-ticking range — and the
weather tests are inside. The control is still a control; what it controls for
is sharper.

### 36.4 The 33 survive, and their stated premise does not

The 33 per-mob sections are negative evidence read off `add_entity`, and §21.2
justifies it in one sentence: *"`add_entity` is recorded for every entity that
enters view, so absence over six runs is evidence rather than silence."*
**That sentence is false, and the conclusion it supports is nevertheless
sound.** Measured over all six recordings:

```text
   960  distinct (recording, scenario, observer, raw entity id) pairs
    96  have an add_entity in their own scenario
   864  do not                                    <- the premise as written fails
   819  of those are raw ids 1 and 2, the two harness players
    45  are an item (38) or a pig (7) still alive from a scenario 1-2 earlier
     0  orphans: ids with no add_entity anywhere in their recording
```

Zero orphans is the number that matters, and the 33 rests on it rather than on
the sentence. The party connection persists across scenarios, so entities
outlive the scenario that spawned them; and no packet other than `add_entity`
carries a `kind_id`, so an entity first seen mid-flight is untyped for good.
**The claim to make is "no entity type outside the four appears in the
per-corpus union", not "every entity produced an `add_entity`".** The 45
carry-overs are attributed by gap-1/gap-2 adjacency, which is strong inference
rather than proof, because raw ids are reused after removal.

**And the same recordings, read forwards, are what the positive tier stands
on.** Seventeen sections — `ai`, `newAi`, `mob tick`, `goalSelector` and the
rest of the mob AI path — are proven from a walk rooted at the class the
recordings show ticking. That root is the exact mirror of the 33: the negative
says *no such mob, so no such section*, the positive says *this mob, so this
section*, and they are one instrument pointed both ways. It follows that they
cannot disagree about a mob without one of them being wrong, which is a
property worth having in a census that had only negatives.

Liveness is discharged **per entity type and by measurement**, not for all
four: a `move_entity`, `entity_position`, `set_entity_motion`, `rotate_head` or
`move_entity_rot` for an id that was `add_entity`'d proves the server ticked it.
Pig, item and player qualify. **`falling_block` does not** — over six runs it
produces 12 `move_entity_heartbeat` observations and never one position or
velocity update — so nothing here witnesses it ticking and every section
reachable only through it stays undecided. That asymmetry is the point: a
premise that held for all four would be an assumption wearing a measurement's
clothes.

### 36.5 What is undecidable, and what would decide it

Sixteen sections are undecided and **that is a result, not a gap in one.** A
classification that resolved all 80 would be more suspicious than one that
resolves 64 and says why the rest cannot be: this project's signature defect is
a check that cannot fail, and a classifier with no undecidable bucket is that
defect in a new place. `--selftest`'s fifth control asserts the bucket is
non-empty for exactly that reason.

```text
  named gate, needs the condition observed
    moving, placing                  a player dismounting            ServerPlayer.wantsToStopRiding
    teleportSameDimension            any teleport                    ServerLevel.dimension
    teleportCrossDimension           a cross-dimension teleport      ServerLevel.dimension
    portal                           an entity in a portal           PortalProcessor.processPortalTeleportation
    rest                             a falling block landing         BlockState.isAir
    spawner                          a spawn-eligible chunk          ServerLevel.canSpawnEntitiesInChunk
    thunder                          a chunk in entity-ticking range DistanceManager.inEntityTickingRange

  no chain within the gate budget
    chunkLoad, queueCheckLight, updateSkyLightSources, explosion_blocks,
    find_path, pathfind, hasLineOfSight, keepAlive
```

**What booting would be required.** Nothing in the first group needs a *new*
instrument, only a scenario that produces the event and a recorder that can see
it: a teleport, a nether portal, an explosion, a dismount. The second group is
harder and is honest about which: `keepAlive` is inside
`trace::is_housekeeping`'s twelve dropped packet types (§21.4), so no recording
can witness it by construction; `queueCheckLight` and `updateSkyLightSources`
hang off `LevelChunk.setBlockState`, which the corpus certainly executes —
`block_update` is the second most frequent kind in the recordings — but the
chain from the tick to that call crosses polymorphic dispatch this walk will
not cross, so *the corpus almost certainly runs them and this instrument cannot
say so*. That is the shape of an honest undecidable: not "no evidence" but
"evidence this instrument is the wrong one for".

**The single next item this produces** is not a bigger number here. It is that
§21.5's work order needs re-reading on the entry axis: rows 6-8 were ranked
"cheapest, and cheap because they are ours", and five of their eight sections
turn out to be entered already, so what those rows actually cost is a scenario
that makes the *work* observable — which is what §26 built the `[[gamerule]]`
mechanism for, and which is now the whole of the remaining distance.

### 36.6 No floor, and the reading that stands in its place

**A census is not a comparison, so ORACLE rule 6 has no premise to fire on and
there is no floor here.** §21.4 is explicit that this costs the claim the thing
a floor buys — a statement of resolving power — and that it must not be
silently omitted. What stands in its place, as there, is a reproducibility
reading: the same six recordings classified one at a time.

```text
  recording          RUNS  PERIODIC   OFF  UNPOP  UNDEC
  r1.json              63         7     1     33     16
  r2.json              63         7     1     33     16
  r3.json              63         7     1     33     16
  r4.json              63         7     1     33     16
  r5.json              63         7     1     33     16
  r6.json              63         7     1     33     16
```

Spread **zero on every bucket**. Quote that beside any figure from this
section; a classification with no spread stated is a classification asserting a
stability it did not measure. It is also the strongest available statement
about what the recordings contribute: only two of the six buckets depend on
them at all (the 33, and the entity roots behind 17 of the 63), and neither
moves between runs of the same vanilla.

**Two controls exist because they failed during construction**, and both are in
`--selftest` rather than in a comment:

* every basic block acquired a self-edge, because block successors were taken
  from every instruction rather than from each block's last one. A self-edge is
  a back edge to a header that dominates itself, so the loop relaxation treated
  every block as a loop and deleted every real edge out of it — after which
  almost everything dominated everything and three gated sections, `dragonFight`
  among them, came out unconditional. `javap` disagreeing about the `ifnull`
  guarding `dragonFight` is what caught it;
* a block that cannot reach a `return` was left holding the post-dominator
  iteration's "everything" initialiser, which made every earlier block look
  control-dependent on it and put a spurious gate on `naturalSpawnCount` —
  whose push is the second instruction of its method. The control asserting the
  refutation is what caught it, which is the argument for writing the control
  that asserts your own headline.

## 52. Every roadmap claim against today's recordings — eight rows were closed already, and five greens are narrower than the row they close — 2026-08-17, branch `roadmap-open-row-audit`

Four of §4's rows were found closed or misfiled on 2026-08-17 **by accident, one
at a time, by agents who happened to look before starting**. Nobody had ever
swept the whole table. This section is that sweep, and it needed **no corpus
recording**: every figure below comes from recordings that already existed.

The result is that **eight scenarios named as open work were already closed**,
the oldest by six days, and that **five of the greens this project is resting on
are narrower than the row they close** — which is the more expensive half,
because a row closed on a vacuous green is worse than a row left open.

### 52.1 The instrument, and the three controls that make it one

Four independent full-corpus recordings, all taken 2026-08-17, all `n = 108`:

| recording | taken | declared M/D/A | strict M/D/A |
|---|---|---|---|
| `~/rustmc-stack/oracle-work/gameplay/report.json` | 20:46 | 97 / 8 / 3 | 93 / 14 / 1 |
| `~/rustmc-refcache-bw-A/oracle-work/gameplay/report.json` | 20:02 | 97 / 8 / 3 | 93 / 14 / 1 |
| `~/rustmc-refcache-bw-D/oracle-work/gameplay/report.json` | 18:36 | 97 / 8 / 3 | 93 / 14 / 1 |
| `/home/sayer/grit/work-itemfix/oracle-work/gameplay/report.json` | 12:31 | 97 / 8 / 3 | 93 / 14 / 1 |

They agree **scenario for scenario, with an empty disagreement set** — not
merely on the totals. Every verdict quoted below is therefore a verdict four
recordings hold, not one.

Three controls, because a sweep of this shape has three ways to be worthless:

* **Coverage.** `ci/checks/gameplay/` holds 108 check files; the report holds
  108 scenarios; the symmetric difference is **empty, both ways**. This is the
  control that matters most here — a scenario that is not recorded produces no
  row in the report, reads exactly like a scenario that passed, and would have
  made this entire audit a list of false closures. It was checked first for
  that reason, and it is the check to repeat before trusting any later sweep.
* **Falsifiability.** All **108 of 108** entries in
  `ci/checks/gameplay-falsifiable.toml` are **tier 2**. No verdict below is
  carried by a check that only a structural mutation can redden.
* **Stability.** Fourteen full-corpus reports from 2026-08-12 23:22 to
  2026-08-17 20:46. Across the twenty-four scenarios audited here there are
  **zero flaps** in that window. Every transition found is a single monotone
  step, and each is dated to a commit below.

### 52.4 What these checks could NOT have seen — the five narrow greens

A green is not always evidence. Each of these is a real pass over a **smaller**
claim than the row it appears to close, and each is stated so that nobody cites
it for more than it carries.

1. **`sound.pitch` is read and thrown away by the recorder, and is not folded
   into `rest` either.** `tools/oracle-runner/src/trace.rs:1498` is literally
   `let _pitch = read_f32(&mut r).ok()?;`, and the test at `:1977`
   (`a_sounds_random_seed_and_pitch_are_not_part_of_the_observation`) pins that
   as deliberate. So **no check in this corpus can grade a pitch.** 420's green
   is evidence on the sound's event id, position, source and volume, and is
   **not** evidence on the `pitch 0.55` the row names as the quantity of
   interest. The whole "deterministic pitch" heading is ungradeable by this
   instrument until `corpus-sound-pitch` merges. That is the single most
   load-bearing blind spot found by this audit.
2. **550 and 551 observe `damage_event`, `set_health` and `entity_event`, and
   vanilla emits none of the three.** Vanilla's answer to a bare-stick attack
   is `entity.player.attack.nodamage` — no damage is dealt, so no damage packet
   exists to compare. Those three kinds are dead weight in the projection. The
   green is evidence that **the attack sound and the reach test are right**, and
   is **not** evidence that damage is modelled. 551's own header is correct that
   the sound count is the content; the three unused kinds are not part of it.
3. **607's green only became informative on 2026-08-13, and a green dated
   before that must not be cited.** On the 2026-08-12 23:22 recording the same
   check projected **12** observations carrying slot numbers and state ids and
   **no item payload and no `set_cursor_item`**. Today it projects **17**,
   ending in `set_cursor_item {count: 4}` — the gather that `PICKUP_ALL`
   exists to perform. So §19.5's charge that 607 passed over an arm it could
   not see was **true when it was made**; what repaired it was the recorder
   learning to decode the item stack, not a change to the check. This is the
   audit's clearest case of a green that was vacuous and later became real, and
   the two are indistinguishable from the verdict column alone.
4. **608 earns tier 2 from `speak`, not from an edit of its measured step.**
   Its `killed_by` list carries `retype` and `speak` and lacks `drop-measured`,
   `reorder` and `inject`. That is the sanctioned narrow promotion for a check
   that declares its measured step silent — 608 asserts that an out-of-range
   slot changes nothing — but it means 608's content is **an assertion of
   absence**, and it should not be counted beside a check that compares a
   payload.
5. **611's raw traces still differ and that is correct, not hidden.** Vanilla
   reaches `container_set_slot.state = 7` where we reach `5`. The field is
   deliberately rebased by `compare::rebase_session_counters`
   (`compare.rs:598`, 2026-08-11) because the wire number counts *packets sent
   on that menu*, not changes made, and vanilla cannot reproduce it against
   vanilla. Written down because anyone diffing the two JSON files by hand will
   find this and read it as a defect.

### 52.5 One row grades a scenario that does not exist

**`160` has no check file in the tree.** `ls ci/checks/gameplay/16*` matches
nothing, and `water-spreads` is absent from all 108 recorded scenarios. It was
parked out of the corpus by `e47d7ca3`, "park water-spreads in open/ — 24/25
flaps, and an error can never be blessed".

It nevertheless still holds a `[[unstable]]` entry in
`ci/checks/gameplay-unstable.toml` and still occupies a row in §22's "eleven
that cannot convert" table with a `declared + strict` denominator **it no
longer consumes**. The fluids row therefore grades a scenario that cannot be
recorded, and any arithmetic over that table is off by one row. Fixing the
denominator is not this branch's to do — it touches figures other agents own —
but the fact is recorded here so the next reader does not re-derive it.

### 52.6 The two rows that are duplicates, not items

* **"block sounds, random pitch" (380, 390) is the block-events row wearing a
  sound heading.** Neither scenario reports `sound` among its missing kinds;
  both report `block_event`, and 390 also `section_blocks_update`. The row
  already says MIS-SITED and this audit confirms it from the recordings. It
  should be **retired into the block-events row**, not worked: as a standing
  row it reads as a second, independent sound item and prices piston work
  twice.
* **"block sounds, deterministic pitch" retains exactly one live member.** 420
  is closed (narrowly — note 1 above), 400 is a scheduled-tick item by its own
  row text, and 430's first divergence is a `block_event` and an extraction
  defect. Nothing under this heading is a sound port today.

### 52.7 What would settle each thing this audit could not

* **The pitch family** — merge `corpus-sound-pitch`. Until then no green on any
  sound scenario is evidence about a pitch, and §4's sound headings cannot be
  graded either way. This is the one blocked item where the block is an
  instrument and not a port.
* **Whether combat damage is modelled** — a scenario in which vanilla actually
  deals damage, so `damage_event` and `set_health` are non-empty in the
  reference. 550 and 551 cannot answer it and were never built to; the row's
  green must not be read as coverage of `Player.attack`'s damage path.
* **780 and 790** — both are live divergences with named missing kinds and
  neither appears in §4's family table. They need rows before they need work.

### 52.8 The count

Twenty-four scenarios carrying a §4 or §0 claim were checked against four
recordings. **Eight were stale in the closed direction** (604, 607, 550, 551,
609, 552, 420, plus the 250/310/320/440 family read as one row), **none were
stale in the open direction** — no row claiming a closure had regressed —
**one row grades a scenario that does not exist** (160), **two rows are
duplicates of other rows** (the two sound headings), and **two live
divergences have no row at all** (780, 790).

Nothing here required a corpus run, a lock, or a server boot. The whole of it
is four `report.json` files that were already on disk, and the reason it had
never been done is that closing a row that is already closed feels like it
cannot be where the work is.
## 49. The accepted tier is empty, and what it cost to empty it — 2026-08-13, branch `gameplay-serverbound-reach`

Branch `corpus-serverbound-surface` measured the serverbound half of the play
protocol and found that **53 of the 69 serverbound play packet types cannot
make any check in this repository go red**. It named the worst single case and
deliberately did not close it. This section is the closing.

Every figure below was re-measured on this tree rather than carried over, and
`ci/serverbound-surface.py` was run here as an out-of-tree instrument — that
branch is not merged, so the script is **not** in this tree's `ci/` and this
section's numbers cannot be reproduced from this tree alone until it is. Said
plainly rather than left for somebody to discover.

### 49.1 What `ACCEPT_TELEPORTATION` turned out to be

Not a gap in coverage. A **live defect**, and a second one hiding behind it.

`crate::player::apply` decoded the packet, wrote
`PlayerState::acknowledged_teleport`, and returned `Update::Teleport(id)`.
Grepped across the whole tree: the only `Update::Teleport` sites were that
constructor and one assertion in `player.rs`'s own unit tests. The arm could
have been deleted and every check in the repository would have stayed green —
which is what the census means by the `accepted` tier, and this packet was the
only member of it.

The second defect is the one worth generalising. The field's doc comment read:

> The last teleport id the client acknowledged. A client that has not
> acknowledged the spawn teleport is still falling into place, and its
> positions are not yet authoritative.

That sentence describes a behaviour **no line of this server implemented**. It
is not a lie about a mechanism that regressed; it is a caveat that was written
alongside the decoder and never had a corresponding read. A comment like that
is worse than none, because it answers the question a later reader would
otherwise have gone and asked of the code.

### 49.2 What vanilla actually does, from the jar

`ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleAcceptTeleportPacket`, `javap -p -c
-constants` against the pinned `server-26.2.jar`:

```text
   12: getId()                       ; the id the client acknowledged
   17: getfield awaitingTeleport
   20: if_icmpne 128                 ; an id we are not awaiting -> silent return
   24: getfield awaitingPositionFromClient
   27: ifnonnull 41
   31: ldc "multiplayer.disconnect.invalid_player_movement"
   37: disconnect(...)               ; right id, nothing awaited
   41..116: absSnapTo, lastGoodX/Y/Z, hasChangedDimension()
  123: awaitingPositionFromClient = null      <- ONLY this is cleared
  128: return
```

`awaitingTeleport` is never cleared and `awaitingPositionFromClient` is, and
that asymmetry is the entire mechanism. Three behaviours fall out of it, and
this server had none of them:

* an acknowledgement of an id we are not awaiting is **ignored, silently** —
  which is what lets a client answer a teleport that has since been superseded;
* the first correct acknowledgement **snaps the player to the position the
  server chose**, over anything the client has claimed since;
* a **second** acknowledgement of the same id matches at 20, finds null at 27,
  and **disconnects**.

And through `updateAwaitingTeleport`, called at `handleMovePlayer` offset 123:

```text
    awaitingPositionFromClient != null:
        tickCount - awaitingTeleportTime > 20 -> teleport(awaiting...) again
        return true  -> handleMovePlayer applies absSnapRotationTo at 137
                        and returns at 140
```

So while a teleport is outstanding the claimed **position and the flags byte
are discarded together, and the rotation still lands**. A client that never
acknowledges cannot move, and is re-teleported about once a second.

### 49.3 A check for it needed a connection the corpus did not have

`crate::record::record` logs in one actor and one observer and replays **every**
scenario in the corpus on those two connections. That is not incidental to this
item, it is the reason the item was open: the cheapest discriminator for this
packet is a disconnect, and a check that disconnects the actor destroys every
scenario after it. The corpus would report that as ninety checks that had
abruptly stopped saying anything — which looks exactly like a broken server.

**This is a harness blind spot with a shape, not a one-off.** Several
serverbound handlers' only observable answer is a
`ClientboundDisconnectPacket`; `handleKeepAlive` is the next one
(`ServerCommonPacketListenerImpl`, offset 51: the disconnect is skipped only
for `isSingleplayerOwner`, and the gate boots a dedicated server). Every one of
them was unfalsifiable here for a reason on our side of the wire rather than
anything in the protocol.

So `trace::Who` gains a third value, `Probe`: a connection a scenario opens
with `probe_join`, is measured on its own socket, and which `run_one` drops
when the scenario ends — whether or not the server hung up first. Three
properties make it safe rather than merely convenient:

* **it is dropped unconditionally, including after an error.** There is no verb
  to close one, so a check cannot forget. A probe that outlived its scenario
  would be a second player standing in the world for every check after it,
  present on one server and not the other exactly when the mechanism under test
  worked;
* **`is_hangup` is narrow** — `UnexpectedEof`, `ConnectionReset`,
  `ConnectionAborted`, `BrokenPipe` and nothing else — so a decode failure or a
  short read is still a loud error, and an unexpected disconnect on the actor
  still fails its scenario. A blanket "any error means we were disconnected"
  would turn a server that crashed mid-corpus into ninety checks quietly
  reporting silence;
* **`From::Both` does not include the probe.** A probe joins inside the measured
  window, so its login sequence is visible to the actor and the observer too. A
  check reading every stream would be comparing a join it never asked about
  alongside the one packet it did.

### 49.4 `790`'s "must stay last" rule was narrower than it read

`ci/checks/gameplay/790-*` claims to be permanently the highest-numbered check,
because it leaves a dandelion in the actor's inventory and `Scenario::load_dir`
sorts by path. The new check is `920`, so the rule had to be settled rather
than stepped around.

What `790` leaks reaches a later check through exactly one route: a `hold` into
a hotbar slot lands beside a different set of items. So the constraint is not
"nothing may follow 790", it is **nothing that reads the actor's inventory
layout may follow 790** — and the two coincided only for as long as every check
in the corpus was an actor check. `920` holds nothing and its `observe_from` is
`probe`, so the actor's stream is not in its projection at all. `790`'s comment
now says this, and says that a check which holds an item still belongs below it.

### 49.5 The surface figure, before and after

Measured by `ci/serverbound-surface.py` on this tree, at `a106314d` plus this
branch:

```text
                            before   after
   in the protocol             69      69
   the server has an arm for   20      20
     HANDLED                   16      17
     ACCEPTED                   1       0
     DISCARDED                  3       3
   handled AND sent            14      15
   no check can fail on        55      54
```

**16 of 69 can make a check go red, before. 17 of 69, after.**

The instrument's own refusal is the better evidence than any of those numbers.
`ACCEPTED_REASON` is a table a packet must appear in when the sink analysis
finds nothing behind its arm — and a packet that *gains* a sink is then
reported as an unnecessary entry. On the first run after the port it exited
non-zero with

```text
serverbound-surface: REFUSED — ACCEPTED_REASON names ACCEPT_TELEPORTATION,
which the analysis does not find in that state — drop the entry
```

which is the census saying, without being asked and without being able to
flatter anyone, that this packet is no longer in the tier it was written up in.

### 49.6 What that figure is NOT, and the discipline it needs

**`handled` is a static reachability claim.** It says an arm exists and
something downstream of it reaches an observable sink. It does not say a check
would fail if the arm were broken, and the two come apart exactly where this
project's defects live. A packet must not be reported as covered because a
check touches its code path.

So the figure above is the census's, and the *mutation evidence* is separate
and is what a claim of coverage rests on: break the handler, watch a named
check go red, restore it, watch it go green. See §49.7.

## 57. What is unmatched in the nether, named: two `bastion_remnant` starts carry 97.6% of the only adjudicable residual — 2026-08-18, branch `nether-biome-census`

`docs/PARITY.md` §5 has called the nether "the honest weak spot" since it was
written, and the sentence it could not finish was *which* spot. It can now.

The nether has exactly one window and one biome where vanilla's own
disagreement with itself is small enough to adjudicate this port at all:
**`soul_sand_valley` at seed 20260722, centre (64,64), r=16, chunks 48..80,
`--ybox 0 127`, twin-masked — 70,130 blocks of 30,089,264, against a floor of
3,442..4,960 over six same-order vanilla pairs.** 14.1x the floor. Every other
biome at every other window measured has a floor larger than our residual and
may only carry deltas (§5's table, eight rows, six of them unquotable).

Charged to vanilla's own saved starts at margin 0 — margin 0 because
`bastion_remnant` declares `terrain_adaptation: none` and therefore beards
nothing, and because at the tool's default margin of 16 a fossil's ring
overlaps a bastion's and 13,844 blocks of bastion material get charged to
three `nether_fossil` boxes:

```text
  46,856   66.8%   bastion_remnant (55,63)        105 pieces, not ported
  21,591   30.8%   bastion_remnant (70,49)         89 pieces, not ported
   1,261    1.8%   outside every structure box     BELOW the 3,442 biome floor
     313    0.4%   ruined_portal_nether (48,64)    portable today, never placed here
      75    0.1%   two nether_fossil boxes         of ~137 fossil starts in the window
```

### CORRECTED THE SAME DAY, before this section was an hour old

The ranking below was written from the three windows this project had
measured, all of which are soul sand valley or basalt deltas. Two more windows
were then generated, holding `crimson_forest` and `warped_forest` for the
first time, and they carry something larger than `bastion_remnant`:

```text
  window                biome            ours          of    exactness    x floor
  31415926 c(0,0)       crimson_forest  79,911   6,674,283   98.802703%      1.7
  31415926 c(-200,200)  crimson_forest  58,229   4,819,195   98.791728%      1.6
                        warped_forest   13,795   1,795,823   99.231829%      1.8
                        nether_wastes    5,053     722,927   99.301036%    297.2
```

`worldgen-dump`'s REFUSED block names the whole cause on both windows, and
nothing else appears in it:

```text
  3,871 / 4,103   minecraft:huge_fungus
  2,870 / 3,425   minecraft:nether_forest_vegetation
  2,378 / 1,913   minecraft:weeping_vines
```

**Three feature families, none ported, ~152,000 blocks across the two windows
— more than twice the entire adjudicable residual of the r=16 window this
section was written about.** They rank **above** `bastion_remnant` by area and
**below** it by resolving power: the forest windows sit at 1.6–1.8x their
floors where the r=16 soul-sand-valley window sits at 14.1x. Port the fungi
first if the goal is what a player sees, the bastion first if the goal is a
number that can be defended.

The reason they were invisible is worth more than the items: **every nether
window this project had ever measured was soul sand valley or basalt deltas,
and none of the three features generates in either.** A dimension is not
covered by measuring it harder in the place you already look, and the cost of
finding out was one afternoon of candidate dumps read for their biome
denominators.

### The four items, in the order they are worth

1. **`bastion_remnant` — 68,447 blocks, 97.6%.** A jigsaw structure, 105 and
   89 pieces at the two starts. This port already walks jigsaws: villages and
   trial chambers are gated piece-for-piece against vanilla's own
   `Children[]`. What bastion adds is its own pool set, its `pool_alias`
   handling and its processors. **This is the whole of the nether's remaining
   measurable defect and it is one structure.** Closing it would take the only
   adjudicable nether window to 1,683 blocks, which is below its own floor —
   i.e. it would close the dimension by the same standard the End was closed
   by.
2. **`FireBlock.canSurvive` — 483 refusals at r=16.** `worldgen-dump`'s
   REFUSED block names it. The rule is
   `below.isFaceSturdy(UP) || isValidFireLocation(pos)` and
   `isValidFireLocation` is `any of the six neighbours has getIgniteOdds > 0`,
   which needs the 177-entry table `FireBlock.bootStrap` builds. `soul_fire`
   was the same shape with a one-tag rule and is ported: it was worth
   **327 -> 104 and 477 -> 253** on the two 20260722 r=7 windows on the day.
   Do not implement only the `isFaceSturdy` clause because the nether has no
   flammable blocks in it — that is an approximation, and an approximation is
   a one-way door.
3. **`ruined_portal_nether` — 313 blocks.** `structure/ruined_portal.rs` is
   ported and the overworld decoration path places its six overworld variants
   from `ruined_portals.json`. The nether decoration path never calls
   `ruined_portal_starts`, so the seventh member of that set is missing in
   this dimension specifically. There is a start at (48,64) inside the r=16
   window, so the fix is measurable the day it lands.
4. **`fortress` — unmeasured, and say so rather than counting it closed.**
   There is no `fortress` start anywhere in the r=16 window, so no window this
   project has generated exercises it. A gate a window cannot exercise proves
   nothing.

### What is NOT on this list, and why that is the finding

* **`basalt_deltas`, at every window.** 109,518 blocks at r=16 against a
  vanilla floor of 313,045..398,660 — the floor is 2.9x our whole residual,
  and 100% of it sits outside every structure box. It is decoration scatter in
  the biome where vanilla is 500x less reproducible than anywhere else in the
  dimension (`docs/DETERMINISM.md` §47). **There is nothing to fix here that
  any instrument this project owns could see.** Do not spend a run on it.
* **The 1,261 blocks outside every structure box in `soul_sand_valley`.**
  Below that biome's own floor of 3,442. Real work may be hiding under them
  and no measurement can say so; a wider ensemble is the only thing that would
  change that, and the floor is a union that grows with every reference added.
* **Seed 31415926, in every biome.** Its basalt floor is 3.4x our residual,
  its soul-sand-valley floor exceeds our residual, and its nether-wastes floor
  exceeds our residual. The second seed exists because one seed could not
  carry the claim; what it carries today is corroboration, and §5 now says so
  rather than implying otherwise.

### The closing condition

`soul_sand_valley` at seed 20260722 r=16 below its own floor, with the
attribution table above empty of structure rows. That is one number, on one
window, and it is reachable by porting one structure. **It closes the
soul-sand-valley half of the dimension and not the dimension** — the forest
half needs `huge_fungus`, `nether_forest_vegetation` and `weeping_vines`, and
its closing condition is `crimson_forest` below ~45,000 on the 31415926
c(0,0) window, which is that biome's own vanilla floor there.
