## 58. What is unmeasured in the overworld, named: 37 of 55 biomes, and `sculk` is the biggest single thing hiding in them — 2026-08-18, branch `overworld-biome-census`

§57 ranked the nether's remaining defects after the same question was asked of
it. This is the overworld's answer, and the shape is the same but an order of
magnitude wider, because the overworld carries the great majority of this
project's published figures and its windows were chosen the same way.

### 58.1 The state before any repair

All 41 registered overworld figures are centre chunk (64,64) at r=16 on three
seeds. They hold **eighteen of the dimension's fifty-five biomes** — a count
this section first published as twelve, before seed 31415926's differently
named references were found; `docs/DETERMINISM.md` §48.5 is the correction —
and exactly one of the eighteen is above its own floor, `lush_caves` at 1.02x.
On the two squares this section was first written from, nothing clears. `docs/DETERMINISM.md` §48 has both
decompositions; `docs/PARITY.md` has the table.

So before this branch the overworld had **one biome with resolving power and
it reads 1.02x**, which is not a measurement anyone should act on.
After three r=7 harvests outside the published centre it has sixteen, in
twenty-three biomes, over three squares each a fifth of the area.

### 58.2 The ranking, by blocks, and it is not the same as by count

From a block-family census of window A against its own reference — a mechanism
the positional diff does not share — and from the REFUSED tallies across all
three squares:

```text
  rank  what                        blocks (window A)   status
   1    sculk + sculk_vein                     38,815   NOT PORTED
   2    pale oak trees + moss                  ~13,400  trunk placer NOT PORTED
   3    dark oak trees                          ~8,200  trunk placer NOT PORTED
   4    stone brick family                      ~8,670  unattributed
   5    large_dripstone                          1,593  NOT PORTED, 4,569 declines
```

**`sculk` is the single largest unported family in the overworld**: vanilla
writes 30,184 `sculk` and 9,053 `sculk_vein` over window A and this port writes
10 and 412. `deep_dark` is 2.67x its floor there and 1.57x in a second window
900 chunks away, so it is the best-corroborated overworld defect this project
has ever had a window on, and its cause is two features:
`sculk_patch_deep_dark` and `sculk_vein`.

**`minecraft:large_dripstone` is the largest refusal by COUNT** — 543, 1977 and
2049 declines in the three squares, 4,569 in total, more than any other feature
anywhere in this port — and only the fifth largest by blocks. That gap is the
warning: a refusal tally ranks by how often a feature is *attempted*, and the
nether lane made the mirror-image mistake reading a residual off its top block
families. Rank by blocks, corroborate by count.

**The dark oak and pale oak trees are one item, not two.**
`minecraft:dark_oak_trunk_placer` is not in `TrunkPlacer::is_supported`
(`Straight | Forking | Fancy`), and `TreeConfig::is_supported` is an AND over
every part of a config, so every dark oak and every pale oak in the dimension
is refused whole. That is ~21,600 blocks in one r=7 square and it is one
trunk placer.

### 58.3 The one repair made here, and why it is the template

`leave_vine`. 160 declines of `straight trunk, blob foliage, decorators
["minecraft:leave_vine"]` — **both placers already supported, one decorator
refusing the whole tree**. Ported from `LeaveVineDecorator`:
`swamp` **21,030 → 4,506**, from 4.97x its floor to 1.07x, 16,532 blocks off
that window's residual, at the cost of one enum variant and one function.

The identical shape is open in jungle right now:
`["minecraft:cocoa", "trunk_vine", "leave_vine"]`, 186 declines, waiting only
on `cocoa`. **But it must not be done blind.** `jungle` sits at 0.53 of its
floor in window B, so the port could be made and nothing this project owns
could tell whether it worked. Harvest a jungle-dominant square first —
`ci/ow-biome-scout.sh` finds one without harvesting anything — then port.

### 58.4 THE SINGLE NEXT ITEM

**Port `sculk_patch_deep_dark` and `sculk_vein`.** It is the largest unported
family in the dimension by blocks, it is the only overworld defect corroborated
across two independent windows, and both of those windows already exist and are
harvested. The result that closes it: `deep_dark` at seed 20260722 r=7 centre
(-1056,-672) below 17,695, and at centre (-480,-1440) below 21,900.

Second: `dark_oak_trunk_placer`, which is one placer and two biomes and ~21,600
blocks — but note that `dark_forest` is at 0.72 of its floor and `pale_garden`
at 0.50, so **it is a port for the player and not for the number**, and a
window that adjudicates it has not been found yet. Say which of the two goals
any commit on it is for.

Third: `large_dripstone`, worth 4,569 declines and 1,593 blocks, in a biome
that resolves in all three squares at 7.49x, 3.63x and 1.87x. The cheapest of
the three to validate and the smallest to win.

### 58.5 Nulls — do not re-run these

* **Do not open an investigation on `mangrove_swamp`.** 82,596 blocks against a
  floor of 214,991 — vanilla disagrees with itself over 2.4% of the biome. It
  is the overworld's `basalt_deltas`, and no instrument this project owns can
  see a defect in it. Its trees also need `upwards_branching_trunk_placer` and
  a root placer, so it is expensive as well as unmeasurable.
* **Do not widen N on the published r=16 squares hoping a biome emerges.**
  `sulfur_caves` carries 43.87% of the 20260722 floor in 3.49% of the window.
  More references grow a floor, they do not shrink it — `docs/DETERMINISM.md`
  §4 — so the biome that is furthest under its floor is the one that will stay
  there.
* **Do not quote an aggregate overworld exactness.** Same argument as
  `docs/DETERMINISM.md` §47 made for the nether, and the overworld's weights
  are more lopsided: 78.70% of the only quotable r=16 overworld figure is
  `frozen_ocean`.
* **`forest` is measured and is not a defect.** 17 blocks in window A against a
  floor of 1,046, and 15,413 against 17,406 in window B. Both under. It is one
  of the few common biomes that needs nothing.

### 58.6 Where the count finished, and what `cocoa` taught that `leave_vine` did not

**40 of 55 overworld biomes now carry a figure, against 18 when this branch
started.** Five r=7 squares hold 29 biomes between them, 22 of which had never
been inside any window this project had generated. Fifteen still have none:

```text
  bamboo_jungle      deep_frozen_ocean  frozen_peaks         savanna_plateau
  cherry_grove       eroded_badlands    mushroom_fields      snowy_slopes
  taiga              flower_forest      old_growth_pine_taiga
  warm_ocean         windswept_forest   old_growth_spruce_taiga
  windswept_gravelly_hills
```

`ci/ow-biome-scout.sh` reaches all fifteen; three more squares would cover
them, and the scout costs no vanilla time at all.

**The lesson `cocoa` added.** `leave_vine` was the easy shape — one decorator
missing, port it, the biome falls to its floor. `cocoa` is the shape that
matters more, and it is this:

> **Unblocking one part of a feature family can make a biome's positional
> residual WORSE while making its contents dramatically more right, and both
> readings are correct.**

`cocoa` put roughly twenty thousand blocks of jungle canopy into a world that
had none — `jungle_leaves` 0 → 8,984 of 12,001, `cocoa` 0 → 65 of 67 — and
`jungle`'s residual went **up** in two independent squares while
`sparse_jungle`'s went **down** in both. The cause is mechanical and worth
knowing before the next port: **a refused tree spends no randomness at all,
while vanilla spends the whole tree's draws.** So every unported tree in a
biome desynchronises the stream for everything decorated after it in that
chunk. Porting *some* of a biome's trees leaves the desynchronisation in place
and adds correctly-generated-but-displaced content on top of it.

Two consequences for how to rank work here:

1. **Port a biome's tree family whole, or expect its positional residual to
   move the wrong way.** `mega_jungle_trunk_placer` — 93 declines in window J,
   69 in B — is not an optional follow-up to `cocoa`; it is the other half of
   the same item.
2. **Read the block census beside the residual on any port that unblocks a
   refusal.** They can disagree, and when they do the census is the one
   measuring whether the port is right.

### 58.7 The ranking, updated

1. **`sculk_patch_deep_dark` + `sculk_vein`** — unchanged and still first.
   38,815 blocks in window A alone, corroborated in two windows (2.67x, 1.57x),
   both already harvested.
2. **`mega_jungle_trunk_placer`** — the other half of `cocoa`. `jungle` is at
   3.94x its floor in window J and will not come down until this lands. It is
   the only item on this list whose *closing result is already measured*: the
   number to beat is 41,024, and 39,874 is what the biome read before `cocoa`,
   so anything above that means the pair is still incomplete.
3. **`dark_oak_trunk_placer`** — one placer, two biomes, ~21,600 blocks, and a
   port for the player rather than the number: `dark_forest` is at 0.72 of its
   floor and `pale_garden` at 0.50.
4. **`large_dripstone`** — 4,569 declines, 1,593 blocks, in a biome that
   resolves in three squares at 7.49x, 3.63x and 1.87x. Cheapest to validate.

### 58.8 One more null

**`deep_ocean` at 2.46x is terrain or carvers and nothing else.** Window O
declines **no feature at all** — zero refusals over 225 chunks — and
`cold_ocean` is byte-identical to vanilla across 1,253,376 blocks in the same
square. So the 555 blocks in `deep_ocean` cannot be an unported feature, and
looking for one there is time spent. That is the most narrowly-scoped defect
this branch found and the only one with no candidate cause attached.

## 67. Jungle moved the wrong way a third time, and the gap is about two draws a tree — 2026-08-18, branch `sculk-deep-dark`

The census left `mega_jungle_trunk_placer` as the one open item whose closing
result was already measured: beat **41,024**, and 39,874 was what `jungle` read
in window J before `cocoa`. It is ported. The number is **44,239**, and this
section is that result rather than an excuse for it.

### 67.1 What was ported and what it is worth

It is two placers, not one. `minecraft:jungle_foliage_placer` is
`MegaJungleFoliagePlacer` and was `Unimplemented` alongside the trunk placer,
and `TreeConfig::is_supported` is an AND, so landing the trunk placer alone
would have changed nothing at all. `GiantTrunkPlacer` is factored out because
mega pine and mega spruce need it unchanged.

The block census says the port is right. Window J, 225 chunks, against its own
reference — no mechanism shared with the positional diff:

```text
                      vanilla    before     after
    jungle_leaves      12,001     8,984    11,798     98.3%
    jungle_log          2,655     1,670     2,593     97.7%
    vine               11,569     9,388    11,400     98.5%
```

`minecraft:bamboo` was ported in the same branch — the last refusal in the
jungle's step-9 list — and vanilla's 131 blocks read 137 in ours.

### 67.2 The positional residual, in both windows that hold jungle

```text
    window J (960,-192)      floor 10,414      before 41,024   after 44,239
    window B (-480,-1440)    floor 12,788      before  7,498   after  8,823
```

**Window B does not adjudicate this and never did.** 8,823 against a floor of
12,788 is 0.69x, so it is under its floor and is not a measurement — the same
verdict the census reached at 0.53x, and one more port has not changed it.
Window J is the only square this project owns that can see jungle, and in
window J the port made the number worse for the third consecutive time, after
`leave_vine` (which helped swamp) and `cocoa` (which hurt jungle).

`sparse_jungle`, which has no mega jungle trees, is 11,708 against a floor of
10,363 — **1.13x** — in the same square. The tree machinery, the selector, the
decorators and `cocoa` are therefore all right. What is wrong is confined to
the mega jungle tree.

### 67.3 The gap is a draw count, and it is about two per tree

Padding the mega jungle tree with `k` extra draws and re-measuring window J:

```text
    k        0        1        2        3        4
  jungle  44,239   43,858   41,671   44,661   43,281
```

A clean minimum at **k = 2** and nothing like it elsewhere, so the port spends
about two values fewer per mega jungle tree than vanilla does. The padding is
not a fix and was not committed: two draws spent at the END of the tree put the
following trees back in step while leaving this tree's own blocks displaced,
which is why 41,671 is still above 41,024 rather than far below it.

Every part of the placer has been read against `javap -p -c -constants` on the
pinned jar and matches: `getTreeHeight` two draws; `foliageHeight` and
`foliageRadius` constant and drawless; `placeTrunk` receiving the **clipped**
height `k1` and not the drawn height `i`; `placeBelowTrunkBlock` four times
with no guard; the branch loop's `nextFloat` and `nextInt(4)`; the crown
carrying `doubleTrunk = true` so it does not take
`MegaJungleFoliagePlacer`'s `1 + nextInt(2)` while each branch does. The
decorator lists are already sorted stably by y, which the port has done since
`858a920e`. **So the two draws are somewhere a line-by-line reading does not
see, and the next lane should build the instrument rather than re-read the
class.** What is missing is a per-feature draw-count oracle: our own draw
count is available through `RUSTMC_TRACE_DRAWS`, and vanilla's is not, which
is the whole difficulty.

### 67.4 A correction, and it is about the mechanism itself

I found `minecraft:bamboo` by noticing that `bamboo_light` sits immediately
before `trees_jungle` in `minecraft:jungle` and is absent from
`minecraft:sparse_jungle`, and read that as the head of the desync chain — an
unported feature refuses, spends no randomness, and displaces everything after
it.

**That is the census's `cocoa` mechanism and it does not reach across
features.** `setFeatureSeed(decorationSeed, index, step)` gives one stream per
feature index, so bamboo cannot displace a single jungle tree by way of the
random; the only coupling is world state, because bamboo blocks occupy space
later features read. Bamboo is worth porting and is not the jungle's problem.

The mechanism operates strictly **within one placed feature's own stream**,
where `trees_jungle` places many trees from one stream. That is the correct
statement of it, and it is narrower than the one this branch started with.

### 67.5 What this does NOT license

It does not license reading three consecutive wrong-way movements as three
causes. `leave_vine`, `cocoa` and `mega_jungle_trunk_placer` are one cause seen
three times: content that is correct and displaced counts twice against a
positional residual, once where vanilla has it and once where we put it. The
test that would distinguish a genuine second cause is the one this section
fails — **a residual that falls when the trunk placer lands never needed a
second explanation** — and jungle's did not fall.

## 66. The deep dark generates: the sculk gate was shut on a measurement four later commits had overturned — 2026-08-18, branch `sculk-deep-dark`

The census ranked `sculk` the largest unported family in the overworld by
blocks — 30,184 against our 10 in window A, 38,815 counting veins — and named
`sculk_patch_deep_dark` + `sculk_vein` as the single next item. **Nothing
needed porting.** `sculk_patch`, `sculk_spreader`, the vein behaviour, the
catalyst and the discharge were all written on 2026-08-09 and were sitting
behind `RUSTMC_SCULK_VEIN`, defaulted off.

### 66.1 Why a shipped feature reads as an unported one

The refusal tally is the instrument that would normally answer this, and it
was silent: **window A declines 1,142 features across 24 distinct kinds and
not one of them is sculk.** A feature switched off at a boolean is not a
feature refused, so it appears in no tally, and the block census — 30,184 to
10 — looks precisely like an unported family.

The switch carried a reason: *"does not terminate usefully"*, from the day a
single chunk took over 120 s where a 25-chunk window had taken seconds. Two
commits later `2ac46e12` found the cause — `vein_config()` re-parsing the
whole block-state extract inside the per-cursor closure — hoisted it into a
`OnceLock` and measured 23.22 s. It left the default off and said why: still
5x the baseline, and sculk volume 4% of vanilla's. Then `c78a5624`,
`a0f17d7c`, `6ab8e40a` and `858a920e` took the volume from 4% to 83% and the
veins to essentially exact. **Both stated reasons expired; the comment did
not.**

> A default with a reason attached is a decision. A default whose reason has
> been overturned by later commits in the same file is a decision nobody is
> making any more, and it will be read as a fact about the port for as long as
> it stands. Re-measure a switch before believing what it says about itself.

Re-measured, window A of `ci/ow-new-windows.sh`, 225 chunks: **18 s off, 23 s
on.** 1.3x, not 5x.

### 66.2 The instrument was wired to its own subject

Every counter and narration line in the dispatcher was gated on
`sculk_vein_enabled()` — the switch deciding whether the counted thing runs.
It cost both directions. Patch start/refusal counts were unreadable in exactly
the configuration whose 10 blocks needed explaining, and a real dump with the
spread on buried the refusal tally under a `SCULK_BRANCH` line per patch.
`RUSTMC_SCULK_TRACE` is now separate: one switch decides what the world
contains, the other what the log contains.

### 66.3 The largest defect the switch was hiding was not sculk

Turning it on made `deep_dark` worse in both windows — 47,290 -> 59,796 in A
and 34,408 -> 54,413 in B — with the block census far better, which is the
`cocoa` shape and was ready to be believed. Decomposing by block pair instead:

```text
  van=air        ours=cave_air        129 -> 15,720   +15,591
  van=sculk      ours=deepslate    19,317 ->  7,389   -11,928
  van=deepslate  ours=sculk             0 ->  5,763    +5,763
```

`SculkVeinBlock.onDischarged` replaces a vein that has lost every face with
`Blocks.AIR` — or `Blocks.WATER` where a fluid is present — and this port
wrote `cave_air`. One wrong block name, reachable only once the spread runs,
worth more mismatches in window A than every misplaced sculk block put
together.

### 66.4 Where deep_dark stands

```text
                  floor(N=2)   census    spread on   + air fix      x
  deep_dark A         17,695   47,290       59,796      44,180    2.50
  deep_dark B         21,900   34,408       54,413      33,499    1.53
```

Better than the census in both windows and **above its floor in both**, so the
figure moved and the movement is a measurement. The census's closing criterion
— below 17,695 in A and below 21,900 in B — is **NOT met**, and the deep dark
is still the largest single defect in the overworld.

Block census, window A: `sculk` 10 -> 25,278 of 30,184, `sculk_vein` 412 ->
8,705 of 9,053, `sculk_catalyst` **exact** at 47, `sculk_sensor` 96 of 164,
`sculk_shrieker` 12 against 10.

### 66.4b A sculk patch does not respect a biome boundary

Switching the spread on moved **nine more registered rows** across windows A,
B and J, none of them `deep_dark`. Same reference pairs, same N=2 floors, same
dump order — only the port changed:

```text
  win  biome              was     now
   A   dripstone_caves  11,105  11,122
   A   birch_forest      9,164   9,385
   A   lush_caves        4,392   4,669
   A   grove             3,160   3,362
   A   meadow              546     616
   B   dripstone_caves  21,761  22,106
   B   sparse_jungle     7,547   7,589
   B   plains              382     271     IMPROVED
   J   sparse_jungle    11,793  11,995
```

A residual attributed to **vanilla's** biome at each position moves whenever a
feature writes across a boundary, and a sculk patch spreading through a cave
system does exactly that. `plains` in B improving while everything around it
worsens is the tell that this is spillover and not a systematic bias.

**And `plains` in B improved its way out of being a measurement.** It was 382
against an N=2 floor of 336 — 1.14x, the thinnest quotable row the census
published in that square — and 271 is *below* the amount the two vanilla runs
disagree by. Rule 6 disqualifies it, and rule 6 does not care which direction
the movement was in: a residual under its floor has no resolving power whether
it got there by a port or by a regression. The row is registered unquotable so
the next reader knows the square can no longer adjudicate `plains`, and the
fix for that is more references, not a better port.

**Window E is byte-identical to the census** — every one of its five rows
unchanged to the block — which is the control: E holds no `deep_dark`, so
nothing spills into it. That the control moved by exactly zero is what makes
the other nine attributable to the switch rather than to drift.

Each old row is retired under its own id and each new one registered as
`<id>-sculk`, because a figure this branch's own code no longer reproduces is
the rot ORACLE rule 29 exists to refuse.

### 66.4c Window A cannot close, and window B can — split by block pair

Decomposing each window's `deep_dark` residual into mismatches where **either
side is a sculk block** and mismatches where neither is:

```text
                    residual   sculk-involved   NOT sculk   floor
  deep_dark A         44,180           24,018      20,162  17,695
  deep_dark B         33,499           33,345         154  21,900
```

The two squares are not the same problem.

**Window A's closing criterion is unreachable by any amount of sculk work.**
Its largest single term is `vanilla=air, ours=deepslate` at **17,706**, and
it is pre-existing at position level rather than merely in count: the same
comparison with the spread OFF gives 17,755, and **all 17,706 are a subset of
those 17,755** — the spread removed 49 of them and introduced none. Checked as
a set intersection, not as two totals, because two totals agreeing is the
weaker claim and this branch has already been caught once by an explanation
that fitted the shape of a number and not its contents. It is terrain: vanilla's deep dark has open cavern where ours has
solid rock. Perfect sculk placement would leave A at 20,162, and the criterion
the census set is **17,695**. The target is below the part of the residual that
sculk cannot reach.

**Window B is the square that adjudicates sculk.** 33,345 of its 33,499
mismatches involve a sculk block on one side or the other — 99.5% — and its
criterion of 21,900 needs roughly a 35% improvement in placement, which is the
size of the face-set defect named in §66.5.

> A closing criterion is a statement about a window as much as about a defect.
> Before spending a run on the biome, decompose its residual by block pair and
> check that the target is above the part your item cannot move.

This is not a reason to withdraw the census's criterion for B, and it is a
reason to stop quoting A's. Both were set from an aggregate that had never been
split this way, because with sculk switched off there was nothing to split: the
whole family read as one absent thing.

### 66.5 The next item, and it is already named by a dead hypothesis

`dadbff41` traced one patch's cursors and found them correct: ten cursors
start at the origin with 32 charge, the first converts and the other nine
decline because the block is already sculk. The fault is which face a
spreading vein occupies — ours converts UPWARD where vanilla converts DOWNWARD
from a vein with `down=true` — and that choice lives in `multiface_growth`,
**upstream of every line of sculk code and shared with glow lichen**. Four
hypotheses have died on this feature and each death moved the fault one layer
up; that one is the first pointing outside sculk entirely, and it is where the
remaining ~7,400 missing and ~5,800 extra sculk blocks are.

### 66.6 Ranking, corrected

`large_dripstone` remains the largest feature refusal **by count** anywhere in
this port — 4,569 declines across the three squares, 543/1,977/2,049 — and is
only **fifth by blocks** at 1,593. Both facts stay in one sentence on purpose:
a tally ranked by count is a tally of how often something is *attempted*, and
this is the pair of numbers that shows how a priority list gets written
backwards. Rank by blocks, corroborate by count.

## 76. `large_dripstone` is ported, and vanilla's draw log was aborting — 2026-08-18, branch `feat-worldgen-refused`

Off `sculk-deep-dark` 7547ce61e. Worktree `~/grit/work-feat`. `ci/figures.toml`
ids `*-lgdrip`; §67's "about two draws a tree" is **withdrawn** below.

### `large_dripstone`: 4,569 declines to 0, and thirteen rows moved

The largest feature refusal **by count** anywhere in this port — 543 in window
A, 2,049 in B, 1,977 in E — and only **fifth by blocks** at 1,593. Both halves
belong in any sentence quoting either: a tally ranked by count ranks how often
something is *attempted*, and this feature is attempted 10..48 times per chunk
over the whole vertical column wherever the dripstone-cave placement fires, so
most attempts land in solid rock and place nothing.

`LargeDripstoneFeature`, `LargeDripstone`, `WindOffsetter` and
`LargeDripstoneConfiguration`, from `javap -p -c -constants` on the pinned jar.
Draw sequence: `isEmptyOrWater` guard, `Column.scan` (no draws, needs **both**
ends), `height >= 4` guard, then radius (1), stalactite bluntness and scale
(2), stalagmite bluntness and scale (2), wind speed and angle (2, **only if
both cones qualify**), then one `nextFloat` per accepted column of each cone
and a second when that float is under 0.2.

```text
  win  biome                      ours    floor      x    before
  A  dripstone_caves             9421     1482   6.36   11122
  B  dripstone_caves             8027    11616   0.69   22106   below floor
  E  dripstone_caves            14912     6874   2.17   24970
  A  deep_dark                  44178    17695   2.50   44180
  B  deep_dark                  33350    21900   1.52   33499
  A  birch_forest                9078     4555   1.99    9385
  A  old_growth_birch_forest    16218     1849   8.77   16252
  A  river                       2398      239  10.03    2396   WORSE
  A  meadow                       576      155   3.72     616
  B  sparse_jungle               7352     3108   2.37    7589
  E  sunflower_plains             841      668   1.26    1435
  E  windswept_hills               33       25   1.32     141
  E  swamp                       4488     4228   1.06    4506
```

**Windows J and O did not move by a single block.** Neither square holds a
dripstone cave, so nothing spills into either, and a control that moves by
exactly zero is what separates a port's effect from drift — §66's window-E
argument, made here by two squares.

**Two of the thirteen are not good news.** `river` in A went 2,396 → 2,398: a
port that improves twelve rows and worsens one has worsened one. And
`dripstone_caves` in **B fell from 1.90x its floor to 0.69x**, so window B has
stopped adjudicating that biome under ORACLE rule 6. An improvement that
removes a window is still an improvement; A and E still resolve it at 6.36x and
2.17x.

Three things in the port that are easy to get wrong and change the world:
`moveBackUntilBaseIsInsideStoneAndShrinkRadiusIfNecessary` halves the radius
and **restarts its walk from the original root**, not from where the walk
stopped; the `< 0.2` test widens `nextFloat()` to double and compares against
the double literal; and a stalagmite is cut off at `WORLD_SURFACE_WG`, the
noise stage's fossil, so it stops at the *pre-decoration* surface while a
stalactite has no such limit.

Two latent defects fell out of it. `IntProvider::max_value` returned a clamped
provider's own bound where `ClampedInt.maxInclusive()` is `Math.min` of that
and its source's, and the doc comment asserted the wrong rule; `min_value` did
not exist at all. **The whole shipped datapack contains exactly one clamped
`IntProvider`** — this feature's `column_radius`, clamping 3..16 inside a
source of 3..19 — so both answers agree on every value the game asks for. Right
by data, wrong by construction.

### The instrument §67 said did not exist

> *"What is missing is an instrument: our own draw count is readable through
> `RUSTMC_TRACE_DRAWS` and vanilla's is not."* — §67

**Vanilla's is readable.** `ci/decorate-once.sh … -Ddecorate.draws=<substring>`
has printed `DRAW <n> <method>(<bound>) -> <value>` on stderr since the
`monster_room_deep` work, in exactly the format `RUSTMC_TRACE_DRAWS` prints, so
the two sequences diff line for line. **It was aborting.**

`GenLevel`, this harness's fake `WorldGenLevel`, threw
`UnsupportedOperationException` on `WorldGenLevel.playSound/6` and then on
`levelEvent/3` — and `SculkSpreader$ChargeCursor.update` calls both. So from
the moment `sculk_patch_deep_dark` started generating (§66, the same day), any
`DecorateGolden` run whose neighbourhood contained a deep dark died part way
through.

**That failure does not look like one.** The run writes no JSON, but the draw
trace streams to stderr as it goes, so what survives is a complete-looking log
of every chunk *before* the sculk patch and no sign at all of the ones after
it. A five-centre run of `trees_jungle` reported three chunks and read as "only
three chunks in this window have jungle". After the fix the same command
reports **fifteen** and writes its JSON.

Both are no-ops in the reference and provably so:
`WorldGenRegion.playSound(Entity, BlockPos, SoundEvent, SoundSource, float,
float)` and `levelEvent(Entity, int, BlockPos, int)` both have the body
`0: return`, and `LevelAccessor`'s three-argument `levelEvent` default
delegates to the four-argument one. Enumerated rather than found one at a time:
`SculkSpreader`, `ChargeCursor`, `SculkBlock` and `SculkVeinBlock` together
make exactly five distinct `LevelAccessor` calls and the other three were
already handled.

### WITHDRAWN: the jungle gap is not two draws a tree

§67 localised the jungle residual to "**~2 draws per tree**", from a padding
sweep with a clean minimum at pad=2 (41,671). With the oracle working, that is
refuted.

Sixteen chunk-runs of `trees_jungle` compared line for line against vanilla's,
each aligned to the 3x3 neighbourhood `DecorateGolden` actually decorates.
**Two are byte-identical.** In every other, the first divergence is a tree that
one side places and the other does not — **and it goes both ways**, which no
constant per-tree draw deficit can produce.

The first divergence in chunk (960,-192) decomposes completely, and none of it
is a draw count:

```text
  draw 0-2   count, then in_square -> (15374, ?, -3069)     IDENTICAL
  draw 3-4   two random_selector floats, 2nd entry passes   IDENTICAL
             -> minecraft:jungle_bush is selected on both sides
  vanilla    heightmap OCEAN_FLOOR -> y = 87 ... places it, 1645 draws follow
  ours       heightmap OCEAN_FLOOR -> y = 114 ... would_survive fails, 0 draws
```

Read out of the two worlds at that column with `anvil-probe`:

```text
  y     ours                          vanilla
  86    grass_block                   dirt
  87    air                           jungle_log[axis=y]      <- the bush
  88    air                           oak_leaves[distance=1]
  113   jungle_leaves[distance=6]     air
```

**A mega jungle canopy stands twenty-seven blocks above the ground in our world
and not in vanilla's**, placed by a chunk that decorated earlier, and it lifts
`OCEAN_FLOOR` from 87 to 114. The tree we then fail to place is a
`jungle_bush` — not a mega jungle tree at all. `trees_jungle`'s selector has
five children and the mega jungle tree is one of them.

So the fault is a **cascade whose head is in a neighbouring chunk**, and the
pad sweep's minimum at 2 is what a compensating desync looks like from
downstream: it puts following trees back in step on average without correcting
anything, which is exactly why 41,671 never beat 41,024. **Do not re-run the
padding sweep and do not add draws to a placer.**

### The dark oak family places, and its census overshoots

`dark_oak_trunk_placer` and `dark_oak_foliage_placer` are ported. One pair of
placers is **five trees** — `minecraft:dark_oak`, `dark_oak_leaf_litter`,
`pale_oak`, `pale_oak_bonemeal`, `pale_oak_creaking` — because
`TreeConfig::is_supported` is an AND over every part of a config. The first two
are placeable now; the pale oaks are still refused on `pale_moss`.

```text
  win  biome            ours    floor      x     before
  A  birch_forest       8614     4555   1.89      9078
  A  meadow              390      155   2.52       576
  A  grove              2563     2604   0.98      3362   below floor
```

**Windows B, E, J and O did not move by a single block** — none holds a
`dark_forest` or a `pale_garden`, so four squares of five are the control.

**Neither `dark_forest` nor `pale_garden` can adjudicate this port.** They sit
at 0.67x and 0.52x their floors in A, so `dark_forest` 7,846 → 7,277 and
`pale_garden` 6,435 → 6,523 are movements without a verdict. The block census
is the instrument, and it says the trees place and **overshoot**:

```text
  minecraft:dark_oak_leaves     0 -> 6784   vanilla 6017   +767
  minecraft:dark_oak_log        0 -> 2651   vanilla 2185   +466
  minecraft:pale_oak_leaves     0 ->    0   vanilla 6732   still refused
  minecraft:pale_oak_log        0 ->    0   vanilla 2397   still refused
```

An overshoot and not a shortfall. `minecraft:dark_oak` is refused *elsewhere*
in these squares too — 110 declines of `dark_oak_leaf_litter` in A — so the
trees now placing are not all of them, and there are still more leaves than
vanilla has. Decompose that before adding anything to the placers.

### The `large_dripstone` census disagrees with its own residual in A

Stated both ways rather than only the flattering one, because this is the
`cocoa` shape:

```text
  window A   dripstone_block   10448 -> 10305   vanilla 12033   AWAY
  window A   pointed_dripstone  2539 ->  2213   vanilla  2799   AWAY
  window E   dripstone_block   36076 -> 39655   vanilla 46215   TOWARD, +3579
  window E   pointed_dripstone  8967 ->  8839   vanilla 10200   away, -128
```

Window E holds 4.5x the dripstone-cave volume of A and there the port closes
**35% of the `dripstone_block` gap**. In A the few large dripstones it adds are
outweighed by the pointed-dripstone clusters its draws displace. Both windows'
residuals improved; only one window's census did. Read them together, as the
census lane's own rule says.

### What `large_dripstone` actually did, by block pair

The residual improved in every window that holds the biome and the census
moved *away* from vanilla in A. Decomposing by block pair — `region-differ
diff` already prints this table and it took one command — settles it:

```text
  window E                                     before    after
  dripstone_block -> air                        6,781    2,074    -4,707
  dripstone_block -> deepslate                  5,277    4,282      -995
  deepslate       -> dripstone_block            4,109    2,279    -1,830

  window A
  dripstone_block -> stone                      1,864    2,084      +220
  stone_bricks    -> deepslate                  2,234    2,234         0
  mossy_stone_bricks -> deepslate               1,189    1,189         0
  pale_moss_block -> grass_block                1,553    1,546        -7
```

**In E the port did exactly what porting a missing feature should do**:
"vanilla has dripstone, we have air" falls by 4,707, 69% of it. And the
remaining 4,282 missing / 2,279 extra is a **displacement pair** — the same
signature as §66's sculk face-choice — so what is left in E is
`large_dripstone` placing in the wrong place, not `large_dripstone` failing to
place.

**In A the dripstone term got 220 blocks WORSE while the window's residual fell
15%.** Both are true and neither explains the other: A's improvement came from
the pointed-dripstone clusters realigning once 543 refusals stopped stealing
their draws, and its large dripstones are placed worse than before. A residual
and a census can move opposite ways in the same window, and only the block-pair
table says which half did what.

**Two terms did not move by a single block**, and they are the control:
`stone_bricks -> deepslate` at 2,234 and `mossy_stone_bricks -> deepslate` at
1,189. Those are `ancient_city`, and **3,423 blocks of window A's residual are
a structure nobody has attributed to anything** — bigger than the whole
`dripstone_caves` term in that square. It is not this branch's, and it is not
sculk's either: §66 decomposed A into "sculk-involved" and "not", and this term
is in the second half along with the terrain.

### Sixty-seven of sixty-nine features in a jungle chunk are byte-identical

The cheapest form of the comparison, and the one that should have been run
first: **both sides already report a per-feature draw count for a whole
chunk.** `DecorateGolden`'s vectors carry `"draws": N` per feature, and
`RUSTMC_TRACE_ATTEMPT=minecraft:` makes our decorator print
`ATTEMPT <feature> chunk (x, z) … draws=N` for every one. No draw log, no
alignment, one run each.

```text
  chunk (960,-192)   69 features   67 identical   2 differ
    step 9  idx  7   minecraft:trees_jungle        van   1645   ours   1182
    step 9  idx 11   minecraft:patch_grass_jungle  van   5128   ours   5107

  chunk (957,-195)   70 features   67 identical   3 differ
    step 9  idx  0   minecraft:glow_lichen         van    478   ours    475
    step 9  idx  7   minecraft:trees_jungle        van   1147   ours   1430
    step 9  idx 11   minecraft:patch_grass_jungle  van   5214   ours   5198
```

**Every feature in steps 0 through 8 spends exactly vanilla's draws, in both
chunks.** Ores, carvable decoration, lakes, springs, geodes, the ruined portal,
the whole underground: sixty-odd features, identical. So the jungle residual is
not a chain of upstream refusals paying forward — there is nothing upstream in
these chunks to pay forward.

Three features differ and all three read the *surface*:

* **`glow_lichen`** by 3 draws in one chunk. That is `multiface_growth`, which
  §66 named as its own single next item — the face a spreading vein occupies.
  It is the same defect, seen in the other family that uses that code, and it
  is *upstream of `trees_jungle` in the same step*.
* **`trees_jungle`**, in both, in both directions.
* **`patch_grass_jungle`**, in both, and it runs **after** `trees_jungle` and
  reads what it wrote — a consequence, not a cause.

So the search narrows from "somewhere in the jungle" to **step 9's surface
vegetation, and `multiface_growth` is already implicated in it**. Fix
`multiface_growth` first and re-take this table: it is three commands and it
tells you whether the jungle's remaining term is one defect or two.

The per-feature draw table again, on the pale-garden/dark-forest chunk at the

```text
  chunk (-1056,-672)   77 features   74 identical   3 differ
    step 9  idx 17   minecraft:dark_forest_vegetation  van   2425   ours   3981
    step 9  idx 24   minecraft:trees_birch             van     61   ours     81
    step 9  idx 77   minecraft:patch_leaf_litter       van    199   ours    197
```

**Seventy-four of seventy-seven exact, and the one that diverges causally is the
one this branch's new placers serve.** `trees_birch` and `patch_leaf_litter`
both run after it in the same step and read the world it wrote, so they are
consequences.

`dark_forest_vegetation` is a `random_selector` over seven entries whose
two-thirds case is `dark_oak_leaf_litter`. The `DRAW` diff on this chunk names
the cause exactly, and **it is not the new placers**:

```text
  draw 0..792   IDENTICAL, both sides
  draw 793      van  nextInt(3)  -> 2      ours  nextInt(16) -> 10
  draw 794      van  nextInt(12) -> 11     ours  nextInt(16) ->  5
  draw 795+     the two streams carry the same values, shifted by two
```

`nextInt(3)` then `nextInt(12)` is `AbstractHugeMushroomFeature.getTreeHeight`
— `random.nextInt(3) + 4`, then a `nextInt(12)` — read off the pinned jar.
**`huge_brown_mushroom` and `huge_red_mushroom` are the only members of this
selector this port still declines**, 18 declines of the red one in this window,
and here is one of them in the act: vanilla spends the mushroom's first two
draws and then abandons it on `isValidPosition`, and we spend nothing at all.
That is the census lane's own mechanism — *a refused feature spends no
randomness while vanilla spends the feature's draws* — observed rather than
inferred, with the two bounds naming the class that did it.

The **total** goes the other way, 3,981 against 2,425, and the arithmetic that
reconciles them is the decorators, not the trees. A placed
`dark_oak_leaf_litter` runs two `place_on_ground` decorators at 96 and 150
tries, three draws a try: **738 draws before any provider draw**. So +1,556 in
one chunk is about **two extra placed trees**, not the sixty to ninety a
twenty-draw tree would imply. (This section said sixty to ninety until the
decorator tries were read; the estimate ignored them.) Two extra trees a
dark-forest chunk over the ~15 such chunks in this square is the same order as
the +466 `dark_oak_log` the census reports, which is the first time those two
numbers have agreed.

**So the open item is the huge mushrooms, not the dark oak placers.**
`AbstractHugeMushroomFeature`, `HugeRedMushroomFeature` and
`HugeBrownMushroomFeature` are three classes and they are the last refusal
inside `dark_forest_vegetation`.

### THE SINGLE NEXT ITEM

**`multiface_growth`'s face choice — §66's own next item — and then re-take the
per-feature table above.** It is the only defect implicated *upstream* of
`trees_jungle` inside a chunk whose other sixty-seven features are exact, and
it costs three commands to know whether the jungle's remaining term survives
fixing it. If it does, walk the decoration order for the first chunk whose
`trees_jungle` sequence diverges and decompose that one the way (960,-192) is
decomposed above. The instrument is:

```bash
ci/decorate-once.sh /tmp/j.json -Ddecorate.seed=20260722 \
    -Ddecorate.centers=<cx>,<cz> -Ddecorate.draws=trees_jungle
RUSTMC_DECORATE_ORDER=zx RUSTMC_TRACE_ATTEMPT=trees_jungle \
    RUSTMC_TRACE_DRAWS=trees_jungle RUSTMC_TRACE_ATTEMPT_POS=1 \
    target/release/worldgen-dump full 20260722 1 /tmp/ours <cx> <cz>
```

Compare the two `DRAW` streams; where they part, read `STAGE #3 heightmap`
against the vector's `stageTrace` entry `[3, x, y, z]` and probe the column in
both worlds. **Take the per-feature draw table first, though** — it is one run
each and it ruled out sixty-seven features before a single `DRAW` line was
read. Two chunks of sixteen already agree, so the head is findable.

Second: **`pale_moss`**, which is the whole of `pale_garden`'s 9,129 missing
blocks in window A. `creaking_heart` is ported here; `pale_moss` is refused on
purpose, because three of its four passes are ordinary decorator work and the
fourth places a whole configured feature — `minecraft:pale_moss_patch`, a
`vegetation_patch` this port already implements — from inside a tree
decorator. A decorator holds a `DecoratorWorld` (five block questions);
placing a configured feature needs the feature registry and a `FeatureWorld`,
and threading either down changes `TreeConfig::parse`'s signature and widens
the bound on every decorator. Porting the other three passes and skipping the
patch would be worse than refusing: the patch costs the stream whatever a
`vegetation_patch` costs, so everything after it would land displaced while
`pale_oak` reported success.

Third: the dark oak **overshoot** above, and window A's **`ancient_city`
term** — `stone_bricks` and `mossy_stone_bricks` against `deepslate`, 3,423
blocks that did not move by one under either port on this branch and that no
section has ever attributed. It is larger than that square's entire
`dripstone_caves` term.

## 69. What the gameplay corpus's own checks can be made to say — 2026-08-18, branch `corpus-falsifiability-audit`

`ci/checks/gameplay-falsifiable.toml` reads **108 of 108** and has for some
time. Every layer above it has now been swept and every sweep found the same
thing, so the question was owed to the corpus itself: a ledger that reads 108
of 108 is either a finished job or an instrument that cannot report.

It is neither, exactly. It is an instrument answering a different question from
the one its name implies, and saying so plainly in its own module docstring —
*"axis A finds no live defect in the corpus today. Its value is the ratchet."*
`--sweep` mutates a **recording** and asks whether the comparator noticed.
Every recording has bytes at every step, so mutating those bytes moves the
verdict of very nearly anything. The result is real evidence about the
comparator and no evidence at all about whether this server could produce the
difference.

### 69.1 Three greens wearing one name

A check that stays green when it should not has failed in one of three ways,
and they need three different repairs:

```
GRADES      a real difference makes it red, demonstrated
VACUOUS     nothing it observes can differ            -> widen `observe`
SUBSTRATE   the world it runs in cannot express it    -> change the rig
UNVISITED   the code path it targets is never run     -> add a step
```

The four instances that motivated this section were each found by hand, one at
a time, and none by the sweep: `710`'s daylight detector agrees only because
the superflat measures `power = 0` on **both** sides; `360` flips its lever
once, so the lamp's four-tick unlight is executed by nothing; `400` was green
while its lamp was a direct neighbour of its lever, a check that cannot tell
one `updateNeighborsAt` call from two; and `power.rs`'s `redstone: no ported`
fires zero times across 59 whole-run logs.

### 69.2 The counterfactual has to be a server, not a byte

`ci/corpus-grades.py` asks the question against
`crates/rustmc-server/src/sabotage.rs` — eight subsystems replaced with the
not-yet-written versions they grew out of. Each control is the server's own
no-op answer rather than an injected value: `state_for_placement` returns
`Some(default)`, which is already its answer for a block with no placement
rule; `use_without_item` returns `Pass`, which is what it did before the table
existed; `updateNeighborsAt` visits nobody; a scheduled tick never comes due;
`setPlacedBy` and `playerWillDestroy` write no second block; the block entity
is created and never described; the screen never opens; the container click
changes nothing.

Controls are armed **by workspace**. `record.rs` pins scenario *n* to absolute
`x = -(n + 1) * 32` so that position-dependent packet order is comparable
between servers, and that pinning is also an address — so one corpus run
carries as many independent controls as there are scenarios, which is what
makes this affordable at a budget of one recording.

The firing counter is half the instrument. `fired = 0` on an armed control is
the `UNVISITED` verdict outright: the scenario's steps do not reach the code,
so no implementation of it could have moved the recording.

### 69.3 `strict` is reported and not gated, and counting it was a bug

`ci/corpus-grades-falsify.sh` builds a check that reads only
`block_changed_ack` — the sequence acknowledgement every server sends whatever
it did with the block — and asserts the reading is `VACUOUS`. It came back
`GRADES`.

Nothing about the check had moved. `strict` had: the corpus's second lens,
keeping `observe_from` and dropping the `observe` kind list, so it sees
differences the check declared it was not looking at.
`ci/selfcheck-aggregate.py` says it in as many words and `ci/t2-gameplay.sh`
never mentions it. **A scenario whose strict reading moves and whose declared
reading does not has not been shown falsifiable — nothing would have gone
red.** It has been shown that the corpus recorded a real difference and this
check does not read it, which is the definition of `VACUOUS`.

### 69.4 Sixty-four recordings were already on the box

`ci/corpus-history.py` needs no lock, no server and no vanilla boot. Every gate
directory on this box holds a recording of our server taken against a different
build; hold the reference fixed, swap the subject across all 64, and each
check's report signature becomes a time series over real code.

```
moved under the reading the gate acts on   41
moved ONLY under the ungated strict lens    6
frozen across every build                  61
```

The six are `a-lever-lights-a-lamp`, `lever-flips-when-right-clicked`,
`button-unpresses-itself`, `a-wooden-button-stays-pressed-longer`,
`a-block-in-hand-does-not-stop-a-lever-flipping` and
`other-player-is-an-entity`. Each is `match` in all 64 recordings. A real build
difference reached the corpus and the check did not read it.

**Frozen is a screen and not a verdict**, and saying otherwise would be the
same error in the other direction: a check can be frozen because this server
has been right about it since before the oldest recording on the box. The 61
are candidates for `ci/corpus-grades.py`, which is what settles them.

### 69.5 The ledger's own ratchet compared a number to itself

Asked what else the sweep writes that nobody reads, after the `MERGE-REGION`
deletion:

* **`dead_fields` could not fire.** `--check` read `dead_fields` out of
  `[meta]` and compared it against `len(dead_field)` — both written by the same
  `write_ledger` call in the same sweep run, equal by construction. The refusal
  it advertises, *"a field was added that couples to no verdict"*, was reachable
  only by hand-editing the ledger, which the ledger's own header forbids.
  `floor` and `weak_floor` are not of this shape: both recount from the
  scenario **files**. A dead field has no counterpart outside the ledger, so
  the counterpart is now in the script, where `MAX_UNSWEPT` already is.

  The selftest had noticed and worked around it: its case built a failure *"by
  lowering the recorded ceiling under the recorded population"*, which tests a
  hand-edit rather than a sweep.

* **`field_universe` had no consumer at all.** Written into `[meta]` and read
  by nothing in the tree. §27's *"4 of 84 `(kind, field)` pairs are read by no
  check"* is quoted against it, and the ledger says **90**.

* **`write_ledger` still deletes the `MERGE-REGION` marker**, so a swept ledger
  gets `ci/merge-docregions.py`'s refusals and none of its resolutions.

### 69.6 What a green under this instrument does not prove

The controls are eight subsystems, not every way an implementation can be
wrong, so `GRADES` is a positive control and not a proof of completeness. The
other three verdicts are the strong ones: each names a difference the check
demonstrably cannot see.

The verdict is also **per check**, and a check can carry more than one claim.
`710` claims that the click cycles `inverted` and that `updateSignalStrength`
then recomputes `power`; removing `useWithoutItem` reddens it, so it grades —
and half its claim still cannot be falsified, because the substrate reads
`power = 0` on both sides whatever recomputes it. So a second reading runs
beside the first over the same pair of recordings: every block-state property a
check's projection carries, and whether any armed control moves its value. A
property no wrong implementation can shift is a property the check names and
cannot grade.

### 69.7 What the comparator already closes, and the one question it does not ask

Three of the four words above already mean something else here, and reading
them first is the difference between a finding and a rediscovery.
`compare::Verdict` carries `Vacuous` — the *reference* said nothing at all;
`Inert` — the reference spoke and said only what the scenario's own actions
force, the acknowledgement and the `handleUseItemOn` resyncs at the clicked
positions, **and the subject said the same**; and `Mute` — both sides silent at
the *measured step* while the scenario as a whole is informative.
`ci/t2-gameplay.sh` refuses all three and `gameplay-baseline.toml` may not
bless any of them.

`Inert` is the self-echo detector, which is the shape `400` had when its lamp
was a direct neighbour of its lever, and `Mute` is what caught
`607-container-click-pickup-all-gathers-matching-stacks` — `match` with seven
observations a side, every one of them from steps 0..5, its step-6 click
producing a `packet:0x60` the check does not name. That check was green
whatever `crates/rustmc-server/src/click.rs` did.

**What the three have in common is that each asks what the recording says.** A
check can be none of them and still be unable to go red, because the question
none of them asks is the counterfactual: could a different implementation have
made the recording say something else? A daylight detector on a superflat reads
`power = 0` under any implementation of `updateSignalStrength`, and a lamp
whose lever is flipped once never reaches the code that unlights it. Neither is
vacuous, inert or mute — both recordings are full of real content that really
did come from the mechanic — and that is the whole of the gap §69 is about.

## 94. One entity-behaviour gap is what a marker census can see; the hierarchy behind it declares 3,870 methods — 2026-08-19, branch `mobs-tick-surface`

`ci/unported-inventory.py --open` finds **exactly one** entity-behaviour gap in
the whole server — `entities.rs:19`, "per-kind entity behaviour not written" —
reached by one scenario. Mobs are one of the largest behavioural surfaces in
the game, so either this server implements nearly all of it or the inventory
cannot see the shape of what is missing.

It is the second, and the reason is structural rather than a defect in the
inventory. **Nothing was ported on this branch. The finding is the
deliverable.**

### 94.1 Why one marker is the most a marker census could have found

A marker needs a host line. It is written *inside* the module that implements
the surrounding mechanic, by the person who implemented it, at the point they
declined to go further. `power.rs` carries redstone's markers because
`power.rs` is 164 KB of ported redstone. A subsystem with **no module at all**
carries however many paragraphs a neighbouring module's author chose to write
about it.

For mobs that is one paragraph, in `entities.rs`'s module doc. `entities.rs:19`
is not even the sentence — it is the heading `# What is here and what is
deliberately not`, matched on the words "deliberately not"; the gap is a clause
three lines below it.

So the inventory's resolution on a subsystem is bounded by how much of that
subsystem is **written**, not by how much is **missing**. That is what a marker
census is, and it means the direction the audit was walking cannot see an
absent subsystem at all.

**Measured rather than argued, by `ci/marker-density.py` over the audit's own
scan root under the audit's own regex: pearson r(lines, markers) = 0.760 across
58 files, permutation p = 0.0001 over 10,000 re-pairings.** The re-count
reproduces the audit's 85 markers exactly. The objection "bigger files have
more of everything" is the finding restated — an instrument whose output is
predicted by how much code exists is measuring how much code exists, and its
number moves when somebody *writes* a module rather than when somebody fails
to. 29 of the 58 files carry no marker at all, across 13,988 lines; they are
not this server's 29 debt-free modules.

Three further consequences, all measured:

* **the scan root is `crates/rustmc-server/src` and nothing else.** Under the
  audit's own regex the workspace carries markers outside it —
  `rustmc-behavior` 9, `rustmc-entity` 4, `rustmc-data` 3, `tools/` 31 (and
  `rustmc-worldgen` 94, owned elsewhere). `rustmc-entity/src/lib.rs` writes the
  same gap out at length — "There is no per-kind behaviour here yet, on
  purpose" — and the inventory cannot see it;
* **the cleanest instance is inside the scan root, which is the harder place
  to notice.** `crates/rustmc-server/src/tick.rs` lines 37-53 are a doc block
  headed *"And what does not tick, which is the more useful half"*. It names
  ten absent mechanics — random ticks, entity motion, `EntityTickList` order,
  the `tickNonPassenger`/`tickPassenger` body, mob AI, mob spawning,
  `checkDespawn`, item merging and pickup, fluid ticks, the block-entity
  tickers. **The audit's regex matches exactly one line in that range**, and
  one in the whole file: bullet 1, on the words "deliberately not". The other
  nine mechanics use no refusal keyword, so the inventory sees `tick.rs` as a
  file with a single random-tick gap. The ten is a hand count and is labelled
  as one; the one is mechanical, and it is the load-bearing half;
* **the second entity gap has no marker at all.** `SpawnEggItem` is unported;
  `crates/rustmc-server/src` contains no occurrence of `spawn_egg` or
  `SpawnEggItem`. There is no line declining to implement it because there is
  no code where such a line would go. The audit's own §"THE MARKER SET IS A
  LOWER BOUND" predicted exactly this shape with `item.rs:32`, and this is a
  harder instance: `item.rs:32` at least had prose.

### 94.2 The size of the thing that one row stands for

Derived by `ci/mob-tick-census.py` from the pinned jar, none of it typed in,
all of it pinned in `ci/checks/mob-surface.json` and gated by `--check`:

| | |
|---|---|
| entity types registered | 158 |
| — `MobCategory.MISC` | 72 |
| — in a spawning category | 86 |
| subtypes of `Mob` | 114 |
| classes in the `Mob` hierarchy | 115 |
| **method declarations in it** | **3,870** |
| distinct signatures | 1,548 |
| signatures two or more classes declare | 371 |
| a mob tick enters, in `ai/**` | 1,754 methods across 240 classes |
| a mob tick enters, in `level/pathfinder/` | 164 methods across 14 classes |

and the per-kind hooks the marker literally names: **54** classes declare their
own `registerGoals`, **39** their own `aiStep`, **39** their own `tick`, **38**
their own `customServerAiStep`, **59** their own `finalizeSpawn`, **41** their
own `mobInteract`, **18** their own `createNavigation`.

`Mob.serverAiStep` is eight subsystems in one method, read from the bytecode:
`Sensing.tick`, `GoalSelector.tick`, `GoalSelector.tickRunningGoals`,
`PathNavigation.tick`, `customServerAiStep`, `MoveControl.tick`,
`LookControl.tick`, `JumpControl.tick`. The workspace contains **zero**
occurrences of `GoalSelector`, `NaturalSpawner`, `PathNavigation` or
`registerGoals` in any form.

**And one constraint out of that method that a porter has to know before
choosing a data layout.** The goal lists are fully re-evaluated only when
`(tickCount + getId()) % 2 == 0`, or on a mob's first two ticks; otherwise
only the already-running goals tick. The `getId()` term is a stagger, so
**entity id allocation order is behaviour-visible** — which mob re-picks its
goals on which tick is a function of the id it was handed.
`crates/rustmc-entity/src/lib.rs` already records that vanilla's tick *order*
is observable and freezes an `EntityId`-sorted query order for that reason;
this says the id itself is observable too, through a path no single packet
shows. The full transcription with offsets is in
`docs/cold-start/mob-tick-surface.md`.

**Ours: three `EntityKind` constants, `PLAYER`, `ITEM` and `FALLING_BLOCK`.**
(Two until `2313ff73c` on `stack-gameplay` ported the block half of a gravity
block; `ci/mob-tick-census.py` reddened on the re-pin the same commit owed it,
which is that gate working.) The intersection with the jar's 86
spawning-category types is **still empty** — none of the three is a mob, and
`our_mob_kinds` is still 0 — so no mob can exist in this server and every mob
mechanic is unreachable **by construction** rather than by omission, which is a
stronger and more checkable statement than "not ported" and the one the census
gates on. **What changed underneath that sentence is the reason for it.** Since
main `f4fa28ff8` the workspace *does* carry `GoalSelector`, `PathNavigation`,
`registerGoals` and `serverAiStep` — `mobs-goals` landed the goal system and
the pathfinder in `crates/rustmc-entity/src/ai` — so "unreachable by
construction" no longer means "the code does not exist". It means the code
exists and nothing can be spawned into it: `NaturalSpawner`, `SpawnEggItem` and
`spawn_egg` are still zero occurrences across the workspace, and that is now
the whole of the gap.

The unrestricted call-graph closure from the mob tick roots is 24,251 of the
jar's 53,685 methods. It is **not** quoted as a finding: devirtualisation makes
it most of the jar, so it measures the approximation and not the mob.

### 94.3 The one scenario that reaches the gap cannot grade it

`080-spawn-egg-makes-a-mob` declares `observe = ["add_entity",
"set_entity_data"]` — the mob's **announcement**. Everything the mob then does
travels on `move_entity`, `move_entity_rot`, `move_entity_heartbeat`,
`entity_position`, `set_entity_motion` and `rotate_head`, and every one of
those is dropped before the two servers are compared.

Measured over **N = 17 distinct** vanilla recordings — 22
`~/rustmc*/oracle-work/gameplay*/vanilla.json` files hold them, and **counting
files overcounts N by 29%**: the reference cache serves one recording to
several trees, and copied trees carry older ones. De-duplicated on the sha256
of the scenario's own recorded block:

| | |
|---|---|
| vanilla emitted | 29..150 observations, **15 distinct counts in 17 runs** |
| the check compares | **6..6** |
| behaviour channels emitted | 10..104 |
| behaviour channels compared | **0** |

**The check is stable precisely because it cannot see the mob.** Six in twenty
runs of twenty, while the thing it is nominally about swings by a factor of
five. That range is one server disagreeing with itself across runs and is not a
divergence — the same distinction `551` was retracted on.

Derived from the tree, not asserted: **exactly one** of the 108 loaded checks
can put a mob in the world; **four** observe a behaviour channel; the
intersection is **empty**. The four are `other-player-is-an-entity`,
`dropping-an-item-throws-it-on-the-floor`,
`a-standing-player-is-rebroadcast-on-a-timer` and
`a-player-that-leaves-the-ground-is-resynced` — every one about a player or an
item, which are the only two entity kinds this server has.

### 94.4 The audit's reach column for this row is wrong in both halves

`ci/unported-inventory.py` files `entities.rs:19` under "reached, and the
divergence would be visible today", noting *the entity exists and is tracked;
it does nothing*. Over **N = 21** `report.json` files on this box, two of them taken after this branch existed:

| | |
|---|---|
| declared verdict | `absent`, **21/21** |
| strict verdict | `diverge`, 21/21 |
| `reference_obs` | 6 |
| `subject_obs` | **0** |
| missing kinds | `add_entity`, `set_entity_data`, 21/21 |

`subject_obs = 0` in every run: the entity does not exist and is not tracked.
What is red today is the **announcement** — a different gap, the one with no
marker. The gap the row names is per-kind behaviour, and no verdict this check
can return is about it. The row belongs in "reached but invisible", the column
the audit itself calls the worst of the three.

It is a worse instance than `710`. `710` is green over a dead path and would go
red the day a check ran at a sun angle that resolves. `080` **can never go
green either**: it is in `ci/checks/gameplay-floor.toml` at 15 flaps of 15 pairs
over 6 runs — vanilla disagreeing with *itself* about the mob's spawn yaw — and
the yaw rides on `add_entity`, inside the projection. So the check cannot grade
the behaviour it is filed against and cannot pass on the announcement it does
grade. It is not a signal in either direction.

### 94.5 The substrate, and what it makes unmeasurable

`ci/t2-gameplay.sh` boots `minecraft:flat` with `gamemode=creative`,
`difficulty=peaceful`, `spawn-monsters=false`, `spawn-radius=0`,
`generate-structures=false`, and the game rules `advance_time=false`,
`spawn_mobs=false`, `random_tick_speed=0`, `advance_weather=false`.

Its own comment says "`difficulty=peaceful` is not tidiness, it is the
substrate", and gives the reason: superflat is full of slimes, one scenario
recorded 32 sound observations that had nothing to do with it. What it does not
say is the cost, and the cost is this lane's whole subject. Read out of the jar
by `ci/mob-substrate.py`:

* **38 of the 158 registrations are built `.notInPeaceful()`**, every one
  `MobCategory.MONSTER` — 38 of the 86 spawning-category types. Of the 45
  MONSTER types, **7 survive peaceful**: `camel_husk`, `ender_dragon`,
  `piglin`, `shulker`, `sulfur_cube`, `zombie_horse`, `zombie_nautilus`.
* Those 38 cannot enter this world **at all**, and that rests on three call
  sites read individually rather than on the call graph, which
  over-approximates: `SpawnEggItem.useOn` and `SpawnEggItem.use` call
  `EntityType.canSpawn`, whose body is `isAllowedInPeaceful() || difficulty !=
  PEACEFUL`; `SummonCommand.createEntity` does not use `canSpawn` at all — it
  reads the difficulty and `isAllowedInPeaceful()` itself and **throws**, so
  `/summon` is refused with a message; and `Mob.checkDespawn` discards such a
  mob *before* the entity-ticking range gate, so a fourth route would not
  survive a tick.
* Natural spawning is off **three times over**: peaceful, `spawn-monsters=false`
  (which feeds `ServerChunkCache.spawnEnemies`, read by
  `NaturalSpawner.getFilteredSpawningCategories`), and the `spawn_mobs` game
  rule (read by `NaturalSpawner` and `ServerChunkCache` both).

So **no spawn-selection mechanic is measurable by this corpus as it stands**,
and a check written against the default substrate would be vacuous by
construction rather than by omission. That is `710`'s failure mode arrived at
from the world rather than from the projection, and it is the trap a mob lane
walks into first.

### 94.5.1 But the substrate is not the binding constraint, and saying so was half a finding

Two corrections to the paragraph above, both from work already on `main` that
this lane found after writing it. **`origin/corpus-dark-systems` got here on
2026-08-12 and the honest thing is to point at it rather than re-derive it.**

* **Peaceful does not empty the world.** 86 spawning types minus the 38
  `.notInPeaceful()` ones leaves **48 that spawn perfectly well in a peaceful
  superflat**, and that branch measured them: with `spawn_mobs` lifted for one
  scenario's window, **8 to 21 `add_entity` per eight-second window**, 113..531
  observations, different types and positions every run.
* **The suppression is liftable, per scenario.** `[[gamerule]]` in a check
  applies a rule down the reference's console fifo after the rig is quiet and
  restores it after the settle window, so the effect lands inside the measured
  window. `780-random-ticks-turn-covered-grass-to-dirt` is the check that
  exists because of it.

So the substrate is a wall with a door in it, and the door was tried.
`spawn_mobs` came back **NULL — 15/15 pairs over 6 runs, 6 distinct
projections.** Not hard: *unmeasurable*.

**And the cause is two fields on two packets — see §94.9, which corrects this
paragraph's first draft.** The first is the one every prior branch has named:
`EntityType.create` draws the spawn yaw at **offset 103** —
`ServerLevel.getRandom().nextFloat()`, times `360.0f`, straight into
`Entity.snapTo` fifteen instructions later. That generator is unseeded. The
same draw is why:

* `spawn-egg-makes-a-mob` flaps 15/15 pairs in `ci/checks/gameplay-floor.toml`
  and can never reach `match`;
* natural spawning is a null with numbers rather than an open work item;
* **the whole corpus floor is entity-shaped** — all four names in the standing
  4-of-92 floor are entity scenarios, which `origin/entity-parity` established
  and nobody had joined to the other two.

Three separately-recorded facts, one unseeded field between them. That changes
what the next lane should try: **the substrate is not what stands between this
project and spawn parity**, and lifting it buys nothing. What stands there is
that vanilla does not agree with itself about where a mob faces, on the packet
a check would have to compare.

### 94.9 The projection search, and the second draw nobody had named

`ci/mob-projection-search.py` applies each candidate projection to every
recording already on disk and compares runs **pairwise**, so it measures
vanilla against itself and boots nothing. Sixteen distinct recordings on one
recorder schema — one of the 17 uses an older `add_entity` decoder and mixing
it in makes every row read ~74% stable when the truth is 0% or 100% — giving
**120 pairs**:

| projection | pairs identical | |
|---|---|---|
| `observe` as declared | **0/120** | 0.0% |
| `observe`, minus `y_rot` + `y_head_rot` | 34/120 | 28.3% |
| `observe`, minus `y_rot` + `y_head_rot` + `rest` | **120/120** | 100.0% |
| `{add_entity}` alone | 1/120 | 0.8% |
| **`{add_entity}` minus `y_rot` + `y_head_rot`** | **120/120** | **100.0%** |
| `{set_entity_data}` alone | 34/120 | 28.3% |
| `{update_attributes}` alone | **120/120** | 100.0% |

**`080` as declared is 0 of 120.** Not mostly unstable — vanilla never once
agreed with itself over the whole population. And **the announcement minus the
two yaw fields is exact across every pair**: position, kind id, `data`,
`x_rot` and the encoded remainder already match across sixteen cold servers.
So the mob announcement is measurable, and a countable number of fields stand
in the way.

**That number is two, not one, and the second is new.** `set_entity_data` is
independent of the yaw — which is what the 28.3% row means — and the bytecode
says why:

    Pig.finalizeSpawn -> PigSoundVariants.pickRandomSoundVariant(
                             registryAccess(), level.getRandom())
                      -> Registry.getRandom(RandomSource) -> setSoundVariant

a uniform pick over `minecraft:pig_sound_variant`, three entries in the shipped
jar: `big`, `classic`, `mini`. It lands in synched data and so on the wire.

**Every unseeded draw a spawned pig makes, and which reach a client.** Read
from the jar, then checked against the recordings in that order — because the
last inference was wrong, which is the useful part:

| draw | call site | packet | on the wire? |
|---|---|---|---|
| spawn yaw | `EntityType.create` @103, `nextFloat() * 360.0f` | `add_entity` | **yes** |
| sound variant | `Pig.finalizeSpawn` -> `PigSoundVariants.pickRandomSoundVariant` -> `Registry.getRandom` | `set_entity_data` | **yes** |
| left-handed | `Mob.finalizeSpawn` -> `nextFloat()` -> `setLeftHanded` | `set_entity_data` | **yes** |
| age | `AgeableMob.finalizeSpawn` -> `nextFloat()` -> `setAge` | `set_entity_data` | **yes** |
| follow-range bonus | `Mob.finalizeSpawn` -> `triangle(0.0, 0.11228)` on `FOLLOW_RANGE` | `update_attributes` | **NO** |

**The last row is the one worth the space.** A continuous `triangle` draw into
an attribute modifier looks like the worst case there is — a real-valued
divergence on a packet the corpus already records — and it is not a case at
all: `{update_attributes}` alone is **120/120 identical**. The jar says why.
`Attributes`' static initialiser registers `FLYING_SPEED` through
`RangedAttribute.setSyncable(true)` at offsets 420-424 and registers
`FOLLOW_RANGE` at 430-451 **with no `setSyncable` call**, so it keeps the
default and `isClientSyncable()` is false. The draw happens on every spawn and
no client is ever told.

A divergence in the server is not a divergence on the wire, and only the
measurement could say which this was. The bytecode said "unseeded draw"; the
recordings said "exact in every pair"; the bytecode then said why.

The three that do reach `set_entity_data` are consistent with what is measured
there — 5 distinct payloads over 16 runs at 8/3/3/1/1 reads as three sound
variants with two rarer left-handed ones beside them, `setLeftHanded` being a
5% draw whose expectation over 16 runs is 0.8. **Consistent with, not proven**:
the recorded field is a digest, so the decomposition is inference and is
labelled as one.

None of this argues for a field exemption. `origin/entity-parity` ruled out a
type-keyed yaw exemption twice and the reason survives — a pig's yaw is random
only on the `EntityType.create` path and the wire does not carry which path
spawned it, so an exemption blinds every other path. What this adds is the
**cost side of that decision, measured**: exempting the two yaw fields takes
the announcement from 0/120 to 120/120, and without a second, separate decision
about `set_entity_data` it takes `080` to 28.3% and no further.

This is not an argument for changing the substrate. Peaceful is load-bearing,
and `origin/survival-substrate` is a whole branch on how expensive moving one
of these settings is. It is an argument for saying so before anyone reports a
spawn figure. `ci/mob-substrate.py --check` refuses if the substrate moves,
because every finding in this section is conditional on it.

### 94.6 The positive controls, all of them

Three instruments, three gates, three falsifiers, and every one of them exists
because its headline is a **zero** or an **absence** — the readings that a
broken reader and a correct one produce identically.

* **`ci/mob-tick-census.py`** refuses before printing anything if it cannot
  find `PLAYER` and `ITEM` in `entities.rs` **and** match both to real jar
  registrations. `ci/mob-tick-census-falsify.sh` corrupts each name in turn and
  asserts exit 3 with nothing on stdout; asserts a cold re-derivation agrees
  with the cache figure for figure, so a warm cache cannot answer for a dead
  parser; and asserts that appending a mob `EntityKind` moves `our_mob_kinds`
  0 → 1, which is why the intersection is computed against the jar's own
  registrations rather than a hand-written list of mob names.
* **`ci/mob-observability.py`** gates that every mob-bearing check has a
  blindness-ledger entry. `ci/mob-observability-falsify.sh` asserts a new
  spawn-egg check is refused, a `summon` check is refused, **and a check that
  makes no mob is not** — that negative control is what gives the other two
  content, since a detector firing on everything would pass both for free. It
  also asserts the behaviour classifier is live by emptying the channel set and
  requiring the count of behaviour-observing checks to fall to 0.
* **`ci/mob-substrate.py`** refuses if it parses fewer than three properties,
  fewer than three game rules, fewer than 100 entity registrations, or **zero**
  `.notInPeaceful()` types. A substrate reader that reads nothing reports a
  world with no suppressions — the sentence "spawning is measurable here",
  which is false and would be believed. `ci/mob-substrate-falsify.sh` asserts
  an unrelated comment appended to `ci/t2-gameplay.sh` is **not** refused, so
  the check reads the substrate rather than hashing the file.

### 94.7 What this lane deliberately did not do

* **No reach widening.** `origin/entity-parity` established that 88 of the
  jar's types are one `hold` away and that reaching them buys nothing — every
  one lands on `EntityType.create` offsets 103-115, an unseeded yaw draw — so
  reaching them adds unstable rows and zero parity.
* **No mob port.** Every mob mechanic is downstream of a `Mob` instance
  existing, and under this substrate the only measurable mob would be a
  peaceful-legal one whose behaviour no check observes. A goal, a navigator or
  a spawn rule written now would be verified by nothing, and
  `docs/AGENT-BRIEF.md` names an approximate pathfinder as the one-way door
  this project must not walk through. Defer verification, never fidelity —
  here the verification is not available yet, so the fidelity work waits.
* **No touch of `add_entity.movement`**, which is a projection drop being
  reclassified on a sibling lane.

### 94.8 What the next lane needs, in order

1. **`SpawnEggItem`**, because it is the only route by which a mob can enter
   this world today and it is the gap with no marker. It does not need the AI:
   `EntityType.canSpawn`, the peaceful gate, and the `add_entity` /
   `set_entity_data` announcement are the whole of it. It moves `080` from
   `absent` to `diverge` and **not** to `match` — the yaw floor is unmovable —
   so it must not be sold as closing the check.
2. **A behaviour channel in some mob check's `observe`**, or mob behaviour
   stays ungraded however much is ported. `ci/checks/mob-blind.toml` is the
   ledger that keeps that visible, and the check that adds one has to survive
   a projection whose vanilla side spans 29..150 observations — which is a
   scenario-design problem before it is a porting one.
3. **The entity tick loop body** in `crates/rustmc-entity/src/tick.rs`, which
   is already written down as a trait with every gate vanilla consults as a
   method, and is unimplemented because none of those gates exists yet.
   `Mob.checkDespawn` is the first, it is fully read in this branch's
   instruments, and it runs before the range gate.

## 101. Entity id allocation is behaviour-visible, and it is one of four order-keyed surfaces — 2026-08-19, branch `entid-alloc-order`

§94 found, in passing and without acting on it, that `Mob.serverAiStep` gates
its goal phase on `(tickCount + getId()) % 2`. That makes **entity id
allocation order behaviour-visible**: two servers that hand out ids in a
different order run goals on opposite ticks and nothing about the entity's own
state says so.

This lane establishes what vanilla's allocator actually is, reduces the
requirement to its real size, finds every other place in the jar where an
observable behaviour is keyed on an order rather than on state, and says for
each one whether vanilla agrees with **itself** about it. **Nothing was
ported.** Four checks and their falsifiers are the deliverable, and one of
them returns a verdict this project did not previously have a word for.

### 101.1 The allocator is not where every note in this tree said it was

`Entity.ENTITY_COUNTER` does not exist in 26.2. `entities.rs`'s own doc
comment named it, and it was wrong. `Entity`'s constructor calls
`Level.getNextEntityId()`; the base `Level` returns `0`; `ServerLevel`
overrides it:

```java
int i = 0;
while (i == 0 || this.chunkSource.hasEntityWithId(i))
    i = ENTITY_COUNTER.incrementAndGet();
return i;
```

`ENTITY_COUNTER` is a `private static final AtomicInteger` on `ServerLevel`,
built no-arg, so the first id in a session is 1. `Entity.getId` throws
`Tried to access entity ID before ID assignment` on a zero id, so 0 is a
tripwire and not merely unused. Three classes in the jar reference the
allocator; exactly one references the counter. That is the whole surface, and
`ci/entity-id-allocator.py` reads twelve properties of it.

**Two differences from ours are real and both are recorded rather than
fixed.** The skip-if-live retry is unreachable under a monotonic counter until
it wraps at 2^31. The other is not so comfortable: **vanilla draws the id in
`Entity.<init>`**, so an entity it constructs and then throws away still burns
a number — and `PlayerList.respawn` is exactly that, building a second
`ServerPlayer`, drawing an id for it, then stamping the old id over it with
`setId`. We have no respawn. Whoever writes one must burn an id or every
entity created afterwards carries the opposite parity to vanilla's.

### 101.2 The requirement is one bit, which is the useful part

`% 2` reads a single bit. The requirement is not "allocate the same ids", it
