## 74. The two things the exclusivity result does not license

`docs/CORPUS-LOCK-HOLD.md` §15 refuted the corpus lock's founding evidence and
bounded the cost of concurrency at **1.3%**. Its own recommendation named two
things it had not measured and one it had priced with a shrug. This section is
those three, and the detail lives in `docs/CORPUS-LOCK-HOLD.md` §§17-26.

### The three answers, before the reasoning

| question | answer |
|---|---|
| Does integrity hold at the full 108 scenarios? | **Yes.** The concurrent arm's full-corpus floor **is** the serial full-corpus floor. The one scenario that looked concurrent-only is an artefact of unequal sample size, shown three ways, decisively by a purely serial six-run ensemble from 2026-08-13 producing the identical five-scenario set. Corpus-wide resolving power **0.461%** against §16's 2.313% |
| Was the 50-110 load band entered? | **Yes, at 62.8**, from 40 `nice 19` workers on half the box; the top was not reached. A corpus recording inside the band runs at **0.86** of its quiet rate, so §15 was right to refuse to force it |
| **What does relaxing exclusivity cost in falsifier work?** | **25 cases to write or rewrite: 19 of the 33 that exist, plus 6 that cannot exist today.** NOT 47 — that figure counted `ok` assertions across two control runs, not cases |

**Neither answer overturns §15's 1.3%.** The full-corpus rate for K=3 is
**1.007x**, and its bias points against concurrency because twelve minutes of
deliberate load landed inside the concurrent arm and not its control.

### 74.1 Integrity at the full corpus, not at eight scenarios

§16's integrity floor was 0/8 in both arms over an **eight-check subset**, and
it said so: "a longer run holds more world state and more chunks, and a
divergence that only appears deep into a corpus would not show here."

`ci/corpus-integrity-108.sh` runs the same comparison over all **108**
scenarios, driving `ci/t2-gameplay-selfcheck.sh` (the reference recording only,
which is the branch-invariant half §2 established and the half §16 measured, at
about 22 minutes a recording instead of the 45 a subject recording adds). Arms
alternate at block granularity, the serial arm rotates trees, every tree gets a
private `RUSTMC_CORPUS_LOCK_DIR` and a port base at 27600 and above, and **no
run takes a slot in the production queue**.

It also closes §16's other stated limit. §16's sixteen recordings came from
sixteen trees with sixteen recorder identities and it refused to promote its
floor for that reason; the three scratch trees here carry a byte-identical
`oracle-runner`, so **every recording in both arms is from one recorder**,
`rec:706159cd67984eb2`.

### 74.2 The 50-110 load band, entered rather than waited for

§15 declined to force the band and gave the right reason: a live production
recording held the lock, and loading the box would have inflicted §14's
`settle`-cap contamination on somebody else's merge.

**That reason is a scheduling constraint and this box does not offer a window to
schedule into.** At 13:09 on 2026-08-18 the lock was held with four runs queued,
the oldest waiting 211 minutes. So the window is constructed: the load and both
arms run at `nice 19` (CFS positions are relative, so the contention is real for
the arms and about 1/68 of it reaches a `nice 0` production recording), pinned
with `taskset` to half the box so the scheduler always has twelve CPUs the
experiment cannot touch, and **the production holder's own runqueue delay is
sampled throughout**. `ci/corpus-holder-rate.sh` reads `schedstat` field 2, the
nanoseconds a process spent runnable and not running, which is the one quantity
background load moves and idleness does not, so a recording asleep in a `settle`
wait and one starved of CPU are finally distinguishable. §15 argued the risk;
this measures it, and aborts the load if it appears.

### 74.3 The falsifier rework, as a number

§15 priced it as "47 cases assert exclusion directly" and "cases 2, 3 and 6
invert". **47 is the suite's count of `ok` assertions across two control runs,
not a count of cases**, and case 4 inverts as well. `ci/corpus-exclusion-cost.sh`
carries the classification as a table, checks it against both suites, and
refuses to print a tally if a case is unclassified or a classified case has
disappeared:

| | |
|---|---:|
| existing cases across both falsifiers | **33** |
| assertion false by construction (needs a new property) | 12 |
| assertion stands, setup no longer creates contention | 5 |
| assertion stands, target moves to a slot array | 2 |
| unchanged | 14 |
| **cases needing work** | **19** |
| new cases required, no coverage today | 2 |
| new injections required, no coverage today | 4 |
| **total to write or rewrite** | **25** |

All 19 existing injections stay. The half a "rework" estimate omits is the new
half: a lock that admits N+1 and a slot that leaks are failure modes that cannot
exist under a mutex, so nothing in either suite would go red for them.

### 74.4 What this section does not do

**It does not touch the lock, and the diff proves it rather than promising it.**
Against `lockwhy` the branch is **20 files, 4280 insertions, 0 deletions**:

* **16 new files under `ci/`** — 10 instruments and 6 falsifiers, nothing else;
* **2 modified files**, both documents, both appended to;
* **zero modifications to any tracked executable.** `ci/corpus-lock.sh` is not
  edited at all, not even in a comment, which is one step stricter than
  `lockwhy` (whose single edit to it was a comment block);
* `Cargo.lock` untouched, no crate changed, no gate changed.

`ci/corpus-lock-falsify.sh` was run on the finished tree: **47 passed, 0 failed,
0 injections uncaught.**

### 74.5 Every instrument here is falsified, and writing the falsifiers found
### four real defects in this lane's own tools

| falsifier | cases | injections | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `ci/corpus-integrity-108-falsify.sh` | 16 | 8 | GREEN |
| `ci/corpus-load-band-falsify.sh` | 20 | 9 | GREEN |
| `ci/corpus-holder-rate-falsify.sh` | 11 | 6 | GREEN |
| `ci/corpus-integrity-arms-falsify.sh` | 11 | 4 | GREEN |
| `ci/corpus-overlap-sampler-falsify.sh` | 8 | 3 | GREEN |
| `ci/corpus-holder-progress-falsify.sh` | 6 | 4 | GREEN |
| **total** | **72** | **34** | **0 uncaught** |

`ci/corpus-delay-curve.py --selftest` adds 8 checks, mutation-swept against 7
mutations with all 7 caught. `ci/corpus-exclusion-cost.sh` is self-checking: it
refuses to print a tally at all if either falsifier holds a case its table does
not classify.

**The four defects the sweeps found, all in instruments this lane wrote:**

1. **`ci/corpus-holder-progress.sh` counted loop iterations, not rows that
   landed**, so a run over an unwritable file stamped itself
   `PROGRESS-COMPLETE 2/2` across a file holding only a header. This is the
   instrument that produced the 0.86 band figure;
2. **the fix carried the same trap one line down** — `grep -c` prints `0` *and*
   exits 1, so a `|| echo 0` fallback yielded `0\n0`, the integer test errored,
   and control fell through to the success branch;
3. **`ci/corpus-overlap-sampler.sh` matched a tree path without its trailing
   slash**, so a recording in `~/rustmc-lockwhy-a-anything` would have made
   `~/rustmc-lockwhy-a` read as live. This lane's three trees do not collide, so
   nothing measured was affected, and the next lane to add a fourth would not
   have been so lucky;
4. **`ci/corpus-load-band.sh`'s incompleteness refusal was unreachable by any
   case.** Nineteen cases passed and the branch that refuses to report over a
   truncated calibration had never been executed; the injection exposed it and
   case 12 now reaches it by making the output file unwritable.

None of the four changes a published number. All four were found by pointing
something at an instrument rather than by reading it.

The switch is the owner's; this is evidence.

## 84. Every T1 binary now has a positive control, or a name and a reason

§73.7 counted, over T1's 80 test binaries, how many have ever been shown to
fail: five are named by a falsifier in `ci/`, one carries a real control in its
own file, and **74 have neither**. It was careful about what that does and does
not mean — not that the 74 are worthless, but that "for 74 binaries nobody has
ever demonstrated a red, so nobody knows which of them are in the same state
`can_survive_matches_vanilla_where_both_sides_answer` was in an hour ago."

This section closes that by measurement. Every figure below is a run, not an
argument, and the forcing mechanism for each one stays in the tree.

### 84.1 The count

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **demonstrated** | **60** | 40 `absent`, 17 `perturbed`, 2 `sabotage`, 1 `perturbed+rebuild` |
| instrument | 9 | `println!` with nothing that can fail; named individually |
| unforceable | 3 | the fixture exists in no tree on this box; named individually |
| declared-red | 2 | already failing at their signature in `t1-known-red.toml` |

60 + 9 + 3 + 2 = 74, and 74 plus the six that already had one is 80 — the
number `cargo metadata` reports and `min_binaries` floors.
`ci/checks/t1-positive-controls.toml` is the ledger; `ci/check-t1-controls.py`
compares it to the tree inside `ci/t0.sh`.

### 84.2 The grades are ordered, and the cheapest one proves less than it looks

§73.4 graded 70 tests by removing the fixture each reads, and §73.7 says of its
own method that it "is by fixture removal, which is one axis and not the only
one". It is worth being exact about the gap, because 40 of the 60 above are
still on that axis.

**A binary that goes red when its golden file is deleted has proved that it
opens the file. It has not proved that it compares anything.** A test that loads
a vector and asserts nothing about it fails in precisely the same way. So
`ci/t1-force.py` has a second mode which changes **one numeric leaf** and
requires the binary to notice, and that is the grade which separates a live read
from a live comparison. It costs one integer.

    absent             the binary opens this file                    40
    perturbed          its comparison is live                        17
    perturbed+rebuild  same, for a fixture baked in at compile time   1
    sabotage           it detects a named wrong implementation        2

Two rules make the difference between a red and a control. Non-zero exit is
necessary and not sufficient — a run only counts if a **test in that binary is
named in the failure list**, because a binary that dies at load time with the
same message whatever you break says nothing about its assertions. And the clean
run comes first: a binary already failing goes red under any forcing at all, and
a sweep that skipped that step would manufacture a control for every test the
tree happens to be red on.

### 84.3 Three ways the instrument reported something false, and what each cost

All three are in the tree where they were fixed, because each is the failure
class this branch is about, committed by the thing built to measure it.

* **The evidence line cargo ate.** `rustmc_data::sabotage` announces a firing
  with a print, copied from `crates/rustmc-server/src/sabotage.rs`, where it is
  correct: that module runs in a long-lived server process whose stderr reaches
  a log. This one runs inside `cargo test`, which captures a test's output. The
  first sweep reported **`fired=0`** — the module's own definition of
  `UNVISITED`, "the gate never reaches the arm's code" — for an arm that had
  just turned `golden_rng` from 6 passed to 3 failed. It said the exact opposite
  of what happened, for the reason §73.2 gives for the guard `ci/t1-gate.sh`
  removed. The evidence now appends to a file named by
  `RUSTMC_T1_SABOTAGE_LOG`: no capture flag, no cooperation from the harness,
  the same reasoning `fixture.rs` used to prefer a panic to a print.

* **The restore that left a sabotaged binary in a clean tree.** `restore` used
  `shutil.copy2`, which preserves mtime, so the file came back **older than the
  build that read it**. For a fixture `include_str!` pulls in, cargo's
  fingerprint saw nothing newer and did not rebuild: the restored run still
  failed against the perturbed number while `git status` was clean and every
  byte on disk was correct. That is worse than the red it was chasing, and every
  later gate in that directory would have inherited it.

* **Candidates from path literals only.** Ten binaries reach the datagen extract
  through `worldgen_assembly::DATA` or `data_path(rel)`, and were reported as
  reading nothing — including `golden_biome_tags`, whose first act is to open
  the biome tag extract. A pattern taken from the shape of the examples already
  known is §73.2's defect; following the helper instead turned seven of them
  from `unforced` to red. Perturbing only leaf 0 was the same mistake in
  miniature: a golden file's first number is often a header no assertion reads.

### 84.4 The nine instruments, which is more than §73.4 found

§73.4 listed 7 VACUOUS tests plus a compile-time trait check. Counted over
*binaries* the class is larger, because that list wanted a `println!` and no
assertion at all, and six of these carry one weak assertion apiece — an
`.expect()` on a registry load, an `assert!(visited > 0)` guarding a loop.

* `margin_probe` has **zero** hard assertions and five `println!`, and its own
  module docs open "Instrument, not a gate".
* `probe_population_seed` has zero hard assertions and names its golden vector
  only in a **comment** — "verified against
  `golden/xoroshiro128pp_seed_20260708.json`" — and never opens it. That is why
  the fixture axis reported it unforced.
* `probe_disk_origin`, `probe_margin_context`, `probe_step6_order` each ask a
  question in their module docs and answer it with a sweep.
* `probe_prelim` and `probe_sulfur_index` are already on §73.4's list.
* `probe_sulfur_gradient` and `dig_throughput` are `#[ignore]`d and declared in
  `t1-known-red.toml`'s `max_ignored`.

None is wrong and none is a gate. A positive control for a binary that asserts
nothing would be a control for nothing, which is the whole reason they are
counted separately rather than folded into a total.

### 84.5 The three that cannot be forced, by name

`probe_cluster_boxes` (`oracle-work/van-ruin--58_28`, `van-ruin--57_42`) and
`probe_ruin_height` (`/tmp/ruin-w/region`) are §73.10's, unchanged: the worlds
exist in no tree on this box and only a vanilla boot can produce them. Neither
was built here — that is a corpus job with a lock this branch was told not to
take — and both stay `#[ignore]`d and declared.

`golden_village_start` is **not** in the three, and the distinction is the
point. The binary reached `perturbed` through
`the_reference_village_is_the_one_the_assembler_is_built_against`, which reads
the committed vector. Its other test,
`the_vector_still_matches_the_world_it_came_from`, still needs
`van-village-31415926` and has still never compared anything. A binary with a
control can contain a test without one.

**`golden_chunk_packet` is a fourth name §73.10 does not have.** It looked
forceable: `container_bit_packing_is_lossless` is a pure round-trip and needs no
vanilla bytes. The `palette` sabotage arm was pointed at it and reported
`fired=0`, which is how the arm earns its keep — that test calls `capture()` too
and returns early with the other two. Its capture is 117 packet bodies from a
live vanilla server, Mojang-derived and never committed, and absent here. Twelve
assertions that have never run on this box.

Its skip is invisible to the ratchet built to count skips.
`ci/check-fixture-skips.py` reports `total = 1` for this tree, naming only
`golden_village_start`. It greps for `eprintln!("skipping...` and that file
writes `eprintln!("SKIP golden_chunk_packet: set RUSTMC_CHUNK_CAPTURE")` —
three sites, one wording, and the pattern was taken from the wording of the
sites already known. That is §73.2's defect inside the ratchet written to close
it. Measured over the tree: **exactly one file and three sites** use a wording
it misses. Not widened here; that belongs to the lane that owns the ratchet, and
`ci/checks/t1-positive-controls.toml` is the evidence.

### 84.6 The comment-asserts-a-guard class can be checked, cheaply

§73.8 tabulated four comments naming a guard the code did not have and recorded
the finding: **"None was found by a check. All four were found by reading."**
`t1-audit` repaired three by rewriting the prose, which closed the instances and
not the class.

`ci/check-comment-guards.py` is the class check. It runs in about fourteen
seconds over the whole workspace, needs no build, and has four rules:

| rule | catches |
|---|---|
| `DOCUMENTED-PANIC-WITHOUT-PANIC` | `# Panics` over a body with no panicking path |
| `DOCUMENTED-NEVER-PANICS-BUT-CAN` | `# Panics / Never.` over a body that plainly can |
| `CLAIM-WITHOUT-ASSERTION` | a test named `..._control` / `..._refused` that asserts nothing |
| `GREP-PATTERN-ONLY-CAPTURED-PRODUCER` | a gate greps a log for a string only a passing test prints |

So the answer is yes, and it finds two instances §73.8 does not have:

* **`crates/rustmc-server/src/broadcast.rs:158`.** `tick_lock`'s doc promises a
  panic "if a previous holder panicked while holding it" over
  `.unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner)` — the line you write
  precisely so that it does not panic. A caller following the doc guards
  against an event that cannot happen.
* **`ci/handoff.sh:940`, in the live merge gate.** §73.2 said "the merge gate's
  copy of the guard is worse still: it has no emitter at all", and this is the
  first time a check has said so. Two Rust `println!`s write `skipping: no
  vanilla` and cargo discards both; the only shell emitters,
  `ci/village-pieces.sh` and `ci/village-oracle.sh`, are called by nothing.

Both are declared in `ci/checks/comment-guards.toml` rather than repaired:
removing a guard from `ci/handoff.sh` belongs to the lane that owns it.

`ci/comment-guards-falsify.sh` is the positive control — a checker for
unfalsifiable claims that was itself unfalsifiable would be the joke writing
itself. Six arms, all as required. Four re-introduce §73.8's originals and
require a refusal naming each. **The fifth expects GREEN and is the one that
makes the others mean anything**: it adds the same sentinel with a reachable
shell emitter and requires silence, so the rule is measuring whether a grepped
log could carry the string rather than whether the string exists.

Three earlier drafts of that checker asserted things that were false, and the
reasons are worth keeping because each is the same shape as its subject. Brace
counting over raw text ran `move_entity`'s body 110 lines past its close and
borrowed the `assert!`s of the `#[cfg(test)]` module below it. Blanking only
`"..."` then broke on `r#"{"table": ...}"#` fixtures and reported twelve tests
that plainly assert as asserting nothing. And the first producer rule refused 21
grep patterns, 20 of them greps of output this repo does not write — the Java
server's, git's, and one grep of source rather than of a log.

### 84.7 T1 in the merge gate: a recommendation with a number, and not a change

This branch does not widen the gate. §73.9 is the argument for doing it and
§73.1 is the argument for not doing it lightly, and both numbers should be in
one place:

| | |
|---|---|
| `ci/t1-gate.sh`, extract present | **1521 s** |
| the same, extract moved aside | **122 s** |
| `ci/t0.sh`'s selection | `--lib --bins` |

§73.9 measured what that selection cannot see: a broken core RNG is invisible to
**794 of 795** lib tests, and an inverted ore discard rule to **all 795**. Both
are caught by the golden-vector layer, which lives entirely outside
`--lib --bins` and has been outside every merge gate for the project's life.

The recommendation is therefore **not** "run T1 in the gate", which buys 1521 s
of wall time for a layer whose value is concentrated in a much smaller set. It
is: run the **golden-vector binaries** in the gate and leave the rest in T1.
They are the layer §73.9 shows earning it, and 57 of them now have a
demonstrated control, so the set is no longer a guess. The 1521 s figure is
dominated by whole-chunk comparisons — `golden_carver_chunk` and
`golden_surface_chunk`, which are the two declared reds and cannot regress
further without `t1-known-red.toml` noticing.

What this branch does instead is make the cheap half unconditional:
`ci/check-t1-controls.py` runs in `ci/t0.sh` in milliseconds and refuses a tree
whose ledger has stopped describing it, including a binary that has drifted from
a demonstrated grade into `instrument` — an assertion quietly becoming a
`println!`. Deciding the 1521 s is a gate-owner's call with a cost attached, and
the cost is written here rather than spent in passing.
